News.title: Wild moment mass brawl erupts in stands as fan leaps down rows to stomp on man’s stomach & punches are thrown
News.content:
THIS is the wild moment a mass brawl erupts at a baseball game with dozens of fans punching one another in the face.

Shocking footage shows one man leaping down several rows and landing feet-first on a man’s stomach in the Chicago stands.



“There’s a kid!” shouted one terrified fan while others fled the scene or whipped out their phones to record the dramatic fisticuffs.

It is unclear what exactly sparked the stadium skirmish amongst the White Sox fans, whose team beat the New York Mets 2-1 on Sunday.



One man was thrown to the ground – before he dramatically jumped down two rows to stomp on a guy below him.

The attacked fan then grabbed the aggressor by the shirt and flung him down another row of seats.

READ MORE airport showdown Moment travelers smack each other with wet floor signs in airport brawl

Another pair repeatedly swung fists at each other while a man in a red baseball cap prowled up and down, picking fights with multiple people.

And a third assailant found himself shirtless in the heat of the brawl.

Security guards stormed onto the scene, wielding hand cuffs, but people continued to battle across the stands.

Some even swarmed to the melee with evident glee as bystanders filmed the encounter from multiple angles.



One clip was sarcastically captioned “Happy Sunday!”

Team rivalries were not to blame as White Sox supporters appeared determined to attack each another.

People viewing the clip online said the fighting looked “absolutely insane” with others slamming the fans as “degenerates”.

It comes just days after another huge fight broke out at a Chicago White Sox game on Monday.

An argument quickly spiralled out of control after a group of White Sox fans appeared to gang up on a Cubs fan after their win.



It got so out of hand that even star outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong took notice.

“The fights in the stand are unfortunate and somewhat nauseating,” the MVP candidate said after the game.

It isn’t entirely clear what started the fight, but a two and a half minute video shows the clash unfolding.

One person could be heard shouting “it’s not that serious” as the fight went on.

Other fans quickly vacated the area as the beatdown commenced.

News.title: I worked as Michael Jackson & Bella Hadid’s bodyguard – terrifying taxi tactics that deluded fans used to get to stars
News.content:
BUSY BODY I worked as Michael Jackson & Bella Hadid’s bodyguard – terrifying taxi tactics that deluded fans used to get to stars

MICHAEL Jackson’s former bodyguard has revealed the surprisingly gruelling reality of a model’s working day, and the reason he decided to quit on the spot.

Simon Newton, 45, who lives in Eastbourne, bodyguarding followed a career in the army, with stints in Iraq and Afghanistan; then in private security, which included defending oil tankers against Somali pirates.



His high-profile clients include Bella Hadid, Kendall Jenner, Kate Moss, Michael Jackson, Rita Ora, Halsey and Dizzee Rascal, who he “really enjoyed” working with, and still speaks to.

Kendall was the first model he looked after, but it was Bella he worked with most frequently.



“You can do long days – really long days. You can start at five or six in the morning and you won’t go to bed until midnight,” Simon told The Sun.

“If the girls are on the catwalk, you could be dressing first thing in the morning, going to where the show is to do the walkthrough and rehearsal. Then you go back again for the show.



“Then if there’s a dinner or something in the evening with the show, they might go, you might get back to the hotel at 12, one in the morning and you might be back at nine again the next day.

“You just eat when you can… It had to be fairly quick. You can’t be sitting there waiting for a big steak dinner and all of a sudden you’re going.”

Despite the long days, for Simon the job was nothing compared to life in a warzone.

“I’d lived and worked in Afghanistan and Iraq collectively for about seven years. There’s a lot of things that most people should never be subjected to seeing really,” said Simon.

“One minute you’re in Afghanistan, the next day you land in a Gatwick and you’re walking through the terminal with everyone else, like no one’s got a clue where you’ve just been or what you’ve just been doing.”



Simon’s first ever celeb client was the King of Pop, Michael Jackson, himself.

“I was working in Afghanistan and actually on leave back at home for a month. It wasn’t until I got to the airport I found out who it was,” Simon said.

“I didn’t put much thought into it, to be honest, before the job started.”



He soon realised the lengths obsessive fans would go to see their idol.

“We were getting a lot of people following us around,” he said. “I realised there were five or six black taxis, all on a meter, that were just running the whole day, which fans were paying for to follow him.

“People booked the same hotel so they could be in the lobby, because otherwise it was shut off to people outside.

“There were people coming over from China and they were following him wherever he was going after he was finished with us.

“But it was quite an expensive hotel, so the money these fans must have been spending… that’s when it dawned on me how die-hard these people are.”



Though the mobs were ecstatic, they were rarely in genuine danger.

“There were a few people we were told to look out for. They weren’t well people. It wasn’t like they were trying to harm Jackson, but they weren’t well people,” Simon said.

“There was a guy who used to dress as Jesus all the time and follow him around the world. Again, where they got their money from and how they had time to do it, I’ve got no idea.”

That was in 2006. Since then, Jackson passed away, and faced further allegations that he sexually abused young boys, which are denied by his estate and family.



Working as his bodyguard around London, Simon was only beside him for a few weeks.

“I found him very young for his age, the way he would talk and interact,” Simon said. “But then when he was on stage and singing, he was very professional.”

After guarding Michael, Simon spent five years working as a Close Protection Officer in the Middle East before picking up more bodyguarding jobs in London.

Being papped next to so many icons of the fashion industry has its perks, and by the end of the last decade Simon was being interviewed in Vogue himself.

Since then, he’s started his own fashion brand and has moved into acting, appearing in the new Rise of the Footsoldier film out this month.



When he works with artists, they are provided with a rider – a list given to the venue detailing what drinks, food, and other demands are required in the dressing room. But in reality, most of it gets chucked away.

“You could take it all with you, if you wanted. There might be Champagne in there. There might be chocolate and fruit, maybe sandwiches in the fridge,” said Simon.

“But sometimes we’d go in there, bust open a bottle of water, and the rest of it would get chucked.”

Simon is well versed on the downsides of fame – and his thoughts might make you rethink applying to the next series of Love Island.

“It’s not what people think, if you actually realise what it brings. You need money as well, because you can’t do the same things as what everybody else does,” he said.



“You can’t just get a bus or a train, it’s too much of a nightmare.

“You can’t just leave your house anymore. There’s always some sort of restriction to doing what you and I would take for granted.”

As well as celebs, he’s looked after “some of the richest people in the world” – names you’ve never heard of, who have fortunes of up to £30 billion.

“Celebrities by and large haven’t got a lot of money compared to these people. It’s a different way of living when you’ve got billions. It did make me realise it ruins your life.”

“A lot of them don’t have family,” he said. If you’ve got that money when you’re single, how do you ever trust a woman, or vice versa?



“You might cross paths with someone who genuinely is interested in you, but you’re always going to think that that might not be the case.”

After years working as a bodyguard, Simon was ready for a new challenge – acting.

He’d had a taste of it already, playing a US Special Forces soldier in Matt Damon’s film Green Zone. Then in 2016, he acted as Dave Bautista’s body double in the film Final Score, which came out in 2018.

He said: “I basically woke up one morning and thought I don’t want to be a bodyguard anymore.

“I always had a lot of work, but you could be in another country the next morning and I was just getting pushed from pillar to post, and I’d done everything I wanted to do in the industry.



“I still own a private security company today off the back of it. So I still make a bit of money through that job.”

Having never worked with actors personally, Simon didn’t have a “little black book” of agents to call. But he’s enjoyed breaking into the industry, and experiencing fame from the other side.

“That’s the thing about acting, I get to go and see better parts of the world. Now I get looked after,” he said.

“When you’re a bodyguard, you’re the only one on the team. You don’t get a day off. If no one’s working on Sunday, you still are, because you’re looking after whoever you’re looking after.

“When you’re an actor, everything’s sorted out for me, everything’s paid for.”

News.title: Contaminated chicken wraps are urgently pulled from UK supermarket shelves over deadly E. Coli fears
News.content:
SHOPPERS have been urged not to eat four lunchtime wraps after they were found to possibly be contaminated with deadly E.coli toxins.

Those experiencing any symptoms of this harmful bacteria are recommended to stay away from work and school.



Shiga toxin-producing E.coli has possibly contaminated Summit Foods wraps, forcing the Food Standards Agency to issue an urgent recall.

Shoppers who have purchased the lunchtime items have been urged to dispose of them immediately, and to not consume them.



Included in the recall are the Snacksters Chicken Fajita Wrap, Snacksters Hoi Sin Wrap, East Street Deli Sweet Chilli Chicken Wrap and the Target a Snack Chicken Fajita Wrap

All items displaying a use by date up to and including September 5, 2026 are impacted by this product recall.



Summit Foods, known for its popular “fake-away” items, can be found in many major retailers such as Tesco, Aldi, Asda and Morrisons.

Its Snacksters Chicken Fajita Wrap can still be found on the Iceland website, where it is sold for £1.50.



Shiga toxin-producing E.coli, or STEC, can cause severe stomach pain, bloody diarrhoea and kidney failure after infection, with symptoms usually appearing two to four days after contamination.

In its most severe cases, a small number of people, mainly children, can develop a serious life-threatening condition called haemolytic uraemic syndrome (HUS) from E.coli.

Everything you need to know about Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) THE most common type of Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) in the UK is O157. Symptoms People infected with STEC can have a combination of the following symptoms: diarrhoea (about 50 per cent of cases have bloody diarrhoea)

stomach cramps

fever Some people may have mild diarrhoea, or even no symptoms at all. Symptoms can last up to two weeks in cases without complications. A small proportion of patients, mainly children, may develop haemolytic uraemic syndrome (HUS) which is a serious life-threatening condition resulting in kidney failure. And a small proportion of adults may develop a similar condition called thrombotic thrombocytopaenic purpura (TTP). How it’s transmitted Cattle are the most important reservoir of STEC O157 in the UK, although STEC have also been found in the faeces of a range of animals, including deer, rabbits, horses, pigs and wild birds. People can become infected by: eating contaminated food

contact with infected animals either directly or through inadvertent contact with animal faeces, for example at farms, petting farms and campsites

contact with other people who have the illness (through inadequate hand hygiene after using the toilet, before food handling – particularly in households, nurseries and infant schools, or both

drinking water from inadequately treated water supplies

swimming or playing in contaminated water such as ponds or streams How to avoid getting it Good hygiene practices relating to food and drink, and animals and their environment can hep you avoid getting infected. You must: cook all minced meat products (burgers, meatloaf, meat balls) thoroughly, until the colour is the same all the way through, and no blood runs from them

ensure refrigerators are working correctly – bacteria grow more quickly at temperatures over 4 o C

C only leave cooked foods, meat and dairy products out at room temperature for a short time

store uncooked meats below cooked meats and salad vegetables to avoid dripping juices onto ready to eat food

store uncooked and cooked meats on different plates, avoid all contact between raw and cooked meats

thoroughly wash all salad vegetables and do not prepare them with utensils that have also been used for raw meat

children and the elderly who are particularly susceptible to the severe effects of STEC should avoid eating or drinking unpasteurised dairy products

people who have been ill should not prepare food for others for at least 48 hours after they have recovered

boil any drinking water if you are unsure of it’s source

do not swim in water that you think may be contaminated by cattle and sheep in nearby fields

wash your hands thoroughly after using the toilet (or helping others including changing nappies), handling raw meat, before meals and after contact with animals How to treat STEC There is no specific treatment for STEC infection. The illness is usually self-limiting, and will clear itself within a week. It’s important to drink plenty of fluids as diarrhoea can lead to dehydration. Antibiotics are not recommended and are likely to increase the risk of getting complications such as HUS. Also, stay away from work or school until 48 hours after you’ve stopped vomiting or having diarrhoea. Source: UK Health Security Agency

Characterised by decreased urination, pink or brown urine, fatigue, swelling, and unexplained bruising, this condition can pose a risk of kidney failure and death – particularly in children aged five and under.

Those experiencing any of these are urged to stay away from work, school or nursery until the symptoms have stopped for at least 48 hours.



All retailers selling the affected products will display point of sale notices throughout its branches, explaining why the item has been recalled and that it should not be consumed.

Refunds will be issued by Summit Foods if the proof of purchase is emailed to the company directly, stating where and when the item was bought.

POLL OF THE DAY Must TikTok clamp down on yobs showing off with ‘idiotic’ videos like joyriding? VOTE NOW

THE government has ordered TikTok and other social media platforms to take down “idiotic” daredevil content showing drivers speeding the wrong way down motorways.

It comes after two cops were killed in a head-on collision with a VW Passat driven by a “TikTok joyrider” in the early hours of Saturday morning.

Tributes flooded in for PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, who died at the scene in Cleveland, Yorkshire.



The five young men in the Passat were also killed in the horror crash and have since been named as Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Jacob Matusiak, 23, and Makai Saddington, 18.



The A66 tragedy has prompted fears the men may have been taking part in a rapidly-spreading TikTok trend which encourages reckless driving.

TikTok footage has since emerged showing Matusiak driving dangerously in the months leading up to the crash.

It follows a similar head-on collision in Co Kildare in Ireland on August 16, which left five young men dead and a family hospitalised.

News.title: Teacher, 53, ‘raped student, 17, in classroom’ as she sues school for ‘failing to protect her from serial predator’
News.content:
TWISTED ‘PREDATOR’ Teacher, 53, ‘raped student, 17, in classroom’ as she sues school for ‘failing to protect her from serial predator’

A TEACHER has been accused of repeatedly raping a teen student with the girl filing a lawsuit claiming the school ignored her cries for help.

The 17-year-old alleges that John Kennedy, 53, committed sickening acts of sexual abuse inside his classroom in Long Island.



Pupils previously called Kennedy, formerly an art instructor at Bay Shore High School, their “favourite teacher”.

But a shock new lawsuit filed against the school alleged that Kennedy flagrantly abused a female student in front of the class – and that the school turned a blind eye.



She would be forced to sit at his desk while he massaged her neck and called her his “favourite”, court docs say.

The teacher is also alleged to have groped the girl and repeatedly forced her into despicable sex acts between June and October 2025, according to the teen’s lawsuit.

“Kennedy was at all relevant times a serial sexual predator who sexually assaulted and abused Plaintiff and other students throughout his employment”, states the complaint.

Suffolk County Police Department previously launched an investigation into Kennedy but later shut the case after finding no evidence of criminal conduct.

The school district was also said to have received multiple accusations against Kennedy from the student’s parents and others, the suit alleges.

It was only in October – four months after the teacher’s alleged campaign of abuse – that Kennedy was suspended from his position.



The move was prompted after text messages of an allegedly sexual nature were discovered between himself and the teen.

Just one month earlier, the girl’s mother had pleaded with school officials – including Principal Stephen Gordon and guidance counselor Michelle Plett – to stop Kennedy having contact with her daughter.

But the lawsuit alleges that they continued to allow contact, “failing to adequately supervise or separate” the two.

A classmate of the girl even posted a video of Kennedy to TikTok – with the comment section flooded with accusations that the art teacher would flirt with his students.

The district demanded the deletion of the video – but took no action over the allegations in the content, according to court docs.



“At the end of the day, this guy was a teacher in a position of power over a student, and he used his position of power to groom her and abuse her” said prosecuting lawyer Andrew Silvershein.

Silvershein alleged that Bay Shore district had covered for child molesters before – including ex-teacher Thomas Bernagozzi.

Bay Shore Superintendent Steven Maloney said the district acted quickly in response to the allegations by placing Kennedy on leave, barring him from district property and alerting the police.

He said: “When the matter was first brought to our attention in October 2025, the District took immediate action. The Suffolk County Police Department was immediately notified and the District fully cooperated throughout their investigation.”

News.title: UK weather: ‘Significant’ rain & thunderstorms to batter Britain this week, Met Office warns – after glorious heatwaves
News.content:
RAIN RETURN UK weather: ‘Significant’ rain & thunderstorms to batter Britain this week, Met Office warns – after glorious heatwaves

BRITAIN is set to get soaked in wet weather this week as the country’s heatwave spell comes to a damp end.

After a settled start to the week, heavy rain and thunderstorms are on the cards across the country.



Summery weather will come to an end this week as rain sets in across the country and thunderstorm threat increases.

Today will see above average highs of 25C in southwestern and northwestern England with Tuesday also settled, apart from the odd shower.



But sunny spells are coming to an end on Wednesday as humid air spreads northwards.

Thundery showers and heavy rain are likely to develop across England and Wales with more showers approaching the northwest later in the day.

Met Office Deputy Chief Forecaster, Mark Sidaway, said: “While many areas will see dry and increasingly warm conditions at the start of the week, attention is turning to the potential for heavy rain and thunderstorms from Wednesday onwards.

“As warmer and more humid air moves north across the UK, there is an increasing likelihood of some heavy rain developing. Some places could see 20 to 30mm of rain in just a few hours, while there is also the potential for higher totals where thunderstorms repeatedly affect the same locations.”



By Thursday and Friday, a band of heavy rain is expected to have moved northwards through England and Wales, bringing with it substantial rainfall.

An area of low pressure is expected to strengthen winds throughout Friday particularly in eastern and northeastern coastal areas.

News.title: Shocking moment planes flip in strong 75mph winds on runway forcing airport to close as storms batter Italy
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment four planes are “thrown around like toys” at an airport as violent storms batter Italy.

Wild footage shows extreme gusts of wind knocking the four light aircraft around the runway before causing them to flip over.



One plane was blown off course during landing, while three other stationary aircraft were also tossed and flipped.

It comes after a strong cyclone ravaged Forlì in Italy’s Emilia-Romagna region, with winds reaching around 120 km/h.



The severe weather caused lots of damage, forcing Forlì Airport to temporarily close for an hour.

Some parts of the airport’s hangar wall were ripped off and the arrivals terminal roof was damaged, according to reports.

Once the winds slowed down, firefighters and airport emergency crews carried out extensive inspections to assess the wreckage and check for any hazards, such as fuel spills.

The emergency teams also stabilised the remaining aircraft to prevent any further danger.



Violent storms also swept through several other areas of northern Italy, including Liguria, Lombardy, Tuscany and the Italian Alps.

The cyclone brought gale-force winds, lightning, flooding, and heavy rain.

The storm has wreaked havoc on northern Italy, causing flash flooding, landslides, fallen trees, and power outages.



On August 21, red thunderstorm warnings were issued in Liguria as the Italian Air Force National Meteorological Service warned its citizens to “be prepared.”

Roads were turned into rivers in Chiavari, a town in Liguria, with cars floating like boats down the streets.

That same day, 250 people were evacuated from a riverside campsite in Bergamo after rock and mud shifted near a river.

This is the latest in a string of powerful storms that have swept through Europe, causing extensive damage.

Elsewhere in Europe, extreme rain and winds have also hit Poland and Spanish tourist hotspots, Mallorca and Valencia.

News.title: Ukraine drones pound ANOTHER ‘Russian Amazon’ retail giant for third night in row in bid to cripple Putin’s war machine
News.content:
UKRAINIAN drones have blitzed another Russian retail giant for the third night in a row as Volodymyr Zelensky tries to destroy the Kremlin’s war machine.

It comes after weeks of dramatic strikes on Moscow’s largest retailer Wildberries, known as Russia’s Amazon, with what Ukraine called “long-range sanctions” in an attempt to bleed Vladimir Putin‘s war chest dry.



Another four logistics hubs owned by Ozon, Russia’s second-biggest online retailer, were struck by Ukrainian drones overnight.

The blasts bring the total number of the company’s sites targeted to six since Friday night.





Ozon said its logistics hubs in Makhachkala and Enem were set ablaze after drone attacks.

Workers at a site in Stavropol were also evacuated after it was targeted by Ukrainian drones.

Dramatic footage showed the warehouses engulfed in flames, with huge clouds of black smoke pouring from the sites.

The company said several were injured in the strikes which coincided with Ukraine‘s independence day.



It’s the third day running that Zelensky’s forces have pounded Ozon’s sprawling sites, with last night’s hits targeting facilities spanning an estimated 3.27million sq ft – the equivalent of roughly 42 football pitches.

It comes as Andy Burnham arrives in Kyiv for his first visit to Ukraine as Prime Minister.

He has vowed Britain will stand with Ukraine “for as long as it takes” as he visits the capital.



The PM arrived by train this morning and has agreed to provide Ukraine with blueprints to produce long-range missiles.

Burnham will allow European defence firm MBDA to declassify information on UK components for the Scalp missile – the French-produced version of the UK’s Storm Shadow.

The PM said: “The friendship between our two countries will long outlast Russia’s illegal war.

“In both the fight and in the rebuilding to come, we will stand with Ukraine.

“And deliver opportunities for people across both our countries.



“Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve.

“We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace.”

It comes after Moscow warned Britain would face “consequences” over the reported use of UK-made drones in Ukrainian strikes deep inside Russia.



Last week, Russia warned that the deeper the country’s involvement became, “the higher the price it will pay”.

And Russia pulled its ambassador out of Britain, rewarding the Kremlin crony with a prestigious post in Moscow.

Andrei Kelin, 69, was in the job for seven years since his appointment in 2019.

He quietly left the role on July 21 and the Kremlin has not replaced him, signalling a serious breakdown in diplomatic relations between Moscow and London.

Ukraine also blasted Putin’s Plesetsk military cosmodrome with more than 40 drones last night.



Smoke was seen pluming from the military spaceport around 1,000 miles from Ukraine, but Russians refused to confirm any damage.

And Nato scrambled two F-16 fighters in Romania after a suspected Russian drone crossed into its airspace in the Târgu Bujor area.

The Romanian defence ministry said: “Two F-16 aircraft of the Romanian Air Force, from the 86th Air Base in Borcea, and an IAR-330 SOCAT helicopter were taken off the ground to monitor the situation.”

The Nato state has already suffered at least six confirmed drone incursions this month.

Russian drones blasted an outlet of Ukraine’s largest home-improvement and DIY retail chain, Epicentr.



Local official Oleh Kiper said the city was “again under massive enemy missile and drone attack”.

He added: “The main blow was to food storage facilities and energy infrastructure. Private homes were also damaged. Fires broke out.

“No information about casualties has been received yet.”

News.title: Family's warning after 'remarkable' 17-year-old stepped in front of train
News.content:
Family's warning after 'remarkable' 17-year-old stepped in front of train

An inquest heard Herbie was kind, generous, full of love and embraced life

View 6 Images Herbie Ballard will be remembered by his family as a 'truly remarkable young man'

The family of a 17-year-old boy say he acted “devastatingly out of character” when he made a sudden decision to step in front of a train. Herbie Ballard died on April 22 at a pedestrian railway crossing in Whitstable during what a coroner described as a “brief and intense period of emotional crisis”.

‌



Police and paramedics were called shortly before 10pm but Herbie could not be saved and was pronounced dead at the scene. Herbie’s family described him as a “truly remarkable young man” who was kind, generous, “full of love”, embraced life with “rare enthusiasm” - and had big dreams for his future.

‌



They now want to raise awareness of how vulnerable young people can be to moments of “overwhelming emotions”, particularly following relationship break-ups, and the impact of social media. An inquest into his death at Oakwood House, Maidstone, heard that, just hours earlier, Herbie had been at the Two Brewers pub in Canterbury Road, where he appeared happy as he drank pints with friends.

‌



View 6 Images Herbie Ballard had big dreams for the future

However, coroner Sarah Clarke heard how an argument with his ex-girlfriend began just before 8pm while he was at the pub, and later continued at his family home, where she had gone to collect belongings. Herbie’s mum Tara told the hearing he had learned some distressing information, and that “the hurt and upset was overwhelming for our son”.

She added she had “never in 17 years seen that face”, adding: “I can’t describe it, but it wasn’t Herbie. He was so angry.” As Herbie ran from the house, Tara tried to stop him from leaving. “As he was going down the stairs, I grabbed hold of him and said, ‘Don’t you dare go outside’, because I didn’t want the argument to ensue,” she said.

‌



“He just got free from me and just said, ‘I’m going to kill myself’, ran down the stairs and out. “But we’d never heard him talk like that.”

Herbie had left without his shoes, and his parents believed he would calm down and return within minutes. Tara recalled thinking: “He’s got no shoes on. It’s getting cold. He’ll be back in a minute.” “It just happened so quickly,” she added.

View 6 Images Herbie Ballard (centre) with mum Tara and dad Dean

‌



The inquest heard Herbie’s ex-girlfriend followed him towards the nearby railway crossing, and attempts were made to persuade him away from the line. The train driver later told British Transport Police he saw two young people near the crossing and described one as moving towards the train in a way which appeared “more deliberate than accidental”.

However, it was dark, visibility was poor, and the driver had only a short time to see what was happening. A post-mortem examination found Herbie died from multiple injuries. Alcohol was detected in a liver sample, although the amount could not be established, and the coroner said the evidence did not suggest Herbie had been too intoxicated to understand what he was doing.

The hearing was told Herbie had never been diagnosed with a mental health condition, was not known to local mental health services and there had been no previous indication he was suicidal. His family described him as kind, cheeky and sociable, with a love of football, cooking and being outdoors.

‌



He began working at 13 and later joined mental health and wellbeing initiative Revival Food and Mood, where he progressed from pot washer to kitchen assistant. After leaving school, he enrolled on a carpentry course at Canterbury College before securing full-time work in construction.

View 6 Images An inquest into Herbie Ballard's death concluded last week

“He was so excited to go to work with the lads in the van, and loved his life, his family and his friends,” Tara said. Herbie was also due to take his driving theory test the following week and had a car waiting for him. It was against that background that the latter stages of the inquest became an emotional discussion over whether Herbie’s death could legally be recorded as suicide.

‌



Tara said the term was difficult to reconcile with the happy teenager who had been making plans for his future. The coroner acknowledged that, but explained she had to decide whether Herbie deliberately acted to end his life in those final moments, rather than whether he had been suicidal in the weeks or months beforehand.

Miss Clarke added that such a conclusion could be reached “even if it’s a very impulsive act”. Tara replied: “Herbie was just caught up in a moment of horrible things that he’d never had in his life and didn’t know what to do with them. It was just a moment of madness. And he didn’t have time to breathe. That was the problem.”

View 6 Images Flowers and cards were left in honour of Herbie Ballard

‌



The coroner stressed her conclusion “doesn’t change the boy that he was”. “The evidence does not suggest that Herbie had any sustained or long-standing intention to take his own life,” she said. However, the coroner found he had expressed an intention to do so during “a moment of extreme upset and distress” during which “tragically, he acted upon thoughts of ending his life”.

“For all of these reasons, the appropriate conclusion remains one of suicide,” she added. Following the hearing, Tara said the family respected the coroner’s finding, but stressed it reflected Herbie’s intention in his final moments rather than evidence of a prolonged suicidal state.

“Herbie was not a young man who had been living with an ongoing mental-health condition or suicidal thoughts,” she said. “He was deeply loved, supported and surrounded by a close family and lifelong friends. Nothing about what happened was consistent with the Herbie we knew. It was sudden, situational and devastatingly out of character.”

‌



View 6 Images Tara Ballard and her son Herbie, then aged three

His family now want others to understand a young person can experience extreme emotional distress even without previously appearing suicidal or having a diagnosed mental health condition. Tara said relationships and break-ups could be experienced with enormous intensity, while phones, messaging apps and social media could leave little opportunity for arguments to end and emotions to settle.

She said families and schools needed to talk about overwhelming emotions, relationship distress and impulsivity, as well as recognising persistent suicidal thoughts. “However unbearable something feels in one moment, that moment can pass,” Tara said.

Article continues below

“If something meaningful can come from the terrible loss of Herbie, we hope it is a greater understanding of that vulnerability, and more conversations with young people before an overwhelming moment becomes an irreversible one.”

The family plans to petition for the closure of the Ham Shades Lane level crossing where Herbie died and is developing Herbie’s Youth Mental Health Ambassador programme alongside Revival to work with schools and youth organisations.

Network Rail has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Hovercraft used to rescue five kids trapped by rising tide at Southend-on-Sea
News.content:
Hovercraft used to rescue five kids trapped by rising tide at Southend-on-Sea

Southend-on-Sea RNLI responded to a 999 call on Sunday and rescued five children from rising waters half a mile offshore at Shoebury Boom on Shoebury East Beach near Southend-on-Sea

View 2 Images Southend-on-Sea RNLI volunteers were tasked by HM Dover Coastguard to a 999-call reporting five children out by the waterline (Image: RNLI/Nigel Gilchrist)

Five children were rescued from rising waters half a mile offshore at Southend-on-Sea.

‌



The youngsters got into trouble at Shoebury Boom on Shoebury East Beach in Essex at 4.45pm Sunday.

‌



Southend-on-Sea RNLI responded to a 999 call reporting five children out by the waterline as the tide was rising.

‌



RNLI volunteers launched the charity’s hovercraft at 5pm and headed at top speed to the reported location at Shoeburyness.

The rescue crew arrived at the scene about half a mile offshore on the waters edge to find the five children in good health. They were taken onboard the hovercraft and given a welfare check.

‌



The kids, cold but uninjured, were taken back to shore where their parents and HM Southend Coastguard Rescue Team were waiting for them, Southend-on-Sea RNLI said in a statement today.

View 2 Images Southend-on-Sea RNLI hovercraft H-004 Vera Ravine was launched at 5pm (Image: RNLI/Nigel Gilchrist)

Southend RNLI volunteer Commander Jonathan Charnock said: “Southend has a vast tidal flat area, at low tide whilst the water can be seen it can be over 1 mile from the shore. East Beach has the added danger of the MoD firing range to the east of the Boom.

Article continues below

“The children were found on their return to shore however they could have come into real danger quickly. With no way of calling for help, improper footwear and an unfamiliarity with the area today’s call could have had a very different outcome.

“If you do go onto the beaches of Southend, check out the local area, know where you can and can’t go. Tell someone your plan and time, properly prepare and have a way of calling for help.”

The charity urged members of the public to always check the weather and tide times for the local area if you are planning to head to the coast.

News.title: Melania Trump tells Donald 'I can't take anymore' as tense exchange spotted by lip reader
News.content:
Melania Trump tells Donald 'I can't take anymore' as tense exchange spotted by lip reader

EXCLUSIVE: Following Donald and Melania Trump's appearance at the Freedom 250 Grand Prix, a professional lip reader has exclusively shared his verdict on a conversation between the pair

View 3 Images Melania and Donald Trump were caught having a tense exchange (Image: x)

US President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump's apparently tense exchange has been uncovered by a lip reader. The world's most powerful couple were in attendance at the Freedom 250 IndyCar Grand Prix in Washington DC yesterday (August 23). And cameras appeared to pick up on a passionate conversation between the pair.

‌



In a 26-second clip shared on the platform X, Melania is seen seemingly saying something into her spouse's ear as he appears to listen intently. The 56-year-old could then be seen moving her hair away as she eagerly waited for a response. Once she received one, the wife of Trump went on to say more to her spouse before holding up two fingers.

‌



Professional lip reader Jeremy Freeman exclusively told the Mirror that, although their exchange cannot be fully seen, he believed she started the chat by saying: "That’s the problem, people react."

‌



Her husband supposedly replied: "We'll knock it off.". Then, Melania apparently said in a "snappy" tone: "Are you?" The next section of the video was undecipherable, before Melania was seemingly spotted saying: "It happened two times."

Donald then replied: "I know", to which Melania finished with a cutting remark: "I can't take anymore." After the footage went viral on X, users commented their thoughts in their droves with one writing: "To me it looks like they are having a serious discussion about something," while another commented: "I don't think I've ever seen them interact this much in public."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



At the event, the pair were reportedly joined by family members and White House staffers, including Trump's executive assistant Natalie Harp.

In another short clip from the race, Trump's aide is seen going over to speak to the President briefly after Melania leaves.

Personal correspondence from the aide to the president, obtained and published by the Daily Beast, has recently circulated widely online.

‌



View 3 Images President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump at the start of the race

The letters appear to reveal her emotional connection to Trump, including one in which she refers to him as her "guardian and protector."

In the text, reportedly written in 2023, she expressed: "I never want to bring you anything but joy. I'm sorry I lost my focus. You are all that matters to me. I don't want to ever let you down. Thank you for being my Guardian and Protector in this Life."

‌



The wife of Trump has spent considerable time away from Washington since her husband's return to office, including time in New York City to be close to her son, Barron. However, reports about her exact living arrangements have varied.

Article continues below

News.title: Child Benefit warning for millions of parents as payments could stop after August 31
News.content:
Child Benefit warning for millions of parents as payments could stop after August 31

To claim Child Benefit, your child normally has to live with you, or you pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit toward looking after them

View 2 Images Child Benefit is worth £27.05 a week for your first child, then £17.90 for any additional child (Image: Getty Images)

Millions of parents have just one week left to renew their Child Benefit payments before they stop.

‌



Child Benefit is worth £27.05 a week for your first child, then £17.90 for any additional child. You can claim it if you are responsible for a child under the age of 16, or if they are under the age of 20 and they stay on in education or training.

‌



But you must notify HMRC if your child is continuing with education or training - and the deadline for doing this is August 31. It comes after thousands of students picked up their GCSE results last week.

‌



Child Benefit continues for children in full-time, non-advanced education, including A levels, T levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3, and certain approved training schemes.

View 2 Images Child Benefit is paid by HMRC (Image: Getty Images )

It cannot be claimed for children doing a university degree, a standard apprenticeship in England, or a course that forms part of a job contract.

‌



You can update your Child Benefit claim through the HMRC app or GOV.UK, or by phone or post. Once your child has finished their education or training, Child Benefit payments will continue until whichever of these comes first: the end of February, May 31, August 31 or November 31.

You must inform HMRC if your child leaves education or training before the course is complete, otherwise you risk being paid money that you are not entitled to.

Myrtle Lloyd, HMRC Chief Customer Officer, said: "Exam results season is a big moment for teenagers deciding their next steps, and it’s the perfect time for parents to confirm those plans with us.

‌



"Child Benefit is a vital source of support for many families and we don’t want anyone to miss out. It only takes a few minutes using the HMRC app or GOV.UK, so make sure you’re receiving the payments you’re entitled to."

If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Money newsletter here for all the best advice and shopping deals straight to your inbox.

You can claim the full amount of Child Benefit if you, or your partner, earn under £60,000 a year. If you earn more than this, then the High Income Child Benefit Charge will apply.

Article continues below

If either you earn over £60,000, you have to pay back 1% of your Child Benefit for every £200 you earn over £60,000. Child Benefit is effectively wiped out once you earn over £80,000.

To claim Child Benefit, your child normally has to live with you, or you pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit toward looking after them.

There is no limit for how many children you can claim Child Benefit for - but only one person can make a claim for Child Benefit for any individual child.

News.title: Woman, 22, passed out from miscarriage twice after 'doctors said bleeding was normal'
News.content:
Woman, 22, passed out from miscarriage twice after 'doctors said bleeding was normal'

A 22-year-old woman said she has been left 'scared to get pregnant in the future' after she claimed a hospital refused to give her a scan during her miscarriage

View 3 Images Jodie Evans claimed she had to pay for a private scan to find out she was having a miscarriage (Image: Jodie Evans / SWNS)

A young woman who had a miscarriage at home claimed doctors told her bleeding was normal and she'd have to wait five weeks for a scan.

‌



Jodie Evans, 22, found out she was five weeks pregnant with her first child on June 10, 2026, but started experiencing painful bleeding at the end of July - seven weeks into her pregnancy. The woman, from Wolverhampton, contacted doctors but claimed they said there were no appointments until she was 12 and a half weeks pregnant and told her that it would be ok to wait. Jodie added that all her pregnancy symptoms had "gone overnight".

‌



The 22-year-old booked a private scan at 10 weeks and was told the baby had no heartbeat and died at six weeks and six days.

‌



View 3 Images Jodie said she started experiencing painful bleeding seven weeks into the pregnancy (Image: Jodie Evans / SWNS)

Jodie said her miscarriage last two weeks and she "passed out twice" in that time. The 22-year-old jewellery shop worker said: "The doctors told me a scan was unneeded. I kept getting declined so I booked a private one at 10 weeks to ease my brain.

"All my pregnancy symptoms had gone overnight when I started worrying, like my sore breasts and cravings and I asked my midwife as it said online it could be an indicator of a miscarriage but she said that because I felt fine she won’t give me a scan."

‌



Jodie shared her anger that she and her partner Brad, 22, found out about the miscarriage through a private scan. She said: "I had to pay to find this out which I think is horrible. If I had been allowed a scan before this at eight weeks it would have reduced my risk of infection."

View 3 Images Jodie and her partner Brad (Image: Jodie Evans / SWNS)

The private doctors passed Jodie's details onto her local hospital who said they would ring her within the next 24 hours but Jodie claimed they never called. Jodie said her health took a turn for the worse on August 4 as she started to feel unwell and the pain intensified.

‌



She said: "I went to the emergency department after ringing the doctors and they told me that I was having a miscarriage but they said it will happen on its own.

"They told me I couldn't have any painkillers and it would be like a heavy period. Then two days later I started having contractions which they didn't warn me about. When I felt all the pain and saw the blood I knew something was wrong and I was just neglected."

Jodie claims her miscarriage lasted around two weeks and during that time she fell unconscious twice. She said: "I passed out twice at one point and my boyfriend called the ambulance, but they said it was not an emergency. I was sweating and I was shivering, I thought I had an infection.

Article continues below

"I was bleeding a lot and I thought I was dying and I kept screaming out in pain. The pain and everything lasted around two weeks. Now it is still there but I feel numb to it all now and I feel like I can't trust the hospital.

"It was my first pregnancy and I was scared. The hospital basically told me to get over it and sleep it off but the pain was traumatic physically and mentally. I had to go about my day to day life in a lot of pain. Since then it has all been a bit of a shock and now I am so scared to get pregnant in the future."

News.title: I visited Arctic Circle where it's full sunshine at midnight - 1 thing stood out
News.content:
I visited Arctic Circle where it's full sunshine at midnight - 1 thing stood out

Towering snow-capped mountains — even in May — the sea everywhere you look, beautiful, traditional houses and, of course, a few trolls to keep you company. Clare Fitzsimons takes a trip to Tromsø

View 4 Images Clare Fitzsimons headed to the Gateway of the Arctic

Visiting the Arctic Circle isn't necessarily everyone's first thought for a holiday, but as I'm descended from Viking royalty (apparently… a looooooong way back), it's always been on my bucket list of destinations.

‌



And arriving in the city of Tromsø, the 'Gateway to the Arctic', was as spectacular as I'd hoped.

‌



Towering snow-capped mountains — even in May — the sea everywhere you look, beautiful, traditional houses and, of course, a few trolls to keep you company. So what do you need to know to have a fabulous time in the unofficial capital of the Arctic, known as the 'Paris of the North'?

‌



When to go

It all depends on what you're looking for on your trip. The famous northern lights are often visible from the city and tourists flock from all over the world in the hope of catching a glimpse of them.

But you don't have to go in winter — late spring and summer have plenty of plus points too, including the Midnight Sun.

It's undeniably weird — but also quite a lot wonderful — to walk out of a building in the middle of the night to find it full daylight. Confusing? Undoubtedly. But absolutely worth seeing. Just remember your eye mask for getting some shut-eye.

‌



View 4 Images It is home to a very northerly McDonald's

How to get there

Of course, you can fly into the city, but why not make a trip out of it?

I cruised up the coast with Hurtigruten on the MS Trollfjord to really enjoy the incredible scenery (not to mention some delicious food and drink) on the way.

‌



What to do

The world's northernmost distillery, Aurora Spirits, in Arctic Lyngen, is worth the couple of hours' drive from Tromsø. The scenery along the way is almost beyond description as the Lyngen Alps tower above you and fjords stretch ahead of you as you wind through valleys that feel like they were created at the dawn of time.

The distillery itself is in an equally striking setting and makes whisky and other spirits using Arctic ingredients, including local botanicals and glacier water. It's also a former NATO base and if you get a chance, visit the underground bunkers where they mature the whisky.

They also make a special Seaweed Gin for the Hurtigruten cruise ships I travelled on. If you aren't able to travel beyond the city, there are plenty of things to do within walking distance.

‌



If you're feeling brave, you can do an Arctic sauna and polar plunge in the harbour, though that all seemed a little chilly for my liking.

For some culture there are Norwegian heritage experiences, to celebrate the traditional indigenous Sámi people, with joik (throat singing), duodji (Sámi handicrafts) and language classes. And for a slightly more light-hearted look at the traditions of the country, there's also the Troll Museum.

4 View 4 Images The town is nicknamed the Paris of the North 4 View 4 Images There are good views by the bucketful

‌



Where to stay

There are lots of options for every budget, but for ease and a little luxury, Clarion The Edge on the waterfront was perfect. Comfy rooms, a fabulous breakfast, a stone's throw from the centre of the city and excellent blackout blinds!

Where to eat

If you're looking for a special dinner, then Hildr is a great option. It's pricey, but their seasonal menu celebrates local Norwegian ingredients with a modern twist. There are plenty of more wallet-friendly places to eat too. Raketten Bar is famous for its hot dogs, including a reindeer one, and is hilariously tiny.

Tromsø is also home to the world's northernmost McDonald's and I couldn't resist a couple of chicken nuggets in the Arctic Circle!

‌



Where to drink

In a word… Everywhere.

The streets of the city are lined with cosy bars and coffee shops to sit in the sun or snuggle under a blanket and watch the world go by.

I was there to see teams of relay racers running through the streets and if you time it right you could catch the Midnight Sun Marathon there.

‌



Sitting and watching the runners has got to be more enjoyable than doing it, right?

Though be warned the prices can be enough to make London bars blush and might make you wish you'd put your running shoes on after all…

Book it

Hurtigruten's Svalbard Line (Northbound) travels from Bergen to Longyearbyen over eight days. There are 14 departures between May 2027 and September 2027, on MS Trollfjord and MS Midnatsol .

Article continues below

All-inclusive meals and unlimited selected drinks are included, with prices starting from £2,466pp, based on two people sharing a Polar Inside cabin onboard MS Trollfjord, departing on 30 August 2027. Flights and transfer options start from £250pp per route.

News.title: 'I was diagnosed with skin cancer aged 26 - unethical sunscreen tax must end now'
News.content:
'I was diagnosed with skin cancer aged 26 - unethical sunscreen tax must end now'

Jessica Zbinden-Webster, who was diagnosed with skin cancer aged just 26, will deliver a petition with almost 100,000 signatures to Downing Street calling for the 20% VAT charged on sun cream to be scrapped

View 4 Images Jessica Zbinden-Webster, who was diagnosed with skin cancer at age 26, said 'the unethical tax on lifesaving sunscreen must end now'

A woman who was diagnosed with skin cancer aged just 26 will today deliver a petition with almost 100,000 signatures to Downing Street calling for the 20% VAT charged on sun cream to be scrapped.

‌



Jessica Zbinden-Webster, who is now 34 and cancer-free, had an excision, a skin graft and four ocular surgeries after what she describes as a “shock diagnosis”.

‌



Her Change.org petition, which is signed by more than 99,000 people at the time of writing, comes after record temperatures and consecutive heatwaves ripped through the UK this summer. Up to nine in 10 melanoma skin cancer cases in the UK could be prevented by staying safe in the sun, such as using sunscreen and staying in the shade, and avoiding sunbeds, Cancer Research UK says.

‌



But half (50%) of people in the UK think sunscreen is too expensive and 10% don’t use it at all because of the cost, a 2023 study by charity Melanoma Focus found. Some 67% of people said they would use it more if it was cheaper.

UK facing deadly 38C heat blast in just days as Brits urged to drink plenty and check on vulnerable family READ MORE :

4 View 4 Images Jessica Zbinden-Webster is now cancer-free 4 View 4 Images She described her cancer diagnosis as a 'shock'

‌



In her petition, Ms Zbinden-Webster said: "I had a shock skin cancer diagnosis at 26 years old. One excision, one skin graft and four ocular surgeries later, I'm lucky to be cancer-free, but there are many who aren't as fortunate."

Ahead of her No10 visit on Monday, the London-based campaigner continued: "The unethical tax on lifesaving sunscreen must end now. If you think this record-breaking summer has wreaked havoc on our environment, just imagine what it's done to our skin. And, in a cost-of-living crisis, the poorest are priced out of skin cancer prevention because of the 20% 'cosmetic' tax on sunscreen products. Sunscreen is not 'cosmetic' - it's critical."

She added to The Mirror that regularly applying sunscreen would have prevented her cancer. She said: "I didn't apply sunscreen regularly because I mistakenly thought it was a seasonal product, not an everyday essential. The 'cosmetic' VAT status of sunscreen reinforces this misunderstanding to consumers.

‌



"Wearing sunscreen regularly would have prevented my skin cancer. My tumour was caused by UV damage in childhood, which is why it manifested to early in life. But parents are penalised to protect their kids' skin as the 'cosmetic' VAT on sunscreen also applies to sunscreen products for babies and children."

View 4 Images Jessica will deliver a petition to No10 today calling for the 20% VAT charged on sun cream to be scrapped

In June, a report on UV safety by the All-Party Parliamentary Group (APPG) for Beauty, Hair and Wellbeing said the current VAT classification that deems sunscreen a luxury cosmetic rather than vital preventative healthcare "inflates the cost in a way that deters regular use".

‌



It called on the Government to reduce VAT to zero on all children’s sun protection products that are rated SPF 30 and above and engage with brands and retailers to ensure that the resulting savings are passed onto the consumer. It also demanded VAT be cut to 5% on all dedicated sun protection products designed for adults that are rated SPF 30 and above.

The report added: "Not only would this remove one of the barriers that stands in the way of people using a life-saving product but it would send a clear message to the population that UV safety is not only important to the Government, but that it should be a daily consideration for everyone."

A Government spokesman said: “As part of our 10-year plan to reform the health service, and through a national cancer plan, we will fight cancer on all fronts, from prevention, to diagnosis, treatment, and research. High-factor sunscreen is on the NHS prescription list for certain conditions and is already provided VAT free when dispensed by a pharmacist to these patients.”

Article continues below

VAT is the UK’s second largest tax and is forecast to raise £180billion in 2025-26. The 20% standard rate applies to most goods and services.

Cosmetic services are exempt from VAT where they’re undertaken as an element of a health care treatment programme. Where services are undertaken purely for cosmetic reasons, they will be standard-rated, gov.uk says.

In an advice page on sun safety, the NHS tells people not rely on sunscreen alone to protect from the sun. It also recommends wearing suitable clothing and spending time in the shade when the sun's at its hottest.

News.title: Social media firms should remove dangerous driving videos, minister says
News.content:
Pollard said the government had "already taken steps" to tell social media companies to take down such content.

He added: "They know exactly what content is on their site, they know how their algorithm works.

"They also know that people post content to get views and the more views you get, sometimes you get money for it, so it's a financial incentive to post outrageous content that gets more people watching it."

TikTok said its policies prohibit content that could cause significant physical harm, including dangerous driving, and is actively removing videos and accounts that break the rules.

The company said between January and March 2026, 99.8% of the content removed for violating those policies it took down proactively.

The BBC has also contacted Meta and X for comment.

Pollard later told BBC Radio 4's Today programme "it's absolutely idiotic for anybody to be doing anything other than being completely 100% focused on the road when they're behind the wheel of a vehicle."

The minister said that someone filming themselves or others driving dangerously is "absolutely ridiculous, and of course nobody should be doing that".

"It is a worrying situation if that's becoming more prevalent because it is incredibly dangerous", he added.

News.title: 'It's not Alton Towers' - rows break out over queuing at Wales' highest mountain
News.content:
Visitors to Wales' highest mountain are being urged to respect others by not skipping queues to reach the top following rows among climbers.

Recent hot weather means there have been bumper summer crowds at Yr Wyddfa, also known as Snowdon, where people have reportedly waited more than one hour to reach the 1,085m (3,560ft)-high summit.

Social media videos have shown arguments among queue-jumpers and those patiently waiting their turn to touch the metal plate that marks the top.

A recent video showed Marc Screeton, from Manchester, being heckled as he bypassed the line, saying: "Imagine queuing on a mountain? No chance."

But others have said queuing is necessary for safety reasons.

News.title: Australian shark attack victim grateful for 'second chance at life'
News.content:
An Australian woman bitten by a shark at a popular Sydney beach earlier this year says she has been given a "second chance at life" and will be making the most of it.

Leah Stewart, 34, was mauled by a shark during a morning swim at Coogee Beach in June, suffering multiple bites to her arms and legs, amid a spate of attacks in Australia.

The mother-of-one was placed in an induced coma and had several surgeries, including having one of her arms amputated.

In an online post on Monday, she thanked her supporters who have raised more than AU$550,000 (US$394,000; Â£289,000) for her, saying her recovery has been "incredibly difficult" but she is making "remarkable" progress.

"After what has been an incredibly difficult few months, I'm so happy that I've progressed enough to build some independence, and I can finally see some light after all of this," Stewart wrote, in her first comments since the attack.

"I want you to know that I feel like I've been given a second chance at life, and I'm not going to waste it."

Stewart said she had been "overwhelmed" by the support from family, friends and "even strangers", adding that the "you've inspired me to get better, not bitter".

An online fundraiser for her would now be closed, she wrote, with the money raised giving her the chance to recover at home as well as "options for further medical treatment down the road".

"I still have a long way to go, but my recovery has been remarkable, and a huge part of that is because of the absolute army of love, support, prayers and encouragement surrounding my family and I from all over the world."

In an interview with Nine Network's 60 Minutes, due to be aired this weekend, Stewart described seeing the shark's "horrific" face.

"I'll never forget its face - it was a monster," she says.

"It was holding onto my leg and I just thought of (my daughter) August, and I thought, 'she's not going to have a mum. She's gonna grow up without a mum'."

Fighting back tears, she goes on: "I couldn't handle that, I didn't want her to not have a mum. I just thought, I've got to fight it, do everything I can to be here."

There have been a spate of shark attacks in Australia this year, with four attacks over a two-day period in January, including one on a 12-year-old boy who later died from his injuries.

In May, a man was killed by a shark in Queensland while spearfishing and in Western Australia, a father-of-two died after he was attacked by a 4m (13ft) shark.

News.title: Race Across the World star Jo Gardiner dies aged 61 one year after son's death
News.content:
