Gardiner, a physiotherapist from Manchester, travelled across South America with her son Sam in the second series of the BBC show, which aired in 2020.

Her family said she was "one of a kind" who "lived fully, fiercely and never did anything by halves".

News.title: Why is it so hard to find an NHS dentist? Find out how many have closed where you live
News.content:
Sykes says that none of his friends in his graduating class in dentistry still works in the NHS. "My friends have gone private, retired or teach - any pathway to avoid NHS dentistry."

Shiv Pabary, chair of the British Dental Association's General Dental Practice Committee, says the situation is "the direct result of choices made by successive governments". He warns that unless ministers "fix and fund NHS dentistry", more dentists could choose to reduce their NHS work or leave the service altogether.

Overall dentist practice numbers have risen in England over the last decade.

"This is not a shortage of dentistry but a shortage of NHS dentistry," says Dayan. "Practices will need to be incentivised back into NHS work in the places where the NHS footprint has thinned most."

While most parts of England recorded declines in practices offering NHS dental care, the reductions were smallest in North West London, the Black Country and North East London.

North East London was the only area to see any increase during the period, recording one additional practice offering NHS treatment compared with a decade ago.

Every other region of England saw the number of NHS dental practices fall.

Looking at the number of practices doing NHS work is not the same as looking at exactly how much health service capacity there is - practices can vary in size. But if you look at other measures such as the amount of treatment being done, the numbers are still down, although not as steep as the fall in practice numbers.

The government says that it is changing the dental contract and training more dentists in the areas most in need. The government says it will also make it a requirement for newly qualified dentists to practice in the NHS for a minimum period of at least three years.

Campaign group 38 degrees calls the current dental crisis "shameful", with people being "forced to pay money they can't afford or suffer with the pain, shame, and further complications that come from being denied vital NHS healthcare".

News.title: UK's rarest bird of prey rears new chicks in secret location
News.content:
The UK's rarest bird of prey has successfully nested for the second year running in the same secret location, the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB) has reported.

A male Montagu's harrier, known as "AU" by conservationists, bred with two different females, rearing six chicks across two nests on English farmland.

Montagu's harriers were put on a "red list" of birds most at risk in the UK in 2021. Numbers have declined from a high of nine successful nests in 2011, to no evidence of successful breeding between 2020 and 2024.

An RSPB spokesperson said: "We are doing our absolute utmost to save this iconic species in the UK and are delighted with six flying juveniles this year."

Four chicks hatched in the same secret location last year.

The charity said careful monitoring, in partnership with the farmers on whose land the birds nested, meant the nests were protected by fences to exclude ground predators such as foxes.

The single male Montagu's harrier has also been working very hard to keep his two nests of hungry chicks fed.

The BBC was given exclusive access to the nest and was able to witness some of the spectacular feeding behaviour of the raptors: the male drops prey in mid-air and the female rolls upside down to catch it in her talons.

News.title: Doctors said I was too young to have endometriosis at 13 - I had to take morphine to cope
News.content:
But the most frustrating thing for Grace, and why she contacted BBC Your Voice, is because she does not feel medical experts recognise that teenagers and adolescents can suffer from endometriosis.

Grace's GP did not diagnose her condition and nor did the first consultant she saw privately.

She says: "Even a specialist didn't believe me. And if a specialist won't listen to me, who will?" It was not until the family pushed for a second private opinion that she got a positive diagnosis.

Endometriosis, which occurs when tissue similar to the lining of the womb grows outside it, can cause debilitating symptoms, such as pelvic pain, heavy periods and fatigue. About 10% of women are affected by it, according to NHS data.

This week BBC presenter Emma Barnett revealed she had to have a hysterectomy for her endometriosis - which she said she never wanted to have.

It can develop at any age once periods begin - and it is a common misconception that only older women suffer from the condition, says the charity Endometriosis UK,

Faye Farthing, a spokesperson for the charity, says the government, NHS and health practitioners need to improve menstrual health education for young people "if we are to ensure the next generation are not robbed of the future they deserve".

The charity says it can take a long time to diagnose endometriosis - an average of nine years in older women.

And in the early stages, for example with teenagers, it often doesn't show up on an ultrasound scan. However, new tests are being developed which will help spot the condition earlier.

Getting pregnant can be more difficult - even aged 14, Grace says she has been warned it is likely to affect her fertility. She's been advised she may not be able to have children after the age of 30 because of damage to her reproductive organs.

She feels rushed: "I have to have kids within the next 15 years, otherwise I might not be able to."

News.title: How to get £2,000 to play computer games at university
News.content:
As parents across the country prepare to wave their children off to university, conversations about family finances and the cost of living are growing ever more frequent - and fervent.

Yet every year, millions of pounds worth of scholarships and bursary funding goes unclaimed by students - with many unaware the extra help exists.

So roll up the next generation of gamers, who this year can apply for as esports scholarship from the University of Roehampton - with more than 100 handed out so far.

But can the students balance their studies and their esports? And is the scholarship set to catch on?

Esports, meaning electronic sports, is the name for competitive video gaming.

It is different from standard video gaming as esports includes spectators, much like traditional sports.

Gamers compete against one another in high-stakes tournaments for cash prizes and trophies.

News.title: Pubs and hotels could see business rates reformed after review
News.content:
A review is being launched into the way business rates are calculated for pubs and hotels in England and Wales, and could lead to a reform of the system.

The Treasury says business rates expert Jerry Schurder will lead the review into rate valuations and report back in March 2027, with the government calling for the views of landlords, hoteliers and business owners to feed in to the process.

Last month, Andy Burnham announced a 20% cut in business rates for pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England, to come into effect in April.

Pub groups have argued they face disproportionately higher rates bills, but other businesses have called for a wider reform of the rates system.

According to the British Beer and Pub Association (BBPA), 161 pubs closed in the first three months of this year across England, Scotland and Wales, equating to the loss of around 2,400 jobs.

Rising business rates are cited as one issue facing the sector, although there have also been complaints that increases in National Insurance and the minimum wage have made staff costs more expensive.

James Murray, financial secretary to the Treasury, said the new review would look at "a rethink of valuations - so that we can build a fairer system for the future".

Emma McClarkin, chief executive of the BBPA, said: "For years pubs have paid a disproportionately higher business rates bill which has ground down their ability to keep the doors open, so this review is sorely needed and hugely welcome."

The BBPA says pubs are valued differently for rates than retail venues. Instead of being based just on floor area, they are judged by a measure called Fair Maintainable Trade (FMT) - which means when a pub's turnover increases, so does its rates bill.

Jonathan Lawson, the chief executive of Butcombe Group, which has 120 pubs across the south and south west of England, told the BBC's Today programme that the use of FMT meant pubs were effectively being "punished for success", while large online retailers that operate out of warehouses were not subject to revenue-based rates calculations.

Their rates, he said, "are calculated based on what is deemed to be the market rent for that area, and takes very little on board in terms of revenue driven through that site".

"You can have a very large site paying a relatively low level of business rates versus a relatively small pub... paying a very high level of business rates."

Schurder is a former business rates policy lead at advisory firm Newmark UK, and his review will feed into the next rates revaluation in 2029.

Northern Ireland and Scotland set their own valuations, while Wales presently chooses to align its methodology with England. As the same approach is used across England and Wales, the review will be looking for responses from both nations.

Schurder's appointment was welcomed by Craig Beaumont of the Federation of Small Businesses (FSB) who said he would bring "crucial heavyweight business rates expertise into the Treasury".

However, Beaumont said the government needed to address the wider business rates system and exempt more smaller firms by increasing the rates relief threshold for small businesses.

Jonny Haseldine from the British Chambers of Commerce (BCC) also said the review of valuations should be wider.

"The full reform of business rates, promised by the government at the last election, is urgently needed. This continued piecemeal approach to reform is the wrong approach," he said.

While the BCC said hospitality was the sector most worried about rates, Haseldine warned firms in every sector were struggling with the "complex and outdated" system.

Shadow Chancellor Sir Mel Stride said the review was "far too late for a sector this Labour government has already done its best to kill off".

"Tax hikes on business premises and jobs, alongside job-destroying regulation in the Employment Rights Act, have left many hospitality businesses on the brink," he said.

Liberal Democrat Treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper said reform of business rates was "long overdue", but also called for an emergency VAT cut and a reverse to jobs tax changes "which have hammered hospitality in particular".

News.title: 'It took 30 years to talk about my teacher raping me'
News.content:
It wasn't until 2022 when she had grief counselling that she confronted what had happened.

The following year she made a formal complaint to police.

"I am a mum now and my children are the age that I was then - and that cannot happen to them," she said.

She said finding the courage to contact police was difficult and it "took me a few days just to pluck up the courage".

Det Con Andrew Jones, from West Midlands Police's Major Crime Team, said: "I would like to express my gratitude to the brave woman who came forward to report what Allen had done to her as a child.

"She has been so brave throughout the investigation and court process."

Allen was sentenced at Birmingham Crown Court in July.

His defence argued the offence was committed during a difficult period in his life while he was experiencing anxiety.

But, during his sentencing remarks, His Honour Judge Paul Farrer KC, said he did not accept Allen's judgement was impaired at the time and said he had abused a position of trust.

That his offending remained undiscovered for more than three decades meant he was able to enjoy life in the community, the court heard.

It was noted the defendant was now in poor health, had diabetes, glaucoma and impaired hearing, had previously had a heart attack and might be experiencing the onset of Parkinson's disease.

The woman said it was not the sentencing but the guilty verdict that had been most important to her.

"I felt heard, I felt people have listened and they believe me," she added. "It is really validating and it raises your self-esteem a little bit, it means a lot."

News.title: Rain to return this week with chance of thunderstorms and flooding
News.content:
The weather is set to turn more unsettled this week as rain returns with a chance of thunderstorms and localised flooding.

Some places could see a return to showery conditions by Tuesday, but it is from Wednesday onwards that more widespread and persistent rain will arrive from the south.

The wet weather will be welcome for parched regions of the UK, but a lot more will be needed before drought conditions start to ease.

As well as the rain, temperatures will also be on the rise once more, as warmer air moving in could push midweek highs close to 27C (81F) in places.

News.title: Girl gets tumour diagnosis 12 hours after eye test
News.content:
A mum said she "fell apart" after finding out her four-year-old daughter had a brain tumour, just 12 hours after an eye test.

Katie, 41, said her daughter Phoebe, now five, started to be sick and was getting severe headaches in February, but was told "it was just migraines" by a GP.

Following an eye test in May, Katie was called by the optician who told her to take her daughter straight to A&E at Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge. Just hours later, she was diagnosed with a brain tumour.

"I fell apart and just sobbed and sobbed," said the mum from St Neots, Cambridgeshire. Thankfully, Phoebe's tumour was not cancerous and she is now under the care of specialists.

Katie said: "I felt like we were probably wasting the hospital's time because Phoebe was running around playing like normal but, looking back, she was probably the sickest kid there.

"I kept thinking, how am I going to tell her dad and the other children?

"I kept asking if Phoebe would survive but the doctors said they were unable to answer that at that time, which is the worst thing in the world as a parent."

News.title: Reform says it will prioritise British-born young workers for social housing
News.content:
Reform previously announced it would evict foreign nationals from social housing - a plan criticised by housing charity Shelter which said building more homes is the solution, rather than "changing the order of the queue" and "stoking division".

Tice will set out how Reform intends to pay for the 50,000 affordable homes during Monday's news conference, the party added.

"It is time for us to prioritise young British workers, and that is what our policy is about," Tice said on Sunday.

"I have spent my entire career in property development, as a private citizen I have led companies which delivered thousands of new homes. In government I will break down the barriers to getting generation rent onto the housing ladder."

He added it is "time to get Britain building" and give "our young people the homes they deserve".

UK or Irish nationals made up 88.5% of main social home householders in 2024/25, according to the English Housing Survey.

That means around 11.5% of main householders, the perÂ­son in whose name the social home is renÂ­ted, were non-UK or Irish nationÂ­als.

For its part, Reform estimates 540,000 social homes are currently occupied by foreign nationals.

Labour rubbished Reform's plans and insisted social housing is already "tightly controlled".

"Illegal migrants, asylum seekers and migrants on student or work visas are not eligible for social housing," the Labour spokesperson said.

Labour said the Reform plan would target long-term UK residents that have contributed to our country but are not British citizens, including NHS staff.

"It would leave more families at risk of homelessness and drive up use of temporary accommodation at the taxpayers' expense. It would also mean renegotiations with the EU, resulting in years of wrangling."

The Conservative Party, which also said it would revoke the right of foreign nationals to social housing, accused Reform of "trying to catch up" with its policies.

The Tories have said their plan, which would allow Irish citizens and some EU nationals to remain in social housing, would free up around 230,000 homes.

Sir James Cleverly, shadow housing secretary, added: "The Conservatives have already set out comprehensive plans to ensure British nationals are at the front of the queue for social housing. Now Reform are trying to catch up.

"We also believe in a home owning society and that those who work hard should be able to buy their own home, without unnecessary barriers standing in their way."

Liberal Democrat spokesperson Gideon Amos said that Reform's plan was a "cruel gimmick".

Green MP SiÃ¢n Berry said her party would tackle housing issues by ending Right to Buy, building and buying hundreds of thousands of new council homes, and introducing rent controls.

She added: "Another blatantly racist and cruel policy from Reform, adding to a host of plans to create a two-tier Britain â one for those born in the UK and one for everyone else."

News.title: CrossCountry to run full train service after power outage causes major disruption
News.content:
Train operator CrossCountry says it expects to run a full service on Monday after cancelling nearly all of its UK services the day before following a power cut at its control centre.

The outage in Birmingham at the weekend brought disruption from Glasgow to Penzance.

Major routes were affected between Birmingham and Manchester, which pass through Stoke-on-Trent, Coventry and Wolverhampton. Journeys from Leeds to York and Cheltenham to Cardiff were also caught in the travel chaos, leaving passengers frustrated.

On Monday morning, CrossCountry reported a handful of service cancellations, although these were put down to trains departing late and staff shortages.

Customers are advised to check their journey before travelling.

The operator on Sunday thanked passengers for their patience and understanding during the disruption.

Tickets purchased for travel on CrossCountry services on Sunday will be valid for travel on CrossCountry services until Wednesday, the company has said.

News.title: Wicker Man director's sons complete their late father's film trilogy
News.content:
Robin Hardy always envisaged his iconic 1973 folk horror film The Wicker Man as the first part of a trilogy.

The Wicker Tree, released in 2011, brought him closer to that ambition, but his death in 2016 at the age of 86 left the project incomplete.

Now his sons, Justin and Dominic, have been able to complete their father's trilogy, after finding a script for the final film.

Wrath of the Gods has its premiere at the FrightFest horror festival in London, external on Friday, a family dream made possible thanks to the surprise discovery of some long-lost family archive.

"The person who bought Justin's old family home said they'd discovered six sacks of letters, scripts and other material pertaining to Robin Hardy and The Wicker Man in the attic," says Dominic, an art historian at the University of Quebec in Montreal.

"Justin's first instinct was to burn them, but we couldn't ignore this original source material. Although we left it unopened for six months or more."

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool united in tribute to legend Keegan
News.content:
Kevin Keegan's family were in attendance as Newcastle United and Liverpool supporters came together to pay tribute to the former England captain.

Keegan, who played for both clubs, before going on to manage Newcastle, died at the age of 75 last month following a battle with cancer.

As the teams met for the first time since his death, in their Premier League season opener at St James' Park on Sunday, members of Keegan's family were present in the directors' box.

A number of Keegan's former players from this memorable first spell in charge of Newcastle, between 1992 and 1997, were also at the game.

News.title: Man killed in A66 crash was awaiting trial over alleged assault on police officer
News.content:

One of the men killed in the A66 crash was awaiting trial over alleged crimes against police officers, court records show.

Makai Saddington, 18, was among those pronounced dead at the scene in Teesside on Saturday after a Volkswagen Passat that was driving the wrong way along a dual carriageway after being pursued by police hit an marked armed response vehicle.

Court records show that Saddington was accused of assaulting a police officer and of causing racially aggravated alarm or distress to another in Middlesbrough on June 9.

He had appeared before Teesside Magistrates’ Court on July 17 charged with the offences and was awaiting trial.

Pc Matthew Blades, 37, and Pc Tom Clough, 38, were killed when the Volkswagen hit their marked armed response vehicle.

open image in gallery Makai Saddington, 18, had appeared before Teesside Magistrates’ Court on July 17 charged with the offences and was awaiting trial ( Facebook )

Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Theo Rae, 17, and 23-year-olds Michael Robert Cahill and Jacob Matusiak also died, along with Saddington, in the incident early on Saturday.

It has also been reported that Saddington was involved in filming dangerous driving in TikTok videos before the fatal crash took place.

The government has now urged TikTok and other social media firms to remove wrong-way driving videos.

Defence minister Luke Pollard said social media platforms should act to remove posts of that nature.

open image in gallery Police officers at the scene of the fatal crash involving a police car and a Volkswagen Passat on the A66 ( Owen Humphreys/PA )

Asked about videos being shared on TikTok, Snapchat and other forums, he told BBC Radio 5 Live: “We’ve communicated to those social media platforms that have been hosting content that celebrates this type of dangerous behaviour on our roads to take down that content.

“I think we all need to give the police time, but there’s also things we can be doing in the meantime to make sure that the internet is a safer place for everyone, that doesn’t celebrate and load views and therefore financial incentives on people to generate such awful content.”

He added: “I want to see social media companies step up.

“It’s one of the reasons they’ve argued against some of the regulations, saying they can police themselves. Well this is the perfect opportunity to demonstrate it. Remove the content that celebrates dangerous behaviour on our roads.

“While that content is online, the Government will be using the powers in the Online Safety Act to compel the platforms to take it down.

open image in gallery Pc Tom Clough and Pc Matthew Blades died in the crash ( Cleveland Police/PA )

“But if the social media platforms were to regulate themselves and remove it in the first place, not allow their algorithm to share this type of content, because they know exactly what type of content that algorithm is designed to share, then I think we’d be in a better place.”

TikTok has declined to give a statement in response, but said its policies strictly prohibit content that could cause significant physical harm, including dangerous driving, and that it is actively removing any videos and accounts that break its rules.

Cleveland police and crime commissioner Matt Storey acknowledged the reports about the TikTok videos, but urged people to avoid speculation.

He told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme: “Without being able to say whether that was anything like involved in this case, it’s absolutely idiotic for anybody to be doing anything other than being completely 100% focused on the road when they’re behind the wheel of a vehicle.

“And for somebody to be filming themselves or doing anything like that is absolutely ridiculous, and of course nobody should be doing that.

open image in gallery A police officer leaves flowers at the Cleveland Police HQ Memorial Garden in Middlesbrough, following the line-of-duty deaths of PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough ( PA )

“And it is a worrying situation if that’s becoming more prevalent because it is incredibly dangerous.”

Online safety regulator Ofcom said: “Under the Online Safety Act, platforms must minimise children’s exposure to violent material and content promoting dangerous challenges.

“In July, we launched an investigation into TikTok’s compliance with its child safety duties, and we’ve shown we’ll take action if evidence suggests companies are falling short.”

A fundraiser created by the Cleveland Police Federation for the families of the officers had reached more than £250,000 on Monday morning.

Cleveland Police launched the chase after receiving intelligence relating to “numerous incidents” linked to a Passat, which activated an ANPR camera and is believed to have been using cloned plates, investigating watchdog the Independent Office for Police Conduct said.

open image in gallery (l-r) Jacob Matusiak, Theo Rae, Michael Robert Cahill, Makai Saddington and Cole Robert Worthy all died in the crash ( Facebook )

Pc Blades and Pc Clough were not involved in the original pursuit, but had been called to the area to assist with the search for the Passat.

Family members described former Civil Nuclear Constabulary officer Pc Clough as “our hero” who was “always on public duty”.

The father-of-two’s family called him “our superhero” and said: “He gave his life in the line of duty, protecting and serving others with courage, dedication and selflessness.”

In a statement issued by Cleveland Police, Pc Blades’ wife called him “my beloved husband, my best friend, and the most devoted father to our two young boys”.

She said he was “an adored son and brother, a perfect son-in-law, and the most fun uncle”.

“He was loved beyond words by all his family and friends, and his loss has left a space that can never be filled,” she said.

“Our children will grow up knowing what an incredible father he was and will always be, and I will carry his love, his memory and everything we shared with me always.”

She added: “Forever loved. Forever missed. Forever our superhero. Our Matt and Dad.”

Tributes for the five young men were also shared on social media, with many of their friends saying they “can’t believe it” and were “heartbroken” and “lost for words”.

One message, dedicated to all five, said: “We all knew use and knew use had hearts of gold and most loyalist lads.”

The Passat they were travelling in was spotted and an armed response vehicle pursued for just under seven minutes before the car drove on to the A66 in South Bank against the flow of traffic.

Police aborted the chase and continued to travel on the correct side of the carriageway.

The Passat crashed into Pc Blades and Pc Clough’s vehicle around 10 seconds after the chase ended.

The government has told TikTok and other social media companies to take down content featuring a social media trend showing people driving the wrong way down roads.

It comes after two “hero” police officers died after the police vehicle they were driving was struck by a Volkswagen Passat travelling on the wrong side of the A66 in Teesside on Saturday night.

Later reports claim one of the teenagers killed in the crash was involved in filming dangerous driving in TikTok videos before the fatal crash took place.

Defence minister Luke Pollard said social media platforms should act to remove posts showing people driving the wrong way down roads, saying they would need to “step up”.

“There's lots of content online on social media platforms of people celebrating dangerous driving, celebrating driving inappropriately on our roads down the wrong side of the roads, behaving incredibly badly,” he told BBC Breakfast.

open image in gallery Police officers at the scene of the fatal crash involving a police car and a Volkswagen Passat on the A66 ( PA )

“Now that's a decision that social media companies have now. They've argued for many years they don't need to be regulated that they can police themselves. So this is a challenge for them. Remove that content.

“They know exactly what content is on their site. They know how their algorithm works. They also know that people post content to get views.

“The more views you can get, sometimes you get money for it. So it's a financial incentive for people to post outrageous content that gets more people watching it.”

He told also BBC Radio 5 Live that the government will be using the powers in the Online Safety Act to compel the platforms to take dangerous driving content down.

“But if the social media platforms were to regulate themselves and remove it in the first place, not allow their algorithm to share this type of content, because they know exactly what type of content that algorithm is designed to share, then I think we’d be in a better place,” he said.

Five teenagers and young men who died driving on the wrong side of the road in the crash have also been named as Makai Saddington, 18, Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, and Jakub Matusiak, 23. No-one survived the collision, which is being investigated by the police watchdog.

Court records show that Saddington was accused of assaulting a police officer and of causing racially aggravated alarm or distress to another in Middlesbrough on June 9.

He had appeared before Teesside Magistrates’ Court on July 17 charged with the offences and was awaiting trial.

It has also been reported that Saddington was involved in filming dangerous driving in TikTok videos before the fatal crash took place.

Cleveland Police had launched a pursuit after spotting the VW acting “suspiciously”, the force said in the aftermath of the fatal crash.

Officers began following the car in South Bank, near Middlesbrough in Teesside, before it joined the A66 in the wrong direction.

open image in gallery PC Tom Clough (left) and PC Matthew Blades ( Cleveland Police )

Officers ended their pursuit, but just 10 seconds later the VW collided with an oncoming police armed response unit at 3.39am. The police car, which was travelling in the right direction, was not part of the pursuit.

In tributes released by Cleveland Police, the two officers’ families said they had died “in the line of duty” and that their lives will “never be the same”.

“He was our hero with a fantastic sense of humour,” PC Clough’s family said. “Jumped into action whenever needed, and willing to help anyone for any reason. Proudly fought for his country to make the world a better place. Always on public duty throughout his short life.”

In a separate tribute, PC Blades’ wife said he was a “devoted” father and her “best friend”.

Donations to a fundraiser set up by Cleveland Police to support the families of the two police officers have now reached over £250,000. Organisers said funds raised would be split equally between the two officers’ families and the federation would continue to provide support.

Indonesia on Monday intensified ground and aerial firefighting operations as huge blazes in central and western parts of the country scorched thousands of hectares of forests and peatland, created a choking haze that blanketed cities and crossed borders.

Indonesian authorities have been battling fires driven by an intensifying El Nino pattern and a prolonged dry season, generating dense smoke that crossed into Malaysia and Brunei, according to Indonesia’s National Disaster Management Agency, or BNPB.

The BNPB said Monday that fires remain active in several regions, while large-scale suppression efforts continue in fire-prone provinces including West, Central and South Kalimantan on Borneo island and in Riau, South Sumatra and Jambi on Sumatra island. The fires are part of a broader surge in wildfire activity across Indonesia this year.

After visiting areas devastated by forest and peatland fires in Central Kalimantan on Saturday, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto flew to fire-affected Riau province on Sumatra island, where more than 11,500 hectares (28,400 acres) have burned, to encourage authorities to get the haze cloud under control.

Prabowo vowed the government would continue supporting firefighting operations, including through the deployment of additional water-bombing helicopters and oxygen supplies for firefighters. He urged authorities to “thoroughly document and report the work being carried out by firefighting teams” directly to him.

The Transportation Ministry said it has authorized the use of 35 foreign-registered aircraft to support wildfire response operations, including water-bombing missions and aerial patrols. The ministry said the aircraft can be rapidly redeployed to disaster-hit areas as conditions change, while complying with Indonesian aviation safety regulations.

The Environment Ministry satellite data on Monday showed South Sumatra recorded the highest number of hot spots nationwide with 1,429, followed by West Kalimantan with 1,226 and Central Kalimantan with 811. East Kalimantan logged 576 hot spots, ahead of Riau with 503, while West Papua and Jambi recorded 468 and 458 hot spots, respectively.

Forestry Ministry data indicated that nearly 94,000 hectares (232,000 acres) burned in July alone.

Drought, strong winds and dry vegetation have complicated efforts to contain the fires, BNPB said in a statement on Monday. Some hot spots remained inaccessible to more than 10,700 ground firefighters who were deployed as of Sunday, prompting local officials to request additional water-bombing support and firefighting vehicles.

Cloud-seeding resumed over Kalimantan on Monday, with 30 helicopters for water-bombing and aerial patrol missions, and another 22 helicopters covering Sumatra.

Fires are a regular problem during dry season in Indonesia, a vast archipelago nation of more than 17,000 islands, and often strain relations with neighbors. Plantation owners and traditional farmers often start fires to clear land for farming. It triggers hazardous haze that reduces visibility, disrupts land and air transportation and threatens public health, sometimes affecting neighboring countries in Southeast Asia.

Meanwhile, Malaysia has suffered severe smoke from the fires, with its eastern state of Sarawak among the hardest hit, prompting the closure of nearly 600 schools and affecting about 200,000 students, the Sarawak government said.

___

Associated Press writer Eileen Ng in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, contributed to this report.

Police forces have responded to an online craze showing Dr Seuss’ famous Cat in the Hat character on streets across the UK and Ireland.

Over the past week, mocked-up images and videos using AI have appeared on social media platforms that claim to show the figure based on Mike Myers’ 2003 film adaptation walking along roads, crouching on cars and peering into windows.

Often they are shared with a warning for the town or city, such as “lock your doors Sheffield / Manchester” and “spotted Whitby”.

One user on TikTok even created a statement, supposedly from South Yorkshire Police, which said officers were “aware of a number of reports regarding a suspicious figure described as a ‘cat in the hat’ seen walking in the Meadowhall area”, adding it was taking the matter seriously while asking everyone to remain vigilant.

However, the force has been quick to debunk the fake.

A South Yorkshire Police spokesperson told The Independent: "To confirm, we have not had any reports of a cat in a hat in Meadowhall, or anywhere else in South Yorkshire for that matter.

“We can also confirm no recent sightings of his associates Thing One and Thing Two. On a serious note, if you do see posts online providing policing updates and advice, please check that they are from an official policing account.

“The cat is not out of the hat on this one... we don't have a new account or a new logo. Please don't believe everything you read on social media.”

Sightings have also been reported of the Cat in the Hat character in Lowestoft in Kent, Stroud in Gloucestershire, and Leeds in Yorkshire.

More sinisterly, a post on Facebook asks users if they have seen the “killer Cat in the Hat”. Another shows the character chasing a person down the street.

The issue has alarmed some people, with the BBC reporting that teenagers have decided not to go out at night as a result of the rumours.

Skye, aged 16, said: “I was having a sleepover but everyone started watching Cat in the Hat videos. It was 3am. I wanted to go home. When I started walking down my friends' driveway, I got totally freaked out that the Cat in the Hat was going to jump out. I had to call my mum to pick me up."

The viral posts have also been centred on Limerick and Wexford in Ireland.

In response, the local Gardaí [police] posted on Facebook: “In an unusual turn of events, we are hearing a lot about an elusive Dr Seuss character doing the rounds online, apparently causing havoc in neighbourhoods and towns across the country.

“Fortunately, we can rule out the issue, which is essentially an AI prompt that places the character into images/videos of familiar places. To be clear, the Cat in the Hat was not in your driveway while you were out and he is not currently hiding out in Curracloe.”

TikTok and Meta have been contacted for comment.

The viral posts on social media come amid a more dangerous trend on platforms of of wrong-way driving videos. Earlier this month, five teenagers died in a crash in Kildare in Ireland after a car was struck by another vehicle driving the wrong way on a motorway.

Seven people died on Saturday, including two police officers, after a head-on crash involving a car being driven the wrong way down the A66 near Middlesbrough. The police watchdog is investigating but it is not yet clear whether the men driving the vehicle were following the trend.

On Monday morning, defence minister Luke Pollard said social media companies should take down content featuring people driving the wrong way down roads.

Visitors heading up the hill to the Acropolis are wearing headwear of every kind under the harsh sun, from straw boaters and Panamas to baseball caps and bucket hats.

Hat racks are ubiquitous across central Athens this season. Local shops and kiosks maintain stacked outdoor displays as tourists look for protection against the intense midday heat.

Greece recorded a peak year for tourism in 2025, with the landmark attracting roughly 4.6 million people. Sightseers spend hours exposed to mid-30s Celsius (mid-90s Fahrenheit) temperatures with scarce shade. At the base of the monument, even a carriage horse joined in, sporting a brown bucket hat altered with holes cut for its ears.

“You need a hat. I’m already red as it is,” said Jack Yosif, an Australian tourist wearing a black baseball cap. “It’s a bit more of a common thing nowadays, and people are a bit more aware.”

open image in gallery A Russian tourist tries on a hat and takes a selfie at a shop in Athens, Greece, Tuesday, Aug. 11, 2026. (AP Photo/Thanassis Stavrakis) ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

Scorching temperatures didn't deter a record 38 million visitors last year, the most recent for which there is data. The combination of extreme heat and high demand for sites – which means not everyone can visit in the morning – is adding urgency to sun protection.

Greek health campaigners have welcomed a growing awareness of the dangers of ultraviolet exposure and risk of heat stroke. Red Cross volunteers at the Acropolis hand out kits with sunscreen, water, information leaflets and red caps.

open image in gallery Tourists wearing hats take photographs on the rocky Areios Pagos Hill next to the Acropolis in Athens, Greece, Friday, Aug. 14, 2026. (AP Photo/Thanassis Stavrakis) ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

On nearby Syntagma Square, kiosk owner Konstantinos Mallios says hat sales have risen in recent years. His stylish and souvenir models run up to 20 euros ($24) while the cheapest costs 6 euros. Available elsewhere is semi-disposable headgear: mass-produced hats made using compressed paper pulp.

And there are more ostentatious options. At her basement workshop, hatmaker Lisa Sarigiannidou turns straw braids into boaters using century-old presses and molds in a matter of minutes. Her hats start at around 50 euros, with elaborate designs costing more than 100 euros.

open image in gallery A tourist chooses a hat from a souvenir shop in Athens, Greece, Wednesday, Aug. 12, 2026. (AP Photo/Thanassis Stavrakis) ( AP )

“People’s attitudes toward hats have changed,” said Sarigiannidou, who was trained by her hatmaker father. “In the past, when a young woman tried on a hat and looked at herself in the mirror, she usually laughed. Now they try them on seriously ... and they wear them straight out the door.”

Meanwhile, another devastating summer of wildfires has reignited a debate about the safety of Greece's power networks, especially its cables, which face intense heat and gale force winds and often criss-cross rural areas of scrub or forest that haven't seen rain in months.

News.title: Father of three slain children takes psychologist to court over withheld records
News.content:

The father of three young children killed by their mother is asking a judge to force a psychologist who evaluated her to turn over records that he says could be central to his lawsuit against Los Angeles authorities.

Erik Denton, whose three children were killed by their mother, Liliana Carrillo, in 2021, alleges in his civil lawsuit that Los Angeles police failed to take warning signs about Carrillo’s deteriorating mental health seriously and did not adequately share information with county social workers.

Denton, who filed the lawsuit in April 2022, is suing Los Angeles County and others over the deaths.

The father of three children, allegedly drowned by their mother, is asking a judge to compel a psychologist to produce records from her sessions ( LA Police Department )

“This case arises from the death of plaintiff's three children who were murdered by their mother, Liliana Carrillo, while she was suffering from severe mental health issues,” Denton’s attorneys wrote in court papers. “Her mental health is a central issue in the case.”

Ahead of a Sept. 14 hearing, Denton’s lawyers asked Pasadena Superior Court Judge Jared Moses to order psychologist Dianna Lynn Barnes to comply with a subpoena seeking records related to her evaluation of Carrillo.

Barnes has resisted the request, maintaining that the records are privileged or otherwise protected from disclosure, according to Denton’s attorneys.

Carrillo’s mental health was evaluated by several professionals as part of the criminal case against her, including Barnes and psychiatrist Dr. David S. Rad.

According to Denton’s court filings, Rad cited Barnes’ findings in his own report. Barnes concluded that Carrillo suffered from bipolar disorder with peripartum onset and post-traumatic stress disorder and that her bipolar disorder left her unable to understand that her actions were morally wrong, Denton’s attorneys said.

A process server delivered notice of Denton’s motion to Barnes’ Westlake Village office on Aug. 13, according to the filings.

Carrillo was 33 when her children — 6-month-old Sierra, 3-year-old Joanna and 2-year-old Terry — were killed on April 10, 2021.

In October 2024, Carrillo was found not guilty by reason of insanity in their killings. She was subsequently committed to a state mental health facility, where she remains subject to continuing judicial oversight.

Denton’s lawsuit now puts Carrillo’s mental health history at the center of a separate legal fight over whether authorities failed to respond adequately to warning signs before the children’s deaths.

England cricketer Brydon Carse is under investigation following an incident at a nightclub where he appeared to be handcuffed by police.

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) said the investigation is underway following an incident in Derby on Saturday night.

The Durham fast bowler is in England’s squad to face Pakistan in the second Test of their series at Lord’s this week.

Former England Test captain Ben Stokes, who is Carse’s team-mate at Durham, is also seen towards the back of the video.

His England and Durham team-mate Matthew Potts can also be seen talking to Carse while he is surrounded by four police officers.

“We are aware of an incident which is reported to have taken place in Derby last night, and are currently investigating,” an ECB statement said on Sunday.

“We will provide a further update when possible.”

It has been reported that Carse was not arrested and was released without charge. It is unknown what cause Carse to be detained by the police officers.

English cricket has been embroiled by several late-night incidents around bars and clubs over the last year.

Harry Brook was reportedly involved in a scuffle with a nightclub bouncer in Wellington the night before England played a ODI against New Zealand last October.

England’s Ashes Tour featured allegations of a “stag do” culture during their mid-series break in Noosa, where Ben Duckett was filmed seemingly intoxicated after hours.

Stokes and Gus Atkinson were then alleged to have broken curfew after the first Test against New Zealand this summer and were stood down from the second Test.

Joe Root, who has replaced Stokes as England captain following his retirement, subsequently abandoned England’s midnight curfew.

He told his England team-mates to “be adults, look after yourselves, look after each other”.

Carse has not played for England since the Ashes due to injury but could involved in the second Test against Pakistan this week.

The 31-year-old was an unused member of the squad as England wrapped up victory in the first Test against Pakistan in three days.

On Saturday, Carse was out celebrating Durham’s crushing Division Two victory over Derbyshire in the County Championship.

Carse took two wickets with Stokes starring with bat and ball in a 338-run win at Derbyshire with a day to spare. Potts finished with five for 46.

Durham have refused to comment on the incident, citing the ECB investigation.

Britons travelling by train this Bank Holiday weekend will be able to order a Domino's pizza directly to their seats.

In a UK-first, Trainline has partnered with the takeaway giant to provide the Train Line Train Thru facility on Lumo train services.

Delivery will only be available on some services between London Euston and Stirling in both directions across the Bank Holiday weekend.

Passengers can order a pizza in advance, with the food delivered by staff waiting at Preston station - which is roughly halfway through the trip from London to Stirling.

Travellers can pick from a number of classic Domino’s pizzas - including Cheese and Tomato, Peperoni Passion, Vegi Supreme and Plant-Based Margheri-tastic.

open image in gallery Passengers can pick between Cheese and Tomato, Peperoni Passion, Vegi Supreme and Plant-Based Margheri-tastic for their delivery ( Domino's )

Booking will be open until midnight before a journey.

Research by the brands found that over half (53 per cent) of travellers underestimate their hunger on long trips.

Additionally, research showed that a majority (57 per cent) of travellers thought that food on offer at stations and on board UK trains was lacking.

A third (35 per cent) said they had attempted to get a takeaway delivered while on board a train - but only one in five (20 per cent) managed it successfully.

Natalie Marques, Head of Creative Innovation at Trainline said: “Food shapes how people enjoy travel, so we’re making this busy bank holiday and festival weekend even better by ensuring passengers can satisfy their pizza cravings en route.”

Ryan Kenton, PR Manager & Special Deliveries Expert at Domino’s added: “Over the years we’ve heard the stories of train travellers trying to time a cheeky pizza delivery with a station platform visit. Domino's is known for super speedy delivery, so we’re delighted to partner with Trainline to make those dreams come true.”

It comes as the pizza chain announced it would be recruiting 5,000 new workers in the next few months.

open image in gallery Domino’s has just announced it is creating over 1,000 jobs to cope with demand with the run up to Christmas ( PA )

Jobs are being created for in-store staff and delivery drivers at its 1,400 stores across the UK and Ireland between now and Christmas.

The company said its research showed how jobs often seen as short-term can provide valuable experience, transferable skills and opportunities for longer-term progression.

Domino’s said nine in 10 of its store managers started out as an in-store team member or driver.

Bookings for the Trainline Train Thru are open from today on a first-come, first-served basis.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Frustrated Russell fails to make up ground as Norris wins incident-packed Dutch GP
News.content:
George Russell had another frustrating Sunday as the Dutch Grand Prix weekend slipped by with him failing to reduce his deficit to leader Kimi Antonelli. In a thrilling finale to the 72-lap race at the Dutch seaside, Lando Norris took his second victory in a row with two bold overtakes in one lap.

Yet compatriot Russell was irritated by Mercedes team orders for him to let Antonelli through into second place in the closing stages. It was a decision he believed risked a double podium for the team and threatened to put him even further behind his team-mate in the standings, with two charging Ferraris close behind. It was a race that, once again, fell away, despite Russell doing little wrong.

“Is he [Antonelli] fighting for the win or is he planning to catch Norris?” he asked, when the McLaren driver was 11 seconds down the road – the margin he would win by. “Yeah – we just lost a double podium here, mate,” was his response after moving aside.

Whilst Norris, who lost his lead from pole to Antonelli on the first lap, sealed the victory with two superb overtakes on lap 54 – first the Italian and then Lewis Hamilton – Russell had to mount a stout defence from Hamilton to secure third. It was against the odds, as both Ferraris, like Antonelli, were on fresh rubber after pitting under a late virtual safety car. Like Russell, Hamilton was critical of his team for their strategy choices.

Russell’s first podium finish since Silverstone – with his sprint victory on Saturday – means he at least retakes second place in the championship from Hamilton, but trails Antonelli by the same 59 point-gap he had after Hungary. That is despite him looking the faster and more comfortable Mercedes driver on Friday and Saturday.

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

News.title: How to spend a perfect weekend in Lake Como
News.content:
An hour drive north of Milan, Lake Como is the most glamorous of Italy’s lakes, hemmed in by the snow-capped Alps with picture-perfect villages on the water. Milanesi pop here for the day for a breath of fresh air and to soak up the fabulous vistas, while international visitors – the Clooneys, the Kennedys – have long been drawn by the grand lakefront hotels and the elegant mahogany Riva boats that zip along the lake’s deep blue waters.

Smart hotels and expensive boats aside, Lake Como is rich in culture, with opulent villas that once belonged to artists, writers, opera singers and explorers. Pliny the Elder, author of the first encyclopaedia, was born here, while 19th-century soprano Giuditta Pasta is known to have entertained composers Bellini and Donizetti in her lakefront residence on the eastern shore.

Though famous spots such as pretty Bellagio still pull in the majority of visitors, the lake has retained its authenticity, with plenty of sleepy fishing villages, such as Laglio, Torno and Nesso, home to rustic, family-run trattorias serving up traditional hearty fare, including risotto al pesce persico (risotto with perch).

News.title: Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair
News.content:
It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

News.title: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions
News.content:
The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

News.title: All Blacks stun Springboks in statement win
News.content:
Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry did not begin with the year’s greatest game, but a New Zealand victory against the odds, at high altitude in Johannesburg, has poured intrigue and interest on to a series which was already brimming with them.

The All Blacks’ recent record at Ellis Park, the Springboks’ spiritual home, is by no means shabby – this was their fourth victory from the last six visits – but few fancied Dave Rennie’s galvanised Kiwis on Saturday, against the back-to-back world champions, after a week which had been dominated by chat of officials and law interpretations.

Yet, this stunning victory was almost as comfortable as it was surprising. New Zealand outscored their hosts by five tries to one and, by the end, a 13-player Springboks outfit – both Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach were sin-binned within a minute of each other – were left chasing shadows in an Ellis Park which had been stupefied into silence.

It was at the beginning of that 13-player period when New Zealand put the game to bed, with Will Jordan crossing for his second try. But the damage had already been done by a cast of Kiwi conquerors. Ardie Savea, captain and No 8, could not have delivered more for the cause; Luke Jacobson and Tupou Vaa’i on the flanks were more than deputies to Savea; the locks, until Josh Lord’s unfortunate departure just before half-time, were magnificent; and, behind them, Cam Roigard continues to look every bit the equal of those phenomenal French scrum-halves. The New Zealand midfield got the upper hand on their much vaunted counterparts, too, on the day of Damian de Allende’s 100th cap for South Africa.

Sports.title: When is the Champions League 2026/27 draw? Start time, FREE stream and pots as Arsenal and Man Utd learn fate
Sports.content:
EUROPE’S footballing elite will attempt to dethrone back-to-back supremos PSG as the Champions League gears up for its next electrifying instalment.

Last season’s final saw the Parisian powerhouse sneak past Arsenal after an agonising penalty shoot-out in Budapest crushed the Gunners’ bid to bag North London’s first Champions League crown.



Luis Enrique and his glittering array of attacking talent are strongly tipped to extend their continental dominance and secure a three-peat, having also thumped Inter Milan 5-0 in the 2024/25 curtain-closer.

Hot on their heels will be vengeful Premier League champions Arsenal, alongside German giants Bayern Munich and a Barcelona side bursting with eight top talents from Spain’s World Cup-winning squad.



Five Premier League sides will do battle with Europe’s big boys, with Manchester City, Manchester United, Aston Villa and Liverpool all in the draw for the league phase along with Mikel Arteta‘s runners-up.

A staggering six English clubs reached the last 16 in a record-breaking 2025/26 competition, but the initial euphoria quickly fell flat after four failed to progress further and Liverpool were outclassed by PSG in the quarter-finals.



The fight for the most coveted prize in European club football will kick off with a league phase once more, and SunSport has all the crucial details for the draw.

When is the Champions League draw?

The draw for the league phase of the 2026/27 Champions League will take place on Thursday, August 27.

Proceedings are scheduled to begin at 5pm BST.

Uefa’s headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland, will host the event.

How to watch the Champions League draw FREE

The Champions League draw will be broadcast live and will be available to watch FREE on Uefa.com, Uefa.tv and the Uefa app.

TNT Sports 1 will also air the draw on regular TV, and subscribers will be able to stream it via HBO Max.

Alternatively, you can follow all the ties as they get confirmed on the night through SunSport’s live blog of the draw.

How does the Champions League league phase draw work?

Europe’s premier club competition will once again follow a Swiss System, commencing with a 36-team league phase in which each side plays eight times, evenly split between matches at home and on the road.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The continent’s top 36 teams are seeded into four pots containing nine similarly-matched teams, as determined by their five-year Uefa club coefficient.



Beginning with the top pot, a ball will be physically drawn before the automated software randomly draws two opponents from each pot, in an attempt to ensure every club faces an equally balanced set of rivals.

As stipulated by Uefa’s country protection rule, sides in the same league cannot play each other, and clubs cannot play more than two opponents from any one country.

The top eight teams in the final league standings automatically qualify for the last 16, while those who finish ninth to 24th are whittled down by two-legged play-off ties.

Sports.title: Shocking moment Leandro Trossard is SLAPPED in face as Besiktas blast referees over ‘historically shameful’ performance
Sports.content:
LEANDRO TROSSARD was SLAPPED in the face in just his second Turkish Super Lig game – and the culprit went unpunished.

The former Arsenal winger’s new club, Besiktas, called the refereeing “disgraceful” in a bitter statement after the culprit, Fidan Aliti, escaped a red card.



In an off-the-ball incident, Trossard was tugging at the shirt of Aliti, who responded by thrusting his right palm at the Belgian’s face.

After a brief moment of shock, Trossard went down clutching his head and gave the match officials a decision to make.



But neither referee Adnan Deniz Kayatepe nor the VAR took action.

Trossard, 31, was perplexed that even those with access to replays chose not to punish Aliti.

He said after the 1-0 defeat: “The decision should clearly have been changed; I think the opponent slapped me. Clear red card. The decision needed to be changed.”

Besiktas posted a clip of the slap and captioned it: “The 2026/27 season has begun!”

After the game they turned all guns blazing to social media and wrote a strongly-worded statement, which included: “The management displayed by the referees in our match against Corendon Alanyaspor has taken its place in history as a document of shame for Turkish refereeing.

“Adnan Deniz Kayatepe, the prince of the Central Referee Committee president whose scandalous decisions in last year’s Ziraat Turkish Cup semi-final still linger fresh in memories, has added yet another disgraceful performance to his record, as if to say, ‘Where did we leave off?’

“The opposing player slapped Trossard right in front of the world’s eyes.

“Referee Adnan Deniz Kayatepe failed to see the incident. Bülent Birincioğlu in the VAR room, meanwhile, remained silent.”

Trossard completed a £17.1million switch to Besiktas last month.

The former Brighton star helped Arsenal win the Premier League title last campaign with six goals in 31 league appearances, which rounded off three and a half impressive seasons in North London.

Sports.title: Fans convinced Cristiano Ronaldo revealed true feelings about Gianni Infantino after awkward video emerges

FANS believe Cristiano Ronaldo wasn’t impressed with meeting Fifa president Gianni Infantino after a clip of his reaction went viral.

Ronaldo was spotted at the Esports World Cup in Paris and was filmed greeting the Swiss chief.



Infantino is under fire after his failed attempt to sell off chunks of the World Cup.

He led a plot to set up a subsidiary called Fifa Forward Enterprises, which would have allowed investors to claim a stake in football’s biggest tournament.



Infantino has now faced widespread calls to resign after Uefa led a boycott against him, with the FA losing confidence in his leadership.

And some fans have claimed Ronaldo wasn’t pleased about meeting the 56-year-old at the event.



The video showed Ronaldo shaking hands with the ex-Uefa chief while having a brief chat.

But eagle-eyed supporter noticed Ronaldo appeared to grimace after walking away.”

He apologised for anger over the proposals but vowed to stay in his role following crisis talks with Fifa in Morocco.

Infantino was in the Dominican Republic this week and was tracked down by Sky Sports reporter James Matthews.



But after being questioned over his future, Infantino decided to make a joke about both himself and Matthews being bald.

Sports.title: Raphinha sparks frenzy with ‘Julian Alvarez’ celebration in Barcelona’s win over Elche
Sports.content:
RAPHINHA set tongues wagging with a Spider-Man celebration on the same day Julian Alvarez was heckled by Atletico Madrid fans.

Alvarez, whose nickname is La Araña (The Spider), has been trying to force his way out of Atleti this summer.



And Raphinha‘s Barca are one of multiple teams the Rojiblancos have turned away.

So it appeared telling that, on the same day Alvarez was given a hostile reception at the Metropolitano, Raphinha performed a celebration with the same Spider-Man hand gesture used by the Argentine after scoring Barca’s first goal in a 5-0 rout at Elche.



The conspiracy theories were busted by Raphinha’s wife after the game, however, as she revealed on Instagram that it was actually his son, Gael, who had requested the celebration.

Alvarez was jeered and whistled when he was brought on in the 67th minute of Sunday’s 2-2 draw with Villarreal.



And he was not even allowed to face the supporters after the game, with boss Diego Simeone admitting his dart down the tunnel was pre-planned.

He said: “It was a club decision to not let Julian Alvarez go over with his team-mates to greet the fans.”

Fans had been chanting during the game: “Get him out of here, tell him to get out of here.”

Evidently, Alvarez going public with his desire to leave Atletico has not gone down well.

Sports.title: Premier League cult hero’s son makes top-flight debut during Newcastle vs Liverpool
Sports.content:
ANDONI IRAOLA handed a league debut against Newcastle to a rising star with a name that will be familiar to Prem fans.

The Reds kicked off their competitive season with an emotionally-charged clash against Newcastle at St James’ Park.



The Magpies led the match twice but an injury-time penalty handed Dominik Szoboszlai the chance to equalise from the spot, sharing the points in the North East.

But while it was not the dream start to the season Liverpool as a whole were hoping for, it was a dream come true for young Lewis Koumas.



The 20-year-old winger arrived for his first Prem appearance as he was substituted on in the 78th minute in place of Ryan Gravenberch.

He didn’t get too much time on the ball, but was on the pitch to celebrate a memorable moment after the late penalty rescued a point with almost the last kick of the game.

It must have also been an equally special day for his dad, Premier League cult hero Jason Koumas.

The 46-year-old was himself released by Liverpool as an academy star, before making the switch to Tranmere Rovers.

He made over 100 appearances for the EFL side before joining Prem outfit West Brom.

He impressed in his first season with the club despite suffering relegation, winning their player of the season award.

While Sunday marked his first Premier League outing, he has already developed considerable experience in the English game after loans with Stoke, Birmingham and Hull over the past two seasons.

Sports.title: Alvarez booed by Atletico fans amid Arsenal interest - so will he leave?
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez was booed by Atletico Madrid supporters on Sunday after all the transfer window noise around him - does that mean a move to Barcelona or Arsenal is any closer?

The Argentine forward cut a disappointed figure when his own fans turned on him during Atleti's 2-2 draw with Villarreal.

And with Arsenal and Barcelona circling ahead of the September 1 deadline, what will happen now? Here is a state of play about the forward's future...

What happened with Alvarez on Sunday?

Alvarez played his first Atletico Madrid match on Sunday after revealing his desire to leave the club during the World Cup.

The Argentine striker wants to leave Diego Simeone's side to join Barcelona. However, Arsenal are also interested in bringing the former Man City striker back to the Premier League.

Barcelona want Alvarez but earlier this summer, Atletico accused the Catalan club of building a "relentless smear campaign" regarding the forward.

"Over the past few months, we've been subjected to a relentless smear campaign against one of our players," wrote Atleti on X.

"Calculated leaks, fake news, constant disrespect, the culé version of the propaganda machine inventing little stories, phone calls before head-to-head clashes.

"But of course, it would never occur to us either to have the vice president of referees on the payroll or to rely on political favours to register players. Respect and values."

With Alvarez wanting to join one of Atleti's closest rivals, the forward was greeted by whistles, boos and jeers from the Atletico Madrid fans on his return to action for the club.

His named was booed as the Atleti team was read out - and Alvarez was sat on the substitutes bench when the first jeers of the afternoon were made. They continued when Alvarez entered the pitch on the 66th minute.

After the game, the Argentina international left the field on his own after the 2-2 home league draw against Villarreal, while his team-mates stayed behind to applaud the fans.

Image: Alvarez was booed by his own supporters on Sunday - and walked off the pitch while his team-mates applauded the crowd

Asked about the situation, Simeone said in his post-match press conference: "People at the club told me that the club decided he shouldn't be near the stands and the fans.

"The decision was made by the club to keep him away and separate him from the rest of the team, so he would come to the locker room instead."

Does this raise Arsenal's chances of signing him?

Just because Alvarez was booed by his own Atletico supporters on Sunday, does not mean Arsenal fans should get excited yet.

Signing the Argentina striker - in what would arguably be the coup of the window - still looks very unlikely to happen before the deadline.

That is because of several obstacles still in their way; primarily the player's heart being set on a move to Barcelona and Atletico Madrid still refusing to sell him with just over a week to go.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking in April, Diego Simeone admitted that Arsenal are interested in Julian Alvarez.

Regardless of the feelings of Atletico fans, the club are digging their heels in, insisting they do not want to sell him to any club; certainly not to Barca and not the Premier League champions nor PSG either.

Arsenal will not completely give up - the door will always be open to a deal from their end right up until September 1 - but until they get an indication that Alvarez has shifted his thinking away from the Nou Camp, there is not much more Andrea Berta and Mikel Arteta can do.

Sky Sports News reported in July that Alvarez's family want to stay in Spain and that remains the case. They are happy and settled and the player's dream has long been to follow in the footsteps of compatriot Lionel Messi and star for Barca.

There is just over a week of the window remaining and anything can happen, but Barcelona will not give up either and it cannot be ruled out that they will not make another push to test Atletico's resolve - which has, until now, held firm.

Do Arsenal need Alvarez?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Friday Night Football panel discuss whether Arsenal are still shy of a world-class attacker that would see them get over the line to win their first UEFA Champions League title.

Arsenal are happy with their squad and showed in their resounding 3-0 opening day win over Coventry that they are in healthy place.

They clearly are now in a position in which signing only the very best will improve on what they have got. Alvarez is that and there are not many others on the market that come close.

However, Gary Neville feels Arsenal getting Alvarez would make them Champions League winners this season. Jamie Carragher feels the Gunners are one stardust signing away from becoming Kings of Europe.

"What a squad [Mikel Arteta] has built," said Neville. "If he puts another forward into that, if they could get Julian Alvarez somehow, that would light this place up as you'd have a world-class striker to go with all the world-class defenders and midfielders.

"They wouldn't just become Premier League title winners they'd go the next step and win a Champions League. It's a massive [few] days [in the transfer window]. He needs a bit of magic up front - someone that can win a game for you when you don't play well."

For the Premier League, Arsenal have shown they are already ahead of their rivals with an opening night victory, with summer signing Christos Tzolis and Martin Odegaard - who missed 30 matches last season - adding another dimension to Arsenal's attack.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Arsenal and Coventry.

Meanwhile, Liverpool, Manchester United and Tottenham all dropped points over the course of the first weekend, while Enzo Maresca admitted his Man City team - who were unconvincing in their late comeback win over Bournemouth - are still a "work in progress."

Arsenal could also move for a left-sided forward - which Alvarez is not - before the transfer deadline, if Gabriel Martinelli moves on this summer.

The Brazilian has been left out of Arsenal's last two matchday squads and has one year left on his deal - plus there is interest from Galatasaray and Saudi Arabia.

Arsenal could also let Gabriel Jesus leave this summer - but will not do so unless a replacement, such as Alvarez, is lined up.

So if Alvarez is unattainable - do Arsenal move elsewhere, or perhaps even not move for a forward at all? Despite being ahead of their rivals, the Premier League champions still face a big final week in the transfer window.
