Sports.title: What makes Norris say “I don't have a car to fight for the championship”?
Sports.content:
The 2026 Formula 1 championship finds itself at a curious intersection where nobody is willing to entertain the idea that they have the best car.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli said after finishing second to Lando Norris in the Dutch Grand Prix that Mercedes no longer has the best car – indeed, that it may only be the third best.

But Norris, now fourth in the standings with 159 points to Antonelli’s 242, was determined to play down talk of him staging a comeback in the final half of the season, despite winning two consecutive grands prix. "I don't have the car I need to fight for a championship," he said after his Dutch GP victory.

Many readers would be tempted to cite the so-called Mandy Rice-Davies principle – "Well they would say that, wouldn’t they?"

What’s clear, though, is that under the latest technical regulations there is still a difference in relative strengths between cars which complicates the competitive picture. In broad-brush terms the McLaren MCL40 thrives in fast corners, Ferrari’s SF-26 is strong in terms of carrying good speed into slow corners, while the Mercedes W17 is somewhere between the two. That makes the competitive balance heavily dependent on circuit layout.

Norris’s contention is that his car is insufficiently rounded to be dominant across the remaining rounds in the way last year’s McLaren was the car to beat at most tracks.

Norris played down the significance of his Dutch GP victory Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

"We have a strong car in certain areas," he said. "It's not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere. We're very, very strong in high speed. The place we've improved the car the most is high-speed performance.

"No one matches us in high speed. And that's a good thing. My pace advantage to Mercedes in Turn 7, Turn 8 was crazy.

"But their advantage that they have to us in slow speed is also crazy. And therefore I don't have the confidence to say, yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season. I know I've just won two races in a row and two poles in a row, but at the minute I don't have the car I need to fight for a championship.

"And I know that's quite a big comment, but I think last year I understood what is needed from a car and what was needed from me. And I know the level that I am now and what I can perform at. And I know just what I need from the car – and what tracks we have coming up where we're going to certainly struggle more."

The issue is more complex than simply saying a particular car is fast around a certain type of corner. This year’s cars are shorter, narrower and slightly lighter – and the chassis characteristics are more interconnected with power unit performance than ever before, given the influence of corner-entry speeds on energy harvesting.

McLaren's decision to run a short wheelbase, helping it save weight at the start of the season, has baked in certain shortcomings in terms of how much aerodynamic load the team can squeeze from the floor.

Performance is often hugely variable between tyre compounds. In Saturday’s sprint race, running mediums, Norris struggled with rear degradation and was overtaken by Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc in the closing stages. In the grand prix he took the restart on used softs, was passed by Antonelli at the start, and didn’t really get into the race until the hard-compound tyres went on.

Norris was able to pressure championship leader Antonelli later in the Zandvoort race Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

"We put on the hard tyres," he said. "We were a bit more aggressive with how we wanted to approach the stint. And we turned things around. I had that feeling in the car that I wanted. I went from just not feeling like I was going to win a race to at least we can force him [Antonelli] to make mistakes.

"When I get what I need from a car, when I have the front I want, when I get the confidence with the rear on entries – just when I get what I need to be able to know and predict every single corner, I'm going to win a race."

Norris has a driving style slightly more aligned to Max Verstappen than the likes of George Russell or even his own team-mate, Oscar Piastri. Rather than separating the throttle off/brake on and turning phases, he likes to blend the throttle and brakes and take a shallower approach angle. Essentially he is feeling for the point in the overlap where the front tyres begin to exert more lateral grip, which helps rotate the car and carry more speed into the corner, towards the apex.

This requires the car not only to have a 'strong' front end, but also to communicate what the front tyres are doing, which represents a tough engineering challenge. Modern F1 cars require a consistent ride height for the aerodynamics to function optimally, so the suspension geometry is designed to minimise dive and squat. A side of this is that it saps driver 'feel'.

Some can live with that, some can’t, which is why McLaren designed an alternate front suspension geometry with a revised kingpin angle for Norris when he was floundering at the beginning of last season. Once he has that feel he can be very adaptable in terms of his lines and the degree of overlap between throttle and brake, which is why he thrives in low-grip conditions.

But although he has a huge amount of adaptability within this range, he still needs that strong front end, good transmission of feel, and confidence that the rear axle will rotate predictably on cue.

"It's clear where our weaknesses are," Norris concluded. "Therefore we need to attack those things. And until we do that, it's still going to be a very tough end of the season."

Sports.title: FIA explains safety car formation lap after F1 driver criticism at Dutch GP
Sports.content:
The opening stages of the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort descended into chaos after rain had started to fall during the grid procedure.

Max Verstappen crashed heavily on the exit of the final corner on the opening lap of the race. The Red Bull driver admitted that it was entirely his own mistake. The Dutchman thought he could get back on the throttle, but that part of the track was clearly still too wet.

Behind Verstappen, Gabriel Bortoleto also came close to crashing, although he miraculously managed to keep his Audi out of the wall, while it was even more remarkable that team-mate Nico Hulkenberg managed to avoid him.

The German immediately said over the radio that he feared he was going to T-bone Bortoleto.

"It was just that corner, if I'm very honest with you. It was full wets, that place. I think that's why Max lost it and it was the same for me," Bortoleto said in the media pen post-race.

"I was on the downside of the banking. I did a little reaction move to the left, I think, when I saw big smoke coming up ahead. And when I did that, I just went as well."

According to Gasly, F1 drivers would have been able to get their tyres up to temperature more effectively if the formation lap had been completed without the safety car Photo by: Clive Rose / Getty Images

Would a normal formation lap have been better?

According to the drivers, the rest of the track had already dried by that point, meaning it was simply a matter of surviving the final two corners. Starting on slicks therefore made sense, as did the FIA’s decision to opt for a standing start.

That said, several drivers were critical of how the start procedure was carried out at Zandvoort.

"If we would go the way we did with one lap behind the safety car and a standing start, then I would have preferred to just do a normal out-lap, so we would have pushed a bit faster,” Pierre Gasly said when asked by Motorsport.com.

"I thought the point was to go at least once through the last corner and the banking with the safety car before doing the normal race start. And yeah, it was damp."

According to the Alpine driver, the FIA would have been better off choosing between two conventional options: a rolling start behind the safety car or a standing start with a normal formation lap.

"I'm sure we'll review at the next race what the drivers' feedback was," Gasly continued. "But I think it was either no safety car and only one formation lap or with the safety car at least giving us one extra lap."

Red Bull stand-in Liam Lawson shared that view and added that he already knew before the start that the procedure would lead to chaos.

Lawson emphasises that he deliberately left more margin than his team-mate Verstappen in the final corner Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

"I don't know why we had the safety car. To do a standing start and also do a lap behind the safety car makes no sense," Lawson said when asked by Motorsport.com.

"I'm not sure what the reasoning of that was, but I feel like we could all see that coming. We were all probably saying the same thing before when we got the news, but we didn't have control over that."

FIA explains reasoning behind safety car formation lap

When asked by Motorsport.com, the FIA clarified that it acted on the information available at the time.

The race director first sent the medical car out for a reconnaissance lap, something an FIA spokesperson said does not normally happen.

The feedback from the medical car was that there was still standing water at Turns 2 and 3, with Turn 3 – the Hugenholtz corner – also being the first banked corner on the circuit. Based on that information, the FIA considered it safer to complete the formation lap behind the safety car.

The intention at that point was to have a standing start, but by completing the formation lap behind the safety car, race control kept both options open. If the standing water had been deemed too dangerous, it could still have opted for a rolling start.

Williams driver Carlos Sainz, however, felt the latter would not have been a solution and would not have prevented the chaos in the final corner.

Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"I think, given it was towards the end of the lap, a non-standing start, a rolling start, would have ended up in the same result, because by that time we were all one by one," Sainz said. "So I don't think it would have changed much. It's an unfortunate situation with a lot of water in only one corner."

It therefore came down to the drivers’ own judgement, with Lawson stressing that he deliberately left more margin – considerably more than Verstappen, who was running ahead of him.

"It was just impossible. The whole first half of the lap was dry and then the last few corners were completely soaked. So, it was really easy to do that [what Max has done] when you have this much power on a slick tyre," he said.

"I really lifted out of it because honestly I had no confidence in how much grip we were going to have there and I think Max was probably trying to get closer and make an overtake, and just lost it."

Verstappen himself, however, did not want to blame any external factors and stressed that he had simply made a mistake.

Sports.title: Hamilton explains Dutch GP radio outburst over Ferrari team orders
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has urged Ferrari to be more like Mercedes with its efficiency after growing frustrated by a lack of team orders during the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix.

The Ferrari driver finished fourth in an action-packed contest at Zandvoort on Sunday, with his mid-race battle with stablemate Charles Leclerc arguably being Hamilton’s defining period.

Hamilton had just overtaken McLaren’s Oscar Piastri for fifth on lap 35 and was right behind a much slower Leclerc, so was therefore angling for team orders but they did not arrive.

“Great way of wasting time guys, good job,” complained a sarcastic Hamilton, who eventually took fourth when Leclerc pitted on lap 43 to end a very drawn-out process.

That is compared to Mercedes which swapped its cars with seven laps remaining, as George Russell gave second to Kimi Antonelli, who had fresher tyres so could attack Lando Norris.

Although the McLaren driver still took victory, it was a decision both Antonelli and Russell agreed with as they completed the podium ahead of Hamilton and fifth-placed Leclerc.

“I want to win,” Hamilton told F1 TV. “I want to win. I'm here to win and it is difficult when you're looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it's done - they execute straight away.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“They let Kimi by and let him get on with the race. I was on a different strategy. It's not the same here and that's a little bit difficult, but we just have to take it.

“We'll take it offline, and when I go back now, I'll speak to them about it.”

Russell did well to take third though, as he feared that Mercedes had “lost a double podium”, because by letting Antonelli by, it put him under instant pressure from Hamilton.

The Mercedes driver held firm though, helped by the lap 70 virtual safety car for debris at Turn 5, and Hamilton reckons the earlier fiasco harmed his chances of overtaking his former team-mate.

When asked by Motorsport.com if the VSC stopped him from getting a podium, the seven-time world champion replied: “It felt like it was the closest opportunity I had.

“I think I'd come out of [Turn] 14 pretty close to him and I was just opening SM [Straight Line Mode] and just getting on the boost.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Michael Potts / LAT Images via Getty Images

“I don't know whether or not we would have got by because the Mercedes is just so quick. You saw the McLaren fly past just on power. We're losing like four tenths of a lap here just on straight lines.

“So that was a challenge, but I do think the time was lost when I was behind Charles, which ultimately meant I had a bigger distance to cover to try and catch up with George at the end.”

The result leaves Hamilton tied with Russell in second and 59 points behind Antonelli with 11 rounds remaining, a run where the Ferrari driver is hoping to add to his Barcelona victory.

But to do so Hamilton thinks the Italian marque must reduce its engine power deficit to Mercedes, despite various chassis upgrades it brought to the Netherlands.

“The one thing I'm definitely really proud of the team, they brought an upgrade here this weekend,” the 41-year-old added.

“We are getting closer to them but half the season we've been down in power. We really need to pick up the power if we're going to be anywhere near trying to fight for them and closing the gap to them.”

Sports.title: What caused Verstappen’s F1 Dutch GP crash
Sports.content:
Making mistakes may be uncharacteristic of Max Verstappen, but that’s exactly what the four-time world champion did on the first lap of his home Formula 1 race.

Starting the Dutch Grand Prix from seventh on the grid after feeling unwell all weekend, Verstappen took a decent getaway but found himself squeezed on the grass in a four-wide moment on the run to Turn 1. He was consequently challenged by Red Bull stand-in Liam Lawson in the following corners – which he didn’t mind: “We are allowed to race, so I think that's normal.”

Verstappen eventually held on to that seventh position, but a rain shower which occurred some 50 minutes before the start had dampened the track, and two drivers lost control in the banked final corner on lap one.

While Gabriel Bortoleto escaped from a 360-degree pirouette unscathed, Red Bull’s superstar couldn’t catch the RB22 and suffered a substantial crash, which caused a red flag.

“I think the start is just a consequence of what is happening on the right. It's OK, it can happen,” Verstappen commented regarding about the incident at lights out.

“Then, yeah, I got caught out. It was still quite wet in that corner, and as soon as I saw the dry patch coming, I was like, ‘Now you can accelerate’, but clearly that didn't work. So probably it was still a bit too early.”

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Photo by: Eric Le Galliot

Verstappen described the impact as “a decent hit” but clarified he’d “had worse”.

Red Bull eventually endured its worst grand prix since the April break results-wise, with Lawson its top car in seventh.

Verstappen did admit to “a disappointing weekend” in terms of pace as McLaren, Ferrari and Mercedes were out of reach, but this situation was no surprise to him.

“I wish for more, but you need to be realistic this season,” the Red Bull racer insisted. “We are the fourth-fastest team, so it's not like walking up to Zandvoort and suddenly we can do some magic things.

“It's just how it is, other teams have brought upgrades, we haven't. When you're already on the back foot, it puts you even more on the back foot. So, there's nothing surprising, it's just the reality that we live in.”

So Verstappen will now focus on resting ahead of the Italian Grand Prix, two weeks from now: “I've just not been feeling well. I'm just looking forward to a break where I can just recover also, because I really didn't feel good.”

Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP: Norris overhauls Antonelli for victory, Verstappen suffers heavy crash
Sports.content:
Formula 1 world champion Lando Norris produced a mega drive to win the Dutch Grand Prix from pole while home hero Max Verstappen caused a red flag by crashing out.

The McLaren driver crossed the line 11.5s ahead of runner-up Kimi Antonelli, with his Mercedes team-mate George Russell completing the podium at Zandvoort.

It came after Norris pipped sprint winner Russell for pole ahead of third-placed Antonelli and they all, like the rest of the grid, started on slicks despite rain an hour before lights out.

But the rain was on and off causing a wet-dry surface, the dangers of which emerged at the end of the opening lap once Norris had a perfect getaway while Antonelli overtook Russell at Turn 1.

That’s because Verstappen dipped a tyre onto the white line on the inside of the final corner, causing the Red Bull driver to spin into the barrier which spread debris on the circuit.

“Yeah that’s it - sorry!,” said the Dutchman via team radio, having brought out the red flag just as Gabriel Bortoleto also had a 360-degree spin at the banking but somehow avoided damage.

So another standing start followed - after Oliver Bearman suffered an engine failure on the formation tour - and much to Norris’ dismay this time, as Antonelli squeezed by at Turn 1 for the lead.

Start action Photo by: Clive Rose / Getty Images

That was despite softs on the McLaren compared to mediums for Antonelli, who essentially had a double delight as title rival Russell lost third to hard runner Oscar Piastri at Turn 7.

Russell just didn’t have the pace, soon being pressurised by Charles Leclerc as he reported balance problems, but the tight track allowed him to hold firm before swapping mediums for hards on lap 18.

McLaren responded the previous lap with Piastri, but this backfired as a slow 5.4s stop put him behind Russell just as Antonelli had streaked 2.2s clear of Norris out front.

That gap closed to a second once the pit window - where all the frontrunners chose hard tyres bar Leclerc on mediums - had passed, yet the reigning champion struggled to make inroads.

The wheel-to-wheel battles were more prevalent lower down: Yuki Tsunoda came out on top in a mega multi-car fight for the top 10, while Leclerc was constantly on Piastri’s tail.

That little battle finally ended on lap 34 when the Ferrari and McLaren went through the opening corners wheel-to-wheel, only for Leclerc to edge by for fourth around the outside of Turn 3.

There was yet more misery for Piastri as he was overtaken for fifth at Turn 1 on the following tour by Lewis Hamilton, who quickly closed in on team-mate Leclerc.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

The seven-time world champion was angling for team orders but they did not arrive and Hamilton sarcastically told his Ferrari squad: “Great way of wasting time guys, good job!”

Hamilton eventually moved by though once Leclerc made his second pitstop on lap 43, two tours after the Mercedes duo, and five before Norris came in for another set of hard tyres.

But Ferrari kept Hamilton out which left him with first on track, yet the battle for the net lead emerged behind as Norris rapidly closed on Antonelli, who complained about his rear Pirellis.

So come lap 54 Hamilton, Antonelli and Norris were all within a second and the reigning world champion made a sweeping move on Antonelli around the outside of Turn 1.

It was that same lap that Norris subsequently took the actual lead at Turn 11 from Hamilton, who dropped behind Antonelli at Turn 1 the following lap - just as Esteban Ocon caused a virtual safety car by stopping at Turn 4.

“Are you using me as a guinea pig,” complained Hamilton, wanting to pit, and that he finally did under the VSC by taking softs - likewise for Antonelli, while Norris and now second-placed Russell stayed out on hard rubber.

Norris admitted he was “worried” by that decision and had reasons to be so, as the advantage of the fresher tyre became evident with Antonelli quickly reducing his gap to Russell.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

Mercedes eventually told the Briton to let his team-mate by with the swap occurring at Turn 1 on lap 65, but this left Russell vulnerable against Hamilton, claiming “we’ve lost a double podium”.

But Russell held firm, helped by a brief VSC on lap 70 for debris at Turn 5, to take the final podium spot, 4.3s behind Antonelli and 15.8s off Norris who took his second win of 2026.

Hamilton finished fourth, Leclerc took fifth and Piastri was sixth, while Red Bull stand-in Liam Lawson, Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg, Aston Martin’s Fernando Alonso and Alpine’s Pierre Gasly respectively completed the top 10.

The result has extended Antonelli’s championship advantage, as the 19-year-old leaves the Netherlands with a 59-point lead over both Russell and Hamilton in second.

Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP red-flagged after Verstappen crash
Sports.content:
Formula 1's Dutch Grand Prix has been red-flagged after one lap following an enormous accident for home hero Max Verstappen.

At the end of lap 1 on a damp circuit, Verstappen lost control of his Red Bull as he tagged the white line on the inside of Zandvoort's final turn - the banked, flat out Luyendyk corner leading onto the main straight.

Verstappen veered head on into the outside wall, before his car crossed the track and came to a standstill on the inside.

The Dutchman soon reported he was OK and apologised to his team for ending his race early.

Verstappen was fortunate not to be collected by any other cars, with Alpine's Pierre Gasly taking avoiding action, while in the background Audi's Nico Hulkenberg also narrowly avoided a huge accident as his team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto spun in front of him.

Under the red flag all drivers gathered in the pitlane awaiting the restart. They were having to navigate a field of debris before pit entry, but teams are allowed to change tyres under a red flag ahead of the restart. That restart is expected at 15:33 local time.

Max Verstappen Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

At the time Verstappen was running seventh after a disappointing qualifying session. Polesitter Lando Norris retained his lead during a chaotic start sequence, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli passing George Russell for second.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc gaining two positions to hold down fourth ahead of the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri and team-mate Lewis Hamilton.

For Verstappen, the accident marks an unfortunate end to a six-year spell racing on home soil, winning the first three editions of the Dutch Grand prix revival in 2021, 2022 and 2023. The race will disappear from the calendar after organisers decided not to pursue a contract renewal with F1 management.

Earlier in the week, the four-time world champion announced he had extended his Red Bull contract until the end of the 2030 season.

Sports.title: Stroll demanded penalties after Bearman and Bortoleto passed red pit exit light | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lance Stroll urged race control to penalise two of his rivals for leaving the pit lane while a red light was shown during the Dutch Grand Prix.

The incident occured as the field left the pits when the race resumed following the stoppage caused by Max Verstappen’s crash.

The pit lane exit lights were green as the field began to leave the pits. However after Fernando Alonso passed by the signal changed to a flashing red light.

Oliver Bearman and Gabriel Bortoleto both drove past the flashing red light. Neither acknowledged the pit lane exit had been closed and continued to the grid, though Bearman suffered a power unit failure before he got there.

Stroll, who was following the pair, noticed the light had changed and alerted his race engineer Gary Gannon:

Stroll The lights red, huh? Light’s red. Gannon Checking, I’m checking. Stroll I’m not going unless it’s green. Gannon Yeah, understood Lance. Stroll 10 seconds later

Tell me if I can go or not. Gannon Waiting to hear back from the FIA.

The signal changes to green and Stroll leaves the pit exit

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

He repeatedly called for the drivers who had passed the red signal to be penalised. Stroll correctly noted that Formula 1’s penalty guidelines state drivers who pass a red light at the pit lane exit during a race should receive 10-second stop-and-go penalties:

Stroll So everybody that went under a red should get a penalty. Gannon Yep, yep. Stroll Stop and go. Gannon Understood, we’ll report it. So the back of the pack… Stroll It’s the rules. Gannon …the back of the pack is in nine, so you can build temp. Good pushing to build temp

Stroll appeared to be under the impression that many more drivers than just the two immediately in front of him had driven past the red signal:

Stroll It’s clear that everyone went under red, then they all should get a penalty. Gannon We’re checking it now. Stroll Stop and go. Gannon Yeah, we’re checking now. Stroll Everybody. Gannon It started out green and then it went red and we’re checking who went through red and reporting it ASAP. Absolutely Lance.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The Aston Martin driver continued to press his case on the formation lap, even when his race engineer was trying to warn him about Bearman’s stoppage ahead:

Gannon ‘Bearman is slow between 10-11. Yellow ahead for Bearman stopped. Bearman stopped between 10-11. Watch for Bearman… Stroll Those are the rules. Gannon …there, watch for Bearmen. Stroll The rules are: it’s red… Gannon Lance, we’ve reported it, we reported it. Now let’s get focused getting around to the grid, okay? We’ve reported and they will action it.

However the stewards chose instead to only reprimand the pair, pointing out that the incident occured before the race resumption and neither had gained an advantage.

“The pit exit light turned red when the driver was approaching the pit exit to join the track for the re-start of the race after a suspension,” they noted. “Such an infringement happening during the race normally requires a very significant penalty as the drivers are obliged to obey light signals at all times. However, in this case the infringement did not happen during a live race, but rather on the build-up before the re-start, although the race had technically already resumed in accordance with Article B5.15.2g.

“In addition to that, the stewards acknowledge that neither any advantage was gained nor any potentially dangerous or unsafe situation was created. Therefore a reprimand to the driver is deemed appropriate given the mitigating circumstances and the unique scenario.”

Sports.title: Mercedes is “clearly not the fastest car on the grid any more” claims Antonelli | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes are no longer the team to beat in Formula 1 claimed Andrea Kimi Antonelli after McLaren’s second consecutive victory in the Dutch Grand Prix.

Lando Norris passed Antonelli on his way to victory in yesterday’s race at Zandvoort, as he did in the previous round in Hungary.

“For sure, we’re clearly not the fastest car anymore on the grid,” said Antonelli, who holds a 59-point lead in the drivers’ championship. “We’re probably second or third, at least in today’s race, and McLaren has taken a huge step, especially since Hungary, since the big upgrade package they brought.”

However Antonelli has high hopes for Mercedes’ forthcoming upgrade for its W17. “The team has been working super-hard on this next package that is coming up and they just want to make sure that it’s going to work out well once we put it on,” he said.

“So for sure, in this race, it’s going to be more difficult, it’s going to be challenging, but we’re ready to do our best and to maximise every opportunity. And then hopefully it’s going to be our turn to bring the package that’s going to give us a little bit of the upper hand again.”

Antonelli’s team mate George Russell believes McLaren’s strength in the last two races has been partly due to the similarities in the track layouts.

“I don’t think it’s a major surprise for us, seeing how competitive Lando was this weekend, considering he won in Budapest,” he said. “It’s a very similar circuit with the long corners, high tyre degradation, with the two-stop strategy, so there’s a lot of similarities between the two circuits.

“I think this may continue for the coming two or three races until we start to bring more to the car, and fingers crossed our competitors don’t.”

He expects Mercedes will be “slightly more competitive” in the next race at Monza, the fastest circuit on the calendar. “However, I believe Ferrari have an engine upgrade incoming, and the truth is we just don’t know.

“But I do believe that these high-degradation circuits really suit McLaren very well, and especially Lando. He’s always been a bit of a specialist in those conditions. We also saw it last year. Monza may be slightly different, but I think they are the team to beat right now.”

Sports.title: Russell defends “fair” decision to let Antonelli into second place | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell said letting his team mate and championship rival overtake him was the correct decision which minimised the risk to their races.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli ran ahead of Russell until he made an extra pit stop during a late Virtual Safety Car period. When Antonelli closed on Russell afterwards, Mercedes ordered the pair to swap positions.

Russell complied, though it handed Antonelli a six-point swing in the championship fight between the pair of them. That erased the gain Russell made in the previous day’s sprint race.

However Russell said letting his team mate by was the correct thing to do for Mercedes.

“We’ve always said as a team, when we’re on different strategies, we’re never going to fight and we’re always going to invert, and that’s always just been our rules,” he explained.

“The fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC and he tried something different to protect us as a team. He kind of copy-pasted what the Ferraris did.”

Although Russell believes there was a chance he could have successfully defended his position from Antonelli – as he later did with Lewis Hamilton, thanks partly to the timing of another VSC period – he also said trying to defend could have compromised his race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Could I have kept him behind? Maybe. But equally it could have been a P5 as well. So, in the end, you know, he deserved to be P2. I think P3 was a fair result for me.”

Russell fell behind Antonelli at the start of the race, then got stuck behind Oscar Piastri and never managed to get back on terms with his team mate. “It was tough,” he said.

“The first VSC came at a pretty awkward timing for me because I felt really strong on the hard [tyre]. I think Kimi’s and my race was kind of the opposite. I had a tough medium stint, he had a very strong medium stint, then I had a strong hard stint, he was struggling.

“But that VSC gave Lewis a free pit stop and obviously Kimi pitted as well. And from there on in, I knew I was going to be under threat.

“I was managing enough in the high-speed corners to allow me to be fast in sector three and defending into turn one [Tarzan]. So I was pleased with that performance.”

Sports.title: Antonelli says extra pit stop “put George at risk” too | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli was not convinced his extra pit stop in the Dutch Grand Prix was the right decision as it risked compromising his race.

The Mercedes driver made an extra pit stop 16 laps from the end of the race, taking advantage of a late Virtual Safety Car period. It dropped him from second place to third behind his team mate George Russell

Antonelli was able to repass his team mate for second place after Mercedes ordered Russell to let him through. However Antonelli was unable to gain on race leader Lando Norris.

Afterwards Antonelli said the strategy call had unnecessarily risked both their races, even though he had been struggling on his previous set of tyres.

“It was a difficult second half for me, especially in the last stint on the hards,” he said. “I was just really struggling. I had little confidence in the car and it was not easy.

“Then obviously we pitted [under the VSC] and also that was a bit tricky. But then also George, I have to thank him because he made my life a lot easier.

“But I still think probably we could have stayed out and gone until the end with the same set [of tyres] because it put us a little bit at risk. Also, I feel we put George at risk with having to let me by and everything.”

Although he led most of the race, Antonelli said he was unlikely to win it. “I still think, at the end of the day, it was a great team execution with how things were,” he said. “”I think today [second place] was the maximum we could have done because the pace of the McLarens, especially in the second half, was just too strong.”

“It was a good ending of a difficult weekend for me where I struggled with the feeling of the car, did a lot of mistakes on my side – sprint quali, quali, also in today’s race with Lando I could have defended a bit better,” he added. “So for sure there were things that I didn’t do well this weekend, and for sure the feeling wasn’t as good.”

Sports.title: “We weren’t unlucky”: Hamilton tells Ferrari their tactics cost him third place | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton told Ferrari they cost him a chance to finish third by failing to use team orders during the Dutch Grand Prix.

He finished fourth behind George Russell after losing time earlier in the race when he caught team mate Charles Leclerc. Hamilton repeatedly urged Ferrari to tell Leclerc to let him through, but the team instead to chose wait a lap and then bring the leading Ferrari into the pits.

“Let’s not hold ourselves up from an potentially better result,” Hamilton told the team when he caught Leclerc.

After spending a lap behind Leclerc, Hamilton warned Ferrari “we’re just losing time.” Once Leclerc came in, Hamilton sarcastically remarked: “Big waste of time guys, good job.”

Hamilton’s attempt to pass Russell at the end of the race was thwarted when the Virtual Safety Car was deployed. After he finished fourth race engineer Carlos Santi told Hamilton: “Thank you Lewis, was a bit unlucky with Russell.”

“We weren’t unlucky,” Hamilton replied, “we lost time earlier on and that cost us P3.”

“We can discuss it offline,” he added.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hamilton explained his frustration after the race, pointing out Mercedes did not hesitate to swap the order of their two drivers when it benefitted them overall.

“I want to win,” said Hamilton. “I’m here to win and it is difficult when you’re looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it’s done and they execute straight away.

“They let Kimi by and let him get on with the race. I was on a different strategy and it was not the same here.

“That’s a little bit difficult but we just have to take it, we’ll take it off line. When I go back now, I’ll speak to them about it.”

Sports.title: Moses Itauma’s Record Chase Cannot Sell Hrgovic PPV
Sports.content:
Mentioning Tyson invites attention that does Itauma no favors. Tyson was already must-see television before defeating Berbick in 1986 because of the way he destroyed opponents. He pressed forward, stayed in the pocket, threw combinations, and kept attacking until the fight was over. Itauma is not that type of heavyweight. He fights on the outside, waiting to launch one shot rather than remaining close and overwhelming opponents with power shots. When opponents pressure him, he tends to retreat to escape. It’s a style that looks like a bigger version of Shakur Stevenson.

That approach may be effective, but it is not guaranteed to turn him into a pay-per-view attraction. Fans watching Tyson knew they would see aggression and violence.

His personality doesn’t make up for what he lacks in the excitement department. Itauma looks half-asleep during interviews and brings low energy to the promotion. He comes across as dull rather than as a young heavyweight eager to take over the division.

Patterson also won a vacant heavyweight championship, defeating Archie Moore after Rocky Marciano retired. Itauma would not be breaking new ground by taking an available title. He would simply be doing it two months younger than Patterson.

The more revealing contrast remains Tyson. Berbick held the WBC belt when Tyson destroyed him in the ring. Itauma received his opportunity after Oleksandr Usyk relinquished the IBF title and Frank Sanchez agreed to step aside.

Winning would make Itauma an IBF champion, but the promotional campaign is using their ages to connect two fighters whose appeal and championship victories bear little resemblance.

Queensberry also waited too long to present Hrgovic as dangerous. A few interviews during fight week cannot transform him into a marquee name. Daniel Dubois would have brought greater attention from fans, punching power, and a real British rivalry.

The age statistic is being asked to create interest that the matchup, undercard, and promotion have failed to produce. Casual fans do not purchase pay-per-views to watch someone move ahead of Patterson on a list. Their money goes toward fighters and rivalries they already care about.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Takes Credit For Zepeda, Teofimo Title Wins
Sports.content:
His loss was not as one-sided as the official scores of 118-110, 118-110, and 119-109 suggested. Stevenson landed 295 of 565 punches, compared with Zepeda’s 272 of 979. Shakur was far more accurate, connecting at approximately 52% against Zepeda’s 28%, but only 23 landed punches separated them across 12 rounds.

A later victory over Lamont Roach Jr. gave Zepeda the WBC lightweight title that Stevenson previously held. It was his first full world championship, but he had already reached interim title status before meeting Shakur.

What was interesting is how Shakur handled it publicly. Before Zepeda fought Lamont Roach Jr, Shakur openly predicted Roach would dish out a beating. Once Zepeda walked away with the full WBC lightweight title, Shakur immediately flipped his tune to build up his own credentials.

By comparison, Lopez had a much stronger championship history. He defeated Vasiliy Lomachenko at lightweight and Josh Taylor at light welterweight before surrendering his WBO 140-pound belt to Stevenson in January. Saturday’s majority-decision victory over Rolando Romero made Teofimo a three-division champion.

Those latest wins add value to Shakur’s record because they confirm that Zepeda and Lopez continued operating at the championship level. Stevenson deserves credit for beating them, especially his dominant performance against Teofimo at Madison Square Garden.

However, the WBC title came to Zepeda through his victory over Roach, while Lopez moved to welterweight and took Romero’s WBA belt.

At most, Shakur can use those wins as proof that he defeated quality opposition. He cannot take partial ownership of championships that Zepeda and Teofimo won through their own performances.

Sports.title: Keith Connolly Says Teofimo Lopez May Delay Jack Catterall
Sports.content:
Allowing Teofimo to take that fight first would only weaken Catterall’s position. Lopez could earn the enormous payday, lose the title in the process, or move toward another opponent, leaving Catterall waiting without any guarantee that his opportunity would retain the same value. His better business decision is to demand the Lopez fight next and pursue the Garcia–Benn winner afterward.

Jack Catterall Blocks Teofimo Lopez’s Three-Unification Plan

Jack Catterall says Teofimo Lopez does not have the freedom to select another opponent after capturing the WBA “Super” welterweight title from Rolando Romero on Saturday night.

When Ring Magazine asked who Teofimo should fight next following his majority-decision win, Catterall responded that the WBA had already provided the answer through its 180-day directive.

“180 days @WBABoxing which means November ✅ I understand the politics of boxing better than most. Rolly had a voluntary; now it’s time for my shot! No ducks, no more swerving. Me v Teo next,” said Catterall on X.

His message also answered Teofimo’s intention to pursue three consecutive unification matches without making a mandatory defense. Such a schedule would leave no room for Catterall and require the WBA to ignore or alter its previous ruling.

Romero was elevated to Super champion before Catterall defeated Shakhram Giyasov for the WBA’s secondary welterweight title on May 23. The WBA ordered the Super champion to face the winner within a maximum of 180 days, placing the deadline in November.

One voluntary defense has already been granted. Romero used it against Teofimo rather than facing Catterall, and the British southpaw does not believe the new champion should receive another exception.

A fight with the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn is Teofimo’s preferred next step, and he has discussed collecting the remaining welterweight belts. Those matches involve more money than a Catterall defense, which explains his preference. Still, taking Romero’s belt also meant inheriting the obligation attached to it.

This is not merely a request for consideration. Catterall holds the secondary belt and has a WBA directive supporting his demand. If the organization enforces its own ruling, three straight unification fights will have to wait.

Teofimo Lopez Wants Three Unifications Without Facing One Mandatory

Teofimo Lopez believes his DAZN contract will take him directly from one welterweight unification to another without stopping for a mandatory defense of his WBA title.

The newly crowned champion is targeting Liam Paro, the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn, and eventually Devin Haney. If Lopez gets his way, every appearance during the rest of his deal will involve another champion.

During his post-fight press conference, Lopez said:

“I got three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title. We’re not taking no title defense, no nothing. Whoever’s next, we’re going for him.”

A unification technically includes a defense of the belts involved, but Lopez’s meaning was clear. He does not plan to face an ordinary mandatory or ranked challenger between attempts to collect the other titles. If that plan proceeds, it will consume well over a year. Each fight requires negotiations between promoters, networks and boxing organizations before the participants complete training camps and recover afterward. Lopez also left the Romero fight with a cut over his right eyebrow that may delay his return.

The first unification depends on another event. Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn are scheduled to fight on September 12, after which the winner will need time to recover and negotiate with Lopez. The next stage against Liam Paro or Devin Haney requires another lengthy round of discussions.

Completing all three fights may leave contenders in several organizations waiting 12 to 18 months. Some will be forced into additional bouts to protect their rankings while the champion moves from one financially attractive unification to another.

Unifications often receive priority because reducing the number of champions is supposed to benefit boxing. That principle becomes difficult to defend when it is used repeatedly to prevent every other challenger from receiving an opportunity.

Granting one exception for a major fight is understandable. Three consecutive exceptions create a separate set of rules for the boxer who generates the most money. Ranked contenders must keep winning while Teofimo remains protected from facing any of them.

The strategy also depends on Lopez winning every fight. A loss transfers the collected titles to another champion, who may then request additional exceptions for more lucrative bouts. The waiting challengers must begin the same process again with someone new.

The schedule Teofimo described requires approval from more than DAZN. The WBA and the other organizations must authorize each step. If they permit three straight unifications without requiring a mandatory defense, the “road to undisputed” will become another example of boxing’s business interests overriding its competitive structure.

Sports.title: Mannix: Jaron Ennis vs. Josh Kelly Talks Are Advanced
Sports.content:
“Boots is chomping at the bit to get back in the ring, and I’m told there are advanced negotiations for Jaron Ennis to face Josh Kelly in a unification fight sometime in November or December,” Mannix said during DAZN’s Sources Say. “Josh Kelly, coming off a win this past month, had some injury issues after that fight. He had a nose injury, but Matchroom, Boots’ team, believes that injury will be healed. I’m told they are targeting that fight on the East Coast before the end of this year.”

If Kelly were a stronger champion, he might be able to make several defenses and earn money from the IBF title before pursuing a unification. His July 25 showing against Caoimhin Agyarko demonstrated why waiting would carry considerable risk.

Heavy punishment left Kelly with a badly damaged nose as he squeezed out a narrow 12-round unanimous decision in Jeddah. Agyarko is ranked No. 15 by the IBF, yet Kelly struggled to keep him under control.

Higher in the IBF rankings are Brandon Adams, former champion Bakhram Murtazaliev, Nikita Tszyu, Israil Madrimov, Ben Mahoney, Xander Zayas, Milan Prat, Giovani Santillan, Yan Marcos, Pavel Sosulin, Ibrahima Diallo, and Bilal Fawaz. Kelly would have a difficult time holding the belt for long against that group.

His title-winning victory over Murtazaliev in Newcastle was also viewed by many as a hometown gift. Kelly stayed mobile rather than engage for long. Near the end of rounds, he used quick shoeshine combinations to impress the judges. Murtazaliev landed the heavier punches and dropped Kelly in the ninth, yet lost on two cards.

Ennis presents a far more severe test. The WBA and WBO champion has more speed, power, combination punching, and offensive variety. The difference is wide enough that placing the fight in Newcastle probably would not change the outcome.

That nose injury may be the greatest immediate concern. If it breaks down during sparring, the unification may have to be postponed. Assuming Kelly gets through camp, taking the Ennis fight now makes more financial sense than continuing with lower-paying title defenses.

Sports.title: Regis Prograis Calls Rocky Marciano Overrated
Sports.content:
“For me, I think Rocky Marciano was overrated,” Prograis said on social media. “He retired undefeated, right? But in this book, I bought this book about Sonny Liston. It said right here about Rocky Marciano that ‘his good fortune was to rise to prominence at a time when his major competitors were either old, like 37-year-old Joe Louis.’ He was 37 when he fought him. Joe Walcott was 37 years old. A natural light heavyweight like Ezzard Charles was 34 years old, and then Archie Moore was 41 at the time.”

The overall point has some merit, but several ages quoted by Prograis are inaccurate. Louis was 37, but Walcott was 38 when Marciano took his heavyweight title in September 1952. Charles was 32 in their first fight and turned 33 before the rematch, not 34. Moore’s birth year remains disputed, leaving him either 38 or 41 when he challenged Marciano in 1955.

Prograis also accused Marciano of avoiding 6-foot-3 Cuban contender Nino Valdes because of his size.

“They had a Cuban fighter called Nino Valdes, and he didn’t want to fight him,” Prograis said. “He said he was too big. So I know a lot of older guys say that Rocky Marciano was this and undefeated this. But I feel Rocky Marciano was overrated at the time.”

Valdes had a legitimate case after rising to the top of the heavyweight rankings, but saying Marciano simply refused to face him leaves out part of the story.

The Cuban lost a 15-round title eliminator to Moore in May 1955. Marciano then met Moore four months later and stopped him in the ninth round. Valdes also suffered numerous defeats during Marciano’s championship reign, making the claim that he was deliberately avoided difficult to prove.

Marciano’s leading opponents were older, and his era lacked the talent found in later generations. Still, Walcott, Charles, and Moore remained dangerous elite fighters. Those victories do not settle every historical argument, but dismissing his entire career as fortunate goes too far.

Sports.title: Rick Glaser Tattles on Eddie Hearn to Turki
Sports.content:
“Turki Alalshikh, you have a great event in the deep planning stage for November 20 on Netflix at the Mecca of Boxing Madison Square Garden in New York And as you know, Eddie Hearn is attempting to undermine your great event,” said Glaser on X. “Whatever Hearn’s reasons may be, personal gain, or other motives, it’s causing havoc in Boxing circles, & the sporting public, especially with Hearn saying on video’s “I don’t care who this upsets” as he mouths off. “Turki Alalshikh, you deserve much better than you are receiving from Hearn in his lack of respect. Best regards from Sonya & I.”

The sign-off completes the effect. Having reported Hearn’s alleged misconduct and lavished Turki with praise, Glaser closes the message as though he were sending a polite letter to a school principal.

Nothing in the post proves that Hearn is trying to damage the event for “personal gain” or any other hidden motive. He represents Anthony Joshua, who signed for the fight to take place at a UK stadium. Joshua prefers Wembley, while Turki and Tyson Fury favor New York.

As Joshua’s promoter, Hearn is supposed to argue his position, even when it clashes with Turki’s plans. That does not automatically make him disloyal or disrespectful.

The message presents the dispute as something more serious. In Glaser’s version, Hearn is creating chaos, sabotaging Turki’s work, and failing to show proper gratitude toward the man financing the event. It is an extraordinary display of public loyalty. Glaser did everything except ask Turki to send Hearn to the headmaster’s office.

Sports.title: Julio Cesar Chavez Broke Edwin Rosario Piece By Piece
Sports.content:
Rosario presented the kind of danger Chavez had not encountered. The WBA champion had knocked out Livingstone Bramble in two rounds the previous year and possessed genuine power in both hands. He also attacked Chavez’s opposition before the bout, dismissing many of his previous opponents as “guys right out of the bar.”

Rosario Could Not Keep Chavez Away

Any doubts about Chavez at lightweight disappeared quickly. Rather than feeling his way into the contest, the 25-year-old Mexican closed the distance and began digging hooks into Rosario’s body.

Rosario had success during the third and fourth rounds. He landed several hard punches and briefly forced Chavez onto the ropes, but nothing discouraged the advancing challenger. Chavez absorbed Rosario’s best shots, turned him, and reclaimed control with short combinations. Once the bout moved into close range, the difference became brutal. Chavez did not simply walk forward and throw punches. He slipped Rosario’s right hand, blocked shots with his elbows and gloves, then answered before the Puerto Rican champion could reset.

The body attack gradually robbed Rosario of his movement and power. Chavez mixed hooks downstairs with uppercuts and straight rights to the head, rarely wasting a punch. HBO’s PunchStat count credited him with landing 450 of 743 punches, an extraordinary 61 percent. Rosario connected with 263 of 731.

A Beating That Lasted Too Long

By the later rounds, Rosario’s left eye was swollen shut, his face was cut, and blood covered his nose and mouth. Still, he refused to go down. His courage allowed the punishment to continue far longer than it should have.

Chavez looked almost untouched as he drove Rosario into a corner during the 11th. With the champion taking another sustained attack, his corner threw in the towel. Referee Richard Steele stopped it at 2:38. All three judges had Chavez far in front: 98-92, 99-91, and 100-92.

The performance made Chavez a two-division champion and erased every question surrounding his move to lightweight. He had taken one of boxing’s most feared punchers, neutralized his power, and broken him down without ever needing a knockdown. Rosario brought danger into the ring that night, but Chavez made it disappear.

Sports.title: Teofimo Defeats Rolly, Now He Has His Eyes Set On Undisputed
Sports.content:
During the first three rounds of the world title bout, Lopez was in control as he used his jab and touched the body of Romero. Late in the fourth round, Romero landed a check left hook that knocked Lopez off balance.

In the fifth round, Rolly got more aggressive, and as a result, he landed a big left hook that produced a cut over Teofimo’s right eye.

Seconds later, Romero connected with a vicious overhand right that buckled Lopez’s knees.

Romero followed the big right hand with a flurry of shots, but Lopez was able to survive the round. Lopez bounced back in the sixth as he returned to his game plan of working off the jab and attacking the body.

Lopez continued to apply intelligent pressure in the seventh as he landed a solid right hand. As round seven was coming to a close, Romero caught Lopez with a powerful check left hook.

For the remainder of the WBA welterweight title bout, Teofimo Lopez fought a smart and very disciplined fight. Despite the low punch output, Rolly had the more eye-catching shots, but Teofimo outworked him and won by majority decision.

With the victory, Teofimo “The Takeover” Lopez (23-2, 13 KOs) became a three-division world champion. As soon as Lopez was announced as the winner, the boxing community was seeking the answer to the proverbial question: What’s next?

During the post-fight press conference, Teofimo Lopez spoke about his future and the path he plans to travel in his boxing journey.

“I think I’m here, this is the road to undisputed, you know what I’m saying? I’m here to reclaim and collect all of the next world titles, and whoever the next champion is, that’s what it’s all about.”

Teofimo Lopez went on to say, “Honestly, I got four fights with, well now three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title.”

Currently, the world champions in the welterweight division are Teofimo Lopez (WBA), Devin Haney (WBO), Ryan Garcia (WBC), and Liam Paro (IBF). In his quest to become undisputed, the first step for Lopez is to become a unified world champion.

If Lopez wants what looks like the softer touch, a unification bout with IBF champion Liam Paro may be next. If Lopez wants a fight that is going to be a big event, then he may want to pursue a bout with the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s gold-driven growth model is unsustainable – Prof Bokpin
Ghana News.content:
We are sacrificing long-term survival for short-term praise – Prof Bokpin

Economist Professor Godfred Bokpin has criticised Ghana’s growing reliance on gold as a key driver of economic stability, warning that the country risks sacrificing its long-term survival for short-term economic gains.

Speaking on the Joy FM Super Morning Show on Monday, August 24, Professor Bokpin said the focus on macroeconomic stability and the benefits of gold had overshadowed the severe environmental damage caused by irresponsible mining.

He warned that Ghana’s current economic gains could quickly be reversed if international gold prices fall sharply, leaving the country vulnerable to another major economic shock.

“Today, we have magnified the effect of the Gold Board to the extent that the discussion about irresponsible mining, the dangers, the existential threat seems infinitesimal in the face of so-called macroeconomic stability, which was just a price shock,” he said.

Professor Bokpin questioned the sustainability of the gains being celebrated, pointing to Ghana’s exposure to fluctuations in global gold prices.

“Look, if gold price today should dip by more than 40%, this macroeconomic stability we talk about will only exist in the textbook. What kind of gain is that?” he asked.

He said a significant decline in gold prices could wipe out the economic gains within months.

“When it's so exposed to price shock, global gold price shock, what kind of gain is that? Everything could just go within six to eight months of that price shock,” Professor Bokpin warned.

He urged policymakers to learn from historical commodity cycles, noting that commodity prices have repeatedly experienced sharp corrections after periods of strong growth.

“Literally every 10 years, prices of commodities correct from a bust, from a boom; they correct almost every 10 years,” he said.

According to Professor Bokpin, Ghana must therefore subject its gold-driven economic strategy to rigorous sensitivity analysis and stress testing rather than assume that current gains will be sustained.

“Look, if you do sensitivity analysis, if you do stress testing, and you say that if the gold price should dip by 40% today, where would we be? You will see that we'll be so exposed,” he said.

‘We are not better off’

Professor Bokpin said the assessment of Ghana’s gold economy must go beyond foreign exchange earnings, reserves and other macroeconomic indicators to account for the environmental and social costs of mining.

He called for a value-chain approach that properly captures the environmental cost of gold production, particularly the destruction of water bodies and ecosystems.

“As a country, we should adopt a value chain approach. Let's account for the environmental subsidy. Ecological integrity we have destroyed,” he said.

He said Ghana could only claim to be better off if the full economic, social and environmental costs of gold production were incorporated into the analysis.

“If you put all of these things together, through the analysis, and you're able to say that we are far better off, then that's good news. But if you do that, what is the gain? What are we celebrating?” he asked.

When asked whether Ghana was better off after taking these factors into consideration, Professor Bokpin was unequivocal.

“We are not better off.”

He described the decision to tolerate severe environmental damage in pursuit of economic stability as selfish and a failure of leadership.

“It's a selfish position to think that you can cause such harm to the environment and water bodies in the name of macroeconomic stability, and say you have gained,” he said.

“It's a selfish position. This is not leadership. We are sacrificing long-term survivability for short-term praise.”

‘Growth model reliant on environmental destruction is never sustainable’

Professor Bokpin urged Ghana to reconsider an economic model heavily dependent on the extraction and export of primary commodities, particularly where such activities come with high environmental costs.

“This is not leadership. Countries that made it didn't do so by exploiting the environment like this,” he said.

“And any growth model that is heavily reliant on environmental destruction, primary commodities, is never sustainable.”

He cited Malaysia as an example of a country that successfully moved away from an economy heavily dependent on primary commodities.

According to Professor Bokpin, Malaysia once faced a situation similar to Ghana’s current dependence on natural resources but gradually transformed its economy by reducing its reliance on primary commodities.

“What we are discussing today was what was prevailing in the 50s and 70s in Malaysia, when the economy was heavily driven by copper and tin,” he said.

“From the 70s, 80s, 90s, they shifted away from primary commodities, and that is how Malaysia is where they are today.”

He said Ghana must similarly look beyond immediate economic gains and pursue a development strategy capable of creating sustainable prosperity without destroying the country’s natural resources.

‘Is this macroeconomic stability compared to a life?’

Professor Bokpin also questioned whether Ghana’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) adequately captures the damage caused by economic activities such as irresponsible mining.

He noted that while mining contributes to GDP, the environmental destruction and social costs associated with the activity are not adequately reflected in the measure.

“How do we celebrate such a growth model with a huge environmental footprint?” he asked.

He referred to the criticism that GDP can sometimes conceal the social and environmental costs of economic activity.

“That is the reason why so many people think that GDP is not just gross domestic product, but gross domestic problem,” he said.

Professor Bokpin warned that the human cost of irresponsible mining should not be dismissed in the pursuit of economic indicators.

“If one person dies today because of irresponsible mining, we have destroyed the water bodies. Is this macroeconomic stability or gain compared to a life?” he asked.

Ghana News.title: Australian shark attack victim grateful for ‘second chance at life’
Ghana News.content:
An Australian woman bitten by a shark at a popular Sydney beach earlier this year says she has been given a "second chance at life" and will be making the most of it.

Leah Stewart, 34, was mauled by a shark during a morning swim at Coogee Beach in June, suffering multiple bites to her arms and legs, amid a spate of attacks in Australia.

The mother-of-one was placed in an induced coma and had several surgeries, including having one of her arms amputated.

In an online post on Monday, she thanked her supporters who have raised more than AU$550,000 (US$394,000; £289,000) for her, saying her recovery has been "incredibly difficult" but she is making "remarkable" progress.

"After what has been an incredibly difficult few months, I'm so happy that I've progressed enough to build some independence, and I can finally see some light after all of this," Stewart wrote, in her first comments since the attack.

"I want you to know that I feel like I've been given a second chance at life, and I'm not going to waste it."

Stewart said she had been "overwhelmed" by the support from family, friends and "even strangers", adding that the "you've inspired me to get better, not bitter".

An online fundraiser for her would now be closed, she wrote, with the money raised giving her the chance to recover at home as well as "options for further medical treatment down the road".

"I still have a long way to go, but my recovery has been remarkable, and a huge part of that is because of the absolute army of love, support, prayers and encouragement surrounding my family and I from all over the world."

In an interview with Nine Network's 60 Minutes, due to be aired this weekend, Stewart described seeing the shark's "horrific" face.

"I'll never forget its face - it was a monster," she says.

"It was holding onto my leg and I just thought of (my daughter) August, and I thought, 'she's not going to have a mum. She's gonna grow up without a mum'."

Fighting back tears, she goes on: "I couldn't handle that, I didn't want her to not have a mum. I just thought, I've got to fight it, do everything I can to be here."

There have been a spate of shark attacks in Australia this year, with four attacks over a two-day period in January, including one on a 12-year-old boy who later died from his injuries.

In May, a man was killed by a shark in Queensland while spearfishing and in Western Australia, a father-of-two died after he was attacked by a 4m (13ft) shark.

Ghana News.title: Nigerian film star Ogogo dies from cancer aged 66
Ghana News.content:
Nigeria's huge film industry, Nollywood, is in mourning after the death at 66 of veteran actor and star of Yoruba-language cinema Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo.

His daughter, Kira Hassan, confirmed the news during an emotional Instagram live broadcast on Sunday, where she struggled to come to terms with her father's death.

Ogogo, who had been suffering from cancer, is due to be buried on Monday in his hometown in Ogun state, south-west Nigeria, in line with Muslim tradition, according to fellow actor Prince Jide Kosoko.

Colleagues and fans have been paying tribute to a man who became one of Yoruba cinema's most recognisable faces.

Before finding fame on screen, Ogogo worked as a mechanic for about 13 years at the Ogun State Water Corporation.

He combined that career with acting in 1981, when he started appearing in films. He eventually switched to performing full time in 1994 focusing on the profession he loved.

Over the course of his career, Ogogo won numerous awards and earned critical acclaim for his role in the movie Anikulapo, where he played the Alaafin of Oyo - the most revered king in Yorubaland..

Ghana News.title: ‘I just want our football to grow’ – Dede Ayew responds to GFA presidency talk
Ghana News.content:
Andre Ayew

Former Black Stars captain Andre Ayew has hinted at a possible move into football administration, with reports suggesting he is considering a bid for the Ghana Football Association (GFA) presidency.

The 36-year-old, however, stopped short of confirming that he intends to contest the position.

Ayew made the comments on the Obi One Podcast, hosted by former Chelsea midfielder John Mikel Obi, in Accra on Sunday.

“First of all, what the masses want is most important.

“I've heard the rumours about people saying I should lead Ghana football, but that's not what is important; I just want our football to grow,” he said.

“Not tomorrow, but now,” Ayew added.

The next Ghana Football Association (GFA) presidential and executive council elections are scheduled to take place in 2027.

Kurt Okraku has been the head of the country's football governing body since 2019.

Ayew is currently without a club after leaving Dutch side NAC Breda in May.

He has remained in Ghana and continued to train ahead of a possible move abroad, with ongoing negotiations with “three clubs”.

He has captained Ghana and represented the Black Stars at several major international tournaments including the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar.

Ghana News.title: Medi-Moses has been doing it for 30 years: Turning research into medicines – Answers Health Minister’s call for action
Ghana News.content:
As Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh urges Ghanaian researchers to move discoveries “beyond laboratory shelves” into commercially viable medicines and vaccines, one indigenous company has already been doing exactly that for nearly 30 years.

Dr De-Gaulle Moses Dogbatsey, CEO of the Medi-Moses Group of Companies, has built a proven track record of converting plant-medicine research into practical herbal products that reach patients across Ghana. His work offers a living example of the health-sovereignty agenda the Minister outlined this week at the Research Meets Manufacturing award ceremony under the PharmaVax Ghana programme.

Mr Akandoh told beneficiaries that the true measure of success “will not be the number of grants awarded but the number of research projects that progressed into commercially viable products.” He stressed that Ghana can no longer afford to wait “at the back of the queue” for essential medicines and vaccines, as happened during the COVID-19 pandemic. Local production, he said, is now a national health-security imperative that will also retain foreign exchange, create jobs and reduce vulnerability to external supply shocks.

Dr Dogbatsey’s journey mirrors that call. A medical doctor trained at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), he later obtained an MPhil in Pharmacognosy (Plant Medicine) from the same university and became the first Ghanaian medical doctor to specialise in the field. He headed the Clinical Research Department at the Centre for Scientific Research into Plant Medicine at Mampong-Akuapem from 2004 to 2008 and trained in Traditional Chinese Medicine at Beijing University of Traditional Chinese Medicine.

After leaving the Centre, he established the Medi-Moses Clinic and Prostate Centre, which has grown from humble beginnings into five branches across the country. The company specialises in the management of enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia), prostatitis and related conditions. Its flagship product, Prostacure Herbal Tea, together with Prostacure-X capsules, is credited with shrinking enlarged prostates without surgery and has earned international recognition.

In total, Dr Dogbatsey has formulated 57 herbal products targeting a wide range of conditions including infertility, erectile dysfunction, hypertension, diabetes, menstrual disorders, peptic ulcer, haemorrhoids, vaginal infections, skin diseases, typhoid, malaria and glaucoma. These products are the direct outcome of research translated into medicines available to ordinary Ghanaians.

Speaking in the spirit of the Minister’s message, industry observers note that Medi-Moses demonstrates what is possible when research is designed with manufacturability, scale-up, regulatory approval and patient affordability in mind.

The Health Minister announced a government framework contract for medicines estimated at GH¢159 million, with plans for expansion, to create a predictable market for quality local products. He also emphasised partnerships “with dignity and respect” that transfer technology and expertise while building Ghanaian capacity.

Dr Dogbatsey’s three-decade record shows that such capacity already exists in pockets of the private sector. As Ghana seeks to become a pharmaceutical hub for West Africa, the Medi-Moses story stands as practical proof that research can – and already does – travel the full distance from laboratory to pharmacy shelf, improving lives and strengthening national health security.

Endorsement

The Society of Private Medical and Dental Practitioners endorses the transition of research material into care for our clients. Ghana News.title: King of Norway’s health has worsened, palace says
Ghana News.content:
Norway's King Harald V's health has worsened, the palace has said, as he remains in hospital receiving antibiotics for a bloodstream bacterial infection.

The monarch has responded to treatment despite the deterioration in his condition, according to the palace, but he will remain at Oslo University Hospital, Rikshospitalet, and on leave from royal duties until further notice.

The 89-year-old, who has been on the throne since 1991, was admitted to hospital and put on sick leave a week ago.

His son Crown Prince Haakon, 53, has been serving as regent while his father is on leave.

King Harald has been treated in recent weeks with cortisone for a rare blood condition haemolytic anaemia. It causes the number of red blood cells in the body to be reduced and leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.

In April 2024, Norway's royal household said that King Harald would make a "permanent reduction" to his public engagements "out of consideration for his age". That year, the king had been fitted with a pacemaker after falling ill on holiday in Malaysia.

The Norwegian royal family has already faced a challenging year in 2026.

Crown Prince Haakon's wife, Crown Princess Mette-Marit, received a lung transplant in June after she had been diagnosed with a rare form of pulmonary fibrosis in 2018.

The transplant came two days after Mette-Marit's son Marius Borg Høiby was sentenced to four years in prison after being convicted of two counts of rape. He had denied the most serious charges, and his lawyers said he would appeal the sentence.

Høiby, 29, was four when his mother married Crown Prince Haakon and is not himself a royal figure.

Also earlier in the year, documents were released revealing Mette-Marit's frequent contact with late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

She later apologised to Norway's king and queen for her three-year friendship with Epstein and admitted to "poor judgement", adding in a national TV interview that she wished she had never met him.

Ghana News.title: Nawuni River swells as NADMO warns of rising flood risk in Northern Region
Ghana News.content:
The National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) has warned residents in and around Nawuni in the Kumbungu District of the Northern Region to prepare for possible flooding as water levels at the Nawuni intake continue to rise.

A reading taken by NADMO on Saturday, August 23, showed that the water level had risen to 23.85 feet, placing it within the critical flood range of 20 to 30 feet.

Officials say the elevated water level increases the risk of the White Volta overflowing its banks and flooding nearby communities and farmlands, particularly if additional rainfall occurs in the area.

Speaking to JoyNews, Chief Disaster Control Officer, Iddrisu Abubakari Ziblim, said NADMO was closely monitoring the situation, including rainfall patterns in the area, ahead of any potential spillage from upstream Burkina Faso.

“For now, the situation is okay,” Mr Ziblim said.

However, he cautioned that any spillage from the Bagre Dam, operated by Burkina Faso’s national electricity company, SONABEL, could significantly worsen the flood risk in the Northern Region.

Mr Ziblim said NADMO would be notified of the exact date and time should SONABEL commence the spillage, with the resulting floodwaters expected to reach the Northern Region within seven days.

He said the organisation had been conducting continuous pre-flood monitoring and public sensitisation since August 4, when it received an initial alert from SONABEL through the Water Resources Commission.

As part of its preparedness measures, NADMO has also pre-positioned a Rapid Response Team in Walewale in the North East Region to support emergency response and evacuation operations should the situation deteriorate.

The agency is urging residents in vulnerable communities to remain alert and follow official instructions as monitoring of the water levels continues.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.
