World.title: Orlando Pirates coach explains Van Rooyen’s exit
World.content:
Orlando Pirates head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou has shared his thoughts on the exit of Deano van Rooyen.

The 29-year-old defender parted ways with the Buccaneers last week after two years with the Soweto giants. He is the third right-back to leave the club after winning four trophies with the Sea Robbers.

Van Rooyen leaves Pirates after two seasons

Following Pirates’ 1-0 win over Sekhukhune United in the MTN8 first leg semi-final, Ouaddou praised the former Stellenbosch FC captain.



“Deano was a fantastic player, in terms of sports and as a human,” he said, as per iDiski Times.

“He gave a lot to the club; he won a lot of trophies and gave joy to the fans; he gave joy to the club as well.”

Van Rooyen was a first choice right back for Pirates during the 2024/25 season but injuries and the signing of Kamogelo Sebelebele limited his game time last season. He played just 10 leage matches in the last campaign and was yet to make an appearance this season.



Ouaddou explained that both the club and the player agreed it was time to move elsewhere.

“I think it’s part of life for the club to have some movements. So, the club and him found a way to continue his career elsewhere,” Ouaddou added.

“I was very proud to work with him and want to wish him all the best for his next project.”



With Van Rooyen gone, Orlando Pirates have only one right-back this season as they look to navigate the league, cup competitions and the CAF Champions League.

Did Pirates make a mistake releasing Deano?

World.title: Durban water relief: Here’s when you can expect supply to return
World.content:
Repairs to Durban’s Southern Aqueduct have been completed after a severe pipeline leak. Image: canva

Residents and businesses affected by the Southern Aqueduct water supply disruption can expect water to gradually return after emergency repairs to the pipeline were completed.

The eThekwini Municipality confirmed that technical teams have finished repairing the severe leak that developed on the pipeline during the charging process on 20 August 2026.

Southern Aqueduct repairs completed

The leak developed at Work Package 6 on Northbourne Road in Westville while the Prestressed Concrete Pipeline (PCP) was being charged following a planned shutdown linked to the Southern Aqueduct Upgrade Project.



The severity of the leak forced technical teams to shut down and isolate the pipeline again while repairs were carried out.

Municipal teams then reportedly worked around the clock to complete the repairs and return the pipeline to service.

The municipality has now confirmed that the necessary work has been completed.

Water will return gradually

Although repairs are finished, Durban residents should not expect water to return everywhere at the same time.

The municipality said water supply will be gradually restored from the evening of 23 August as the system is brought back into operation.

Residents in affected areas may therefore see their water return at different times as the network progressively recovers.



The staggered restoration is expected as the system is recharged and water pressure and reservoir levels recover.

Durban residents who do not immediately have water after restoration begins are therefore advised to allow time for the system to stabilise.

World.title: Warrant of arrest issued for Molemo ‘Jub Jub’ Maarohanye
World.content:
Molemo ‘Jub Jub’ Maarohanye’s legal problems are mounting as an arrest warrant is issued after he failed to appear in court this morning.

Maarohanye was expected to return to the Germiston Magistrate’s Court on kidnapping and intimidation charges, as well as for the unlawful discharge of a firearm, following an altercation with an e-hailing driver in Edenvale on 14 June.

The 45-year-old Uyajola 9/9 presenter allegedly accused the e-hailing driver of being in a romantic relationship with his girlfriend after she was dropped off at a residence in Edenvale



The arrest will not be activated until the matter is due back in court on 7 September, reports eNCA.

Speaking outside the court at his earlier appearance, Maarohanye denied any wrongdoing, even going as far as to suggest foul play.

“I’m shocked at the allegations. They are saying that I kidnapped my girlfriend, [who is] dating an Uber driver. I don’t know, man. I’m just complying and appearing,” he said.

World.title: 'Cat' Matlala's testimony delayed: Here's why
World.content:
PRETORIA - Alleged underworld figure Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala’s legal team says difficulties consulting with him at Kgosi Mampuru II Prison have contributed to delays in filing a late affidavit before the Madlanga Commission.

Advocate Fatima Missi, who represents Matlala, told the commission that the legal team has had to navigate a number of challenges to consult with her client and properly prepare his case.

Missi asked the commission to take these circumstances into account and allow Matlala’s legal team an opportunity to file its replying affidavit, heads of argument and an application for condonation for the late filing.

“We beg this Commission humbly to consider all the elements that we consistently have to do to try and ensure that we represent Mr Matlala,” Missi said.

However, commission chairperson Justice Mbuyiseli Madlanga was not persuaded that Matlala’s involvement was necessary to deal with the issues causing the delay.

World.title: Infrastructure development takes centre stage at Cape Town symposium
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Infrastructure development in South Africa is a hot topic in Cape Town as the Sustainable Infrastructure Development Symposium gets underway.

Key discussion points will be how to develop economic growth through Ports, Aviation and Logistics Corridors.

The symposium kicked off with a site visit to the Cape Flats Managed Aquifer Recharge project.

Delegates are meeting over the next two days to find ways to eradicate stumbling blocks hampering the maintenance and growth of infrastructure.

Ministers and Mayors from other African countries joined the delegation that visited the Cape Flats Managed Aquifer Recharge project in Cape Town's Pelican Park.

Once completed, the more than R1.3-billion project will play a crucial role in augmenting the Cape Flats Aquifer through the managed injection of treated wastewater.

Infrastructure development at municipal level as well as upgrading the country's roads, railways and ports also takes top priority.

A major focus is on how government manages its infrastructure portfolio. Officials say the state cannot spend billions on private leases while its own buildings stand vacant.

World.title: Water woes, broken toilets plague Reiger Park school
World.content:
BOKSBURG - Learners at Reiger Park Secondary School complain that they have limited access to drinking water at the school.

They also allege that the toilets are not up to standard, with only a few functioning toilets available for both boys and girls.

The school has just over 2,000 pupils, and it is alleged that some learners have resorted to drinking water from fire hydrants.

School Governing Body (SGB) Chairperson Charona Louw disputes this.

"We have been fixing the taps almost every month," she says.

"Things are being broken by the same learners vandalising the taps and toilets," she added.

While pupils say the problems have been ongoing for three months, Louw says this is not the case.

She says this is also why the SGB will be escalating the matter to the Gauteng Education Department’s district office.

Louw told eNCA that the school and learners will meet on Monday afternoon in an effort to find a solution.

World.title: Warrant of arrest issued for 'Jub Jub' Maarohanye
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A warrant of arrest has been issued for controversial media personality Molemo “Jub Jub” Maarohanye.

The musician failed to appear in the Germiston Magistrate's Court on Monday.

He faces allegations of kidnapping, assaulting an e-hailing driver, and discharging a firearm during an altercation in June.

The arrest will not be activated until 7 September when the matter is due back in court. Maarohanye claims to be in possession of a medical report showing that he has been booked off for 5 days.

READ | Jub Jub claims case is fabricated

While the state insists he pointed and discharged what appeared to be a firearm during the incident, Jub Jub's lawyer disputes claims that a pellet gun was recovered from his home.

The media personality denies the charges, describing them as fabricated.

World.title: LIVESTREAM | Ronald Lamola on stand at the TRC Cases Inquiry
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - International Relations Minister Ronald Lamola is back on the stand at the TRC Cases Inquiry on Monday.

Lamola previously appeared before the commission to account for his actions and record, during his tenure as Justice and Correctional Services Minister from 2019 to 2024.

His testimony centred on long-delayed apartheid-era prosecutions, recommended by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

Lamola defended his tenure, saying it was the most successful period for addressing TRC-related matters since the dawn of democracy.

World.title: Couple earns matric 34 years after dropping out of school to raise daughter
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Cathy and Edmund Kaas dropped out of school 34 years ago after the birth of their daughter.

The couple dedicated their remaining teenage years and the decades that followed to raising their children and building a life together, believing their dreams of obtaining their matric certificates were a thing of the past.

But Cathy was inspired after seeing social media posts about a woman in her 50s who had completed her matric, even attending a matric dance.

“She had even passed with four or five distinctions,” says Cathy.

That inspired her to tell her husband they should give it a try.

The couple enrolled for night classes, juggling their studies with their responsibilities at home.

Their daughter became their cheerleader and accountability partner.

“She did to us what we did to her when she was younger,” says Cathy.

“She would call us and ask why we were answering our phones, why we weren’t studying. The phones needed to be down,” she adds.

For the Kaases, it was about proving to their children, grandchildren and neighbours that your story is not set in stone.

World.title: LIVESTREAM | 'Cat' Matlala back in hot seat at Madlanga
World.content:
PRETORIA - Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala is back testifying at the Madlanga Commission on Monday.

He is expected to address omissions in his earlier affidavit, including the names of several senior police officials.

These include suspended Deputy National Police Commissioner Shadrack Sibiya, former KZN Hawks head Leseja Senona and former Organised Crime head Richard Shibiri.

Matlala is also expected to provide more information about his alleged links to the criminal underworld.

At his previous appearance, he refused to answer questions about the R228-million Medicare24 tender,

repeatedly citing his right against self-incrimination.

World.title: Pregnant woman shot dead in Wentworth as police appeal for leads
World.content:
DURBAN - The Wentworth Community Policing Forum is calling on residents to come forward with any leads after the brutal killing of a young expectant mother.

Tamia Fredericks was visiting last week when a man shot her in the head and fled.

Fredericks lived in the Newlands East area.

The local CPF says it's not the first time a woman has been killed in this way.

Police say no arrests have been made yet, and investigations are underway to determine the motive for the killing.

Fredericks' family has asked for privacy in the aftermath of her death and burial.
