World.title: Iraq tests return of Basrah crude sales through Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is resuming efforts to transfer more oil straight from its southern export ports, with state marketer SOMO seeking customers for September shipments as restricted tanker access via the Strait of Hormuz reopens.

The offering includes Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy, with purchasers likely to pick up the petroleum from Iraq’s Gulf export facilities rather than using alternate transfer arrangements devised during the recent shipping interruption.

The decision follows a significant breakthrough over the weekend, when Iran granted transit through Hormuz for several tankers carrying Iraqi oil in response to persistent diplomatic pleas from Baghdad.

For Iraq, even a partial reopening is crucial.

The majority of the country’s petroleum typically departs via its southern Gulf ports, rendering the economy especially susceptible when tanker traffic through Hormuz is halted.

Baghdad has spent recent weeks looking for methods to keep exports and government revenues coming. International merchants have utilized smaller boats and ship-to-ship swaps to transport some Iraqi barrels beyond the Gulf, while the government has stepped up attempts to enhance export capacity via Turkey and explore future routes via Syria and Jordan.

SOMO’s recent offering may give an early indicator of whether oil merchants are willing to return to loading straight from Basrah, despite ongoing security and transportation hazards.

QatarEnergy is also testing the market with oil available for collection within Hormuz, indicating that regional producers are progressively investigating whether traditional Gulf shipments may restart.

However, tanker movements remain far lower than usual, indicating that Iraq cannot count on Hormuz recovering to its pre-conflict role.

This uncertainty has fueled Baghdad’s desire to diversify its oil infrastructure. Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s administration seeks to increase exports via Turkey’s Ceyhan port and create new routes to the Mediterranean and Red Sea.

For now, the top objective is to send as many Iraqi barrels to foreign consumers as securely as possible while also restoring the oil revenue on which the government budget is largely dependent.

The SOMO tender is therefore more than just a crude sale. It is an early test of whether Iraq’s key southern oil-export infrastructure can resume regular operations after the Hormuz crisis, which revealed one of the country’s most serious economic weaknesses.

World.title: Oman’s SalamAir adds Erbil as second destination in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — SalamAir, Oman’s low-cost airline, will commence direct flights between Muscat and Erbil on October 25, 2026, strengthening its footprint in Iraq after its debut into the Baghdad market.

The airline has launched ticket sales for the new flight, which will run twice a week between the Omani capital and Erbil.

One-way Lite fares will start at approximately $143 (187,000 Iraqi dinars).

SalamAir adds Erbil as its second Iraqi destination, capitalizing on the success of its current Muscat-Baghdad route.

The new link is designed to facilitate business, tourist, commerce, and family travel between Oman and Iraq, as well as provide travelers from Erbil with additional connections via Muscat to destinations in India and other regions of Asia.

SalamAir Chief Commercial Officer Steven Allen characterized Iraq as an important market for the airline, with Erbil providing an additional potential to meet expanding regional demand and improve Muscat’s position as a connecting hub.

The extension also offers another international link to Erbil International Airport, and it comes as Iraq welcomes more regional airline services as business and tourism flourish.

World.title: Ukraine backers gather as war escalates, air defence runs low
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukraine hosts a meeting of its key European backers on Monday to press for critical air-defence supplies and more pressure on Moscow, with Russian attacks killing more civilians than at any time since the first months of the invasion.

The meeting of the Coalition of the Willing will be jointly chaired by the leaders of Britain, France and Germany.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will be in Kyiv for his first international trip since taking office, and several other leaders are expected to join remotely.

EU Council President Antonio Costa is also due in Kyiv for the talks, which come amid the latest, deadly escalation of the war.

Russia has been pounding Kyiv with ballistic missiles in recent weeks, ripping open apartment blocks and killing dozens of citizens in the capital.

The escalating Russian strikes have pushed civilian deaths to their highest levels since the first months of Russia’s 2022 invasion.

After almost every attack — which sees tens of thousands hunker in the Kyiv metro system and many more in basements and other shelters across the city — Zelensky has issued public pleas for more air-defence support.

Ahead of the meeting, Ukraine has forged ahead with its campaign against Russia’s logistics sites, hitting multiple warehouses belonging to e-commerce giant Ozon.

Ozon reported fires early Monday at its warehouses in Krasnodar and Makhachkala, both in southern Russia, adding that sites in Adygeysk and Nevinnomyssk were evacuated due to threats of drone attack.

Russian authorities also said debris from a Ukrainian drone attack killed two children and wounded nine others.

– UK, French support –

Ukraine celebrates independence day on Monday, which also marks exactly four-and-a-half years since Russia invaded on February 24, 2022.

“Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve,” Burnham said in a statement before his arrival in Kyiv.

“We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace.”

Diplomacy on ending the conflict — Europe’s largest since World War II — is effectively frozen.

Russia is demanding hardline territorial and political concessions that Kyiv has rejected as a capitulation that would only enable another Russian attack.

Burnham is set to announce that the British government is authorising defence firm MBDA to release classified information needed to help Ukraine and France set up local production of the long-range SCALP missile.

And on Saturday, French President Emmanuel Macron pledged Paris would deliver new interceptor missiles.

“It is crucial to provide Ukraine with all the necessary means to defend its skies and thwart this aggression,” Macron wrote on X.

The ballistic missiles Russia has been firing in their dozens are incredibly fast and travel with a high-arching trajectory, making them difficult to stop.

Kyiv’s homegrown weapons cannot shoot them down, meaning Ukraine is reliant on advanced systems — chiefly, US Patriot interceptors — to protect its skies.

But due to shortfalls globally since the US launched its war on Iran, Ukraine has been left exposed.

– Ukraine’s missiles shortfall –

Ahead of the meeting, Zelensky revealed the extent of the deficit, releasing usually closely guarded numbers.

He said deliveries of crucial Patriot interceptors had halved since 2023.

“Over the entire of 2023, Ukraine received 675 missiles, and over all of 2025 — 364, even though Russian missile strikes have increased,” Zelensky said.

“For 2026, as currently projected, it is 264,” he added, saying Ukraine was seeking a package of at least 300 for the upcoming winter.

The United States faces its own shortfall of the missiles during its war on Iran and has resisted releasing large numbers to Ukraine.

Zelensky said Russia could produce around 100 ballistic missiles a month.

Ukraine, meanwhile, has accelerated its own campaign of long-range strikes on Russian energy and logistics sites — including oil refineries and retail warehouses.

The Coalition of the Willing is a Franco-British initiative to deliver support to Ukraine and ramp up pressure on Russia.

Originally designed as a group of countries that would be willing to deploy peacekeeping troops to Ukraine in the event a ceasefire was reached, it has become a parallel forum for marshalling support to Ukraine as uncertainty persists over US commitments under Donald Trump.

World.title: New Zealand moves to ban social media for under-16s
World.content:
Wellington – New Zealand’s government will introduce legislation on Monday banning under 16s from using social media, joining a number of countries seeking to keep youngsters off sites such as Instagram and TikTok.

New Zealand has been investigating a social media ban for over a year, after neighbouring Australia implemented its world-first legislation in December.

Under the Online Safety Bill, firms like Meta could be fined up to 10 percent of their global revenue if they fail to comply.

“We simply cannot accept the harm being done to a generation of New Zealand children,” Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said.

In announcing the Online Safety Bill, Luxon said “one in three children aged between 13 and 17 are now spending at least five hours on social media a day”.

“Social media is exposing them to harmful content, addictive technology and pressures they are not equipped to deal with, and it’s affecting their family life, mental health, sleep, and education,” he said.

Luxon specifically called out platforms Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat and Facebook, saying they would be required to take “reasonable steps to check users are over the age of 16”.

They would have to use “existing account information, facial age estimation, digital ID services and formal ID” to verify age.

Platforms would also be required to assess the risks they pose as well as report on how those dangers are being reduced, and penalties would be introduced for companies that fail to comply.

Education Minister Erica Stanford said the Bill “places legal obligations on platforms”.

“No penalties are proposed for children, their parents or caregivers,” Stanford said.

It’s unclear whether the bill will pass, as both National Party’s coalition partners — the libertarian ACT party and NZ First — have said they oppose it.

In a statement, the populist NZ First said they could not support the law given the “colossal failure” of the legislation in Australia, while ACT said they believed the law “won’t work”, and teenagers would easily get around the ban.

Australia last year banned under 16s from the likes of Facebook, Instagram and TikTok, in a crackdown designed to protect children from online bullying and “predatory algorithms”.

A team of Australia-based researchers in a peer-reviewed study published in June found little evidence to suggest teenagers have turned away from social media as a consequence, however.

World.title: UEFA’s Ceferin tells Infantino to go, but ‘not interested’ in replacing him
World.content:
London – UEFA chief Aleksander Ceferin says he is “not interested” in replacing Gianni Infantino but warned the under-fire FIFA president must quit or face a leadership challenge.

Infantino has come under increasing pressure to step down as head of world football’s governing body over his now-abandoned plan to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.

UEFA, which oversees European football, has threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions with several continental and national federations also withdrawing their support for Infantino.

But Ceferin ruled himself out of a bid to take Infantino’s place, the 58-year-old Slovenian on Monday telling The Rest is Politics podcast: “I’m not interested because of two reasons.

“One reason is that I love UEFA and I love working here, and I think that at a certain point… it’s time to also enjoy life a bit.

“And the second point is, my credibility is much, much higher if I’m not interested in the position.”

Ceferin has been vocal in his criticism since Infantino revealed his controversial plans to seek private investment in a company to run FIFA tournaments.

He now believes Infantino’s previously impregnable position is under threat, with Ceferin forecasting the Swiss will have to stand down or face a leadership challenge if he seeks re-election at the next FIFA Congress, in Morocco in March.

Infantino, a former UEFA secretary general, had the broad backing of European nations when he succeeded Sepp Blatter as FIFA president in 2016.

But Ceferin, who revealed he has not spoken to Infantino since the start of the controversy, insisted the current situation was very different.

“There are two options,” he said.

“One option is that he (Infantino) realises that he doesn’t have the support, and that’s not only a political support of the ones who vote, but the political support of the football community, the political support of fans, the political support of the players, former players, coaches.

“And the second option, that he goes to the elections in March, but in that case I think he will have a candidate against him. I don’t know yet who.”

CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani and AFC boss Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa are considered two of the most likely challengers for Infantino’s position.

– Infantino ‘support’ –

Infantino was in the Dominican Republic over the weekend for meetings with local and regional football officials, despite Montagliani reportedly asking him to stay away from a youth tournament there.

In video remarks released by FIFA on Sunday, the 56-year-old Infantino appeared to reference the furore surrounding him.

“It’s important to engage, to have a dialogue, to express views and opinions,” he said.

“A lot has been happening the last few weeks and it’s important that you hear, you listen, and you’re able to also express what your feelings are.

“So I think overall positive, very, very happy with all the support I get here.”

World.title: Oil falls as Trump pledges economic war on Iran
World.content:
Hong Kong – Oil prices fell on Monday as investors braced for details of a US plan to isolate the Iranian economy that President Donald Trump billed as the “most crushing” financial operation ever against Tehran.

Asian stocks were mostly down in early trading, with South Korea’s tech-rich Kospi falling 1.4 percent after Samsung Electronics said it spent a massive $80 billion to buy back its own shares following weeks of turbulent trading.

The chip giant’s shares, along with those of rival SK hynix, peaked in June on optimism for the artificial intelligence boom, but have since fallen amid investor jitters and a broader tech rout.

In an important week for AI, investors are also looking towards an earnings report from Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company and a bellwether for the sector.

The recurring question for the US chipmaker is whether the AI boom will continue to accelerate as the technology takes over more corners of the broader economy.

“The spending machine is still running, but the bill is getting heavier,” said Stephen Innes of SPI Asset Management.

“Nvidia must now show that the most expensive investment boom in modern market history can still pay its bills.”

Chinese tech giant Alibaba is keeping focus on the sector after announcing on Sunday that it plans to issue $10.2 billion in new shares in Hong Kong to fund its global AI ambitions.

The firm, known for its open-source “Qwen” AI models, has been ploughing tens of billions of dollars into the technology, with shareholders eager to see how it will monetise the huge investments.

Tokyo, Shanghai, Taipei and Wellington were down on Monday. Sydney, Jakarta and Bangkok posted gains, while Manila and Kuala Lumpur were flat.

Hong Kong fell more than two percent despite fast-fashion giant Shein announcing its market debut will take place in the Chinese financial hub on September 1.

The long-awaited listing would value the group — known for its vast selection of products at stunningly low prices — at close to $27 billion.

Eyes are also on US Treasury boss Scott Bessent, who said he would give more details in a news conference on Monday on a fresh push to pile economic pressure on Iran.

The United States warned allies and China on Thursday to join Trump’s new campaign, which comes as the unpopular war in the Middle East drags toward the six-month mark.

US Vice President JD Vance admitted the plan was a “delicate dance” because Iran will “try to apply economic pressure to us”.

Asked whether the United States would pressure China, Bessent told CNBC that “many conversations are best to have in private”, but called on Beijing “to get with the programme”.

Both main crude contracts were down 2.3 percent, with the Brent benchmark sitting at $92 a barrel.

Traders will also be watching this week’s annual gathering of central bankers, economists and finance chiefs in Jackson Hole in the United States, hoping for some clarification on US monetary policy.

The meeting comes after the Treasury bought its own bonds last week in an effort to push down borrowing costs after the 30-year yield surged to levels last seen in 2007, just before the global financial crisis.

Yields have risen on inflation fears and as the United States reported that its federal debt had topped $40 trillion.

World.title: Iraq’s IDC relocates drilling rig from Zubair oil field to East Baghdad field
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Drilling Company (IDC) is relocating the IDC-51 drilling rig from the Zubair oil field in the southern province of Basra to the East Baghdad South field.

Under the supervision of the state-owned Midland Oil Company (MOC), the step is part of a deal with EBS Petroleum, an Iraqi-registered subsidiary of Chinese state-owned firm ZhenHua Oil, to drill 17 horizontal wells to increase production capacity in Iraq’s central region.

The move entails disassembling the rig at Zubair, shipping components, reassembling, and conducting safety tests at East Baghdad South.

This project builds on the IDC’s past development phases in the same field, which featured distinct campaigns of 27 and 18 horizontal wells.

The East Baghdad South field is the extremely productive southern section of the larger, super-giant East Baghdad oilfield complex.

The oilfield is one of Iraq’s most unusual energy resources, measuring around 60 kilometers in length and 12 kilometers in its width. It is located just under the capital’s densely populated suburbs.

Appraisal drilling increased the proved reserves of the East Baghdad field to 15 billion barrels, including an enormous reservoir of medium and light oil.

World.title: Iraq’s PMF repels ISIS attack in Salah al-Din province
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) successfully foiled on Sunday an attack by ISIS terrorists on a military position in the Tuz Khurmatu region in the eastern province of Salah al-Din.

The raid targeted an isolated outpost belonging to the Commando Regiment of the PMF’s 63rd Brigade.

ISIS militants launched an armed attack from a mountain, resulting in an intense battle, with loud gunfire and explosions reported by civilians.

The Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) represent a coalition of Shia paramilitary groups that have been officially incorporated into Iraq’s national security forces. This coalition consists of various militias that have ties with Iran.

PMF fighters engaged the attackers immediately, compelling them to retreat into the challenging terrain without accomplishing any tactical objectives. No casualties have been reported among PMF personnel.

Iraqi Army and PMF soldiers started a coordinated, large-scale search operation in a nearby mountainous area to track down fleeing terrorists and identify their locations.

This failed attack highlights the ongoing threat of secret factions belonging to the ISIS group in isolated places.

Analysts see that these small-scale, opportunistic ambushes are intended to test local defense networks as Baghdad moves to autonomous state security ahead of the scheduled withdrawal of international coalition forces.

NEW DELHI: The

on Monday issued summons to commentator Abhijit Iyer-Mitra and several media platforms in a suit filed by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader

, who has alleged that his residential address and other personal details were published on social media without his consent.

The development came during the hearing of Das's plea seeking interim protection against the alleged disclosure of his personal information. The court was informed that X, formerly known as Twitter, had removed the posts allegedly carrying Das's residential address.

Justice Sachin Datta issued notice on Das's application seeking interim relief and directed the defendants to file their replies. The matter will next be heard on September 14.

Senior Advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for Das, submitted that personnel of The Pamphlet had entered his client's residential property without permission and recorded a video.

Sibal alleged that Iyer-Mitra subsequently added to the video and shared it on social media. He further submitted that some posts on X specifically mentioned Das's residential address.

Seeking protection for his client, Sibal urged the court to ensure that the posts, which had already been removed by X under its policy, were not restored.





Appearing for X, counsel told the court that the concerned links were "no longer accessible." The submission was recorded by the court.

Counsel for The Pamphlet also submitted that the posts were no longer available on X and sought time to respond to the allegations on merits.

The court further allowed Das to correct the name of The Sunday Guardian in the proceedings and permitted him to amend the memo of parties and plaint within three days.

Apart from Iyer-Mitra and The Pamphlet, the suit names LawBeat, The Jaipur Dialogues, The Sunday Guardian, Google LLC and X Corp as defendants.

Das has sought permanent and mandatory injunctions against the defendants, besides damages, alleging violation of his privacy, dignity and security.

In his plea, Das alleged that his residential address and other personal details were recorded and circulated without his consent.

He claimed that the disclosure of his exact address could expose him and other occupants of his residence to security risks.

World.title: Parandur airport project to be dropped by Tamil Nadu government, announces CM Vijay
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Monday (August 24, 2026) announced his government’s decision to drop the proposed airport at Parandur and identify alternative sites for a new, second airport in Chennai. Making a suo motu statement in the Assembly, he said a new terminal, Terminal 5, would be developed in the north-western area of Chennai airport in collaboration with the Airports Authority of India (AAI), along with an approach road and a flyover.

The main Opposition DMK sought to speak on the issue, but Speaker J.C.D. Prabhakar said he would not allow a debate on an announcement made under Rule 110 of the Assembly. Former Finance Minister Thangam Thennarasu said he was not seeking to debate the issue but wanted to make a clarification. The DMK members walked out after the Speaker stood his ground.

The Chief Minister said he had consulted experts on the creation of a new airport and a few alternative sites had been identified without causing much damage to farmland and human settlements.

“The site will be finalised after studying the technical feasibility and consulting the departments concerned,” he said, recalling his visit to Parandur in 2025 to express solidarity with the protesting farmers and his earlier announcement at Vikravandi opposing the airport project.

He said the existing Chennai airport at Meenambakkam was currently handling 30 million passengers a year and that the capacity would increase to 35 million once Terminal 3 was completed. “After the completion of Terminal 5, the passenger capacity will increase to 55 million a year. It will improve the services and transport facilities until a new airport is completed,” he said.

The Chief Minister said he was fully aware of the role of airports in industrial development but maintained that an airport should not be built at Parandur as it would affect vast tracts of farmland and human settlements. “But the previous government tried to create a new airport at the cost of farmers, their lands and human settlements,” he said.

World.title: In Chennai’s beachside food, the secret ingredient is the sea
World.content:
An unmissable part of a visit to Chennai’s beaches is the food. Food is central to the city’s identity, but what you eat by the sea has a character of its own: the maanga pattani sundal, hot bajjis, fish fry, smoky roasted corn, and cloud-like cotton candy.

From the prawns and crabs of Pazhaverkadu and the organised chaos of Kasimedu fish market, to the rows of meen saapadu mess at Pattinapakkam, and the newer food trucks of Besant Nagar, the coast offers a spread for every kind of appetite. For generations, Chennai residents have come to the coast to eat, talk, walk, and make memories.

On an August evening, as the sea breeze cools the shore after a scorching day, 56-year-old Jayashree, comes to the beach with her family after years. The beach has a way of bringing back old memories, she says, and food is an inseparable part of them.

“One of the main reasons we look forward to coming to the beach is for the snacks,” Jayashree says, laughing, as she munches on chunks of raw mango dusted with chilli powder. As a child, she recalls, her father would refuse to buy much of the food sold at the beach, worried that it was unhygienic. “So instead, we would make him buy us toys,” she says. Her father, sitting nearby, now holds a packet of pattani sundal.

Twenty-three-year-olds Rajeeth Nisha and Kirijha, from Karaikudi and Madurai respectively, have recently started coming to the beach with friends after college, and fish fry is already part of the ritual. “We love the fish fry here. Because we come as a group, we enjoy it more,” they say.

For another Nisha, 31, a resident of Kodungaiyur, the beach is a monthly family outing. She comes with her husband and two children, and fish is, again, a mandatory snack here. “At home, I make the same things, but we all eat from separate plates. Here, we buy one big fish or one plate of prawns and everyone shares. It’s nice,” she says with a smile.

So, is there a secret sauce to the distinctive taste of beachside fish fry? At the Alli Muthu fish stall at the Marina, rows of vanjaram, kilangan, kelathi, nethili, paarai and kanava sit ready for the pan, each piece coated in a bright red marinade that catches the eye before it hits the tongue.

Ganesh, who has been in the business for 30 years, starting as a child who used to hang around when his mother ran the stall, says it is the podi sprinkled over the fried fish, a blend of several masalas. “Chicken masala, fish fry masala, garam masala…,” he rattles off nearly 10 ingredients, near-impossible for anyone to remember, let alone recreate. Perhaps, though, the recipe is only part of the answer.

A little away, the bajji stalls have their own cheerful display. Long green bajji milagai hang in bunches like thoranams, while sliced potatoes, raw bananas and onions wait to be dipped into batter and plunged into hot oil.

As much as the bajjis are great — crispy, with just the right consistency of batter and the perfect shade of golden brown — the chutney is something else. A search for ‘beach-style chutney’ throws up countless recipes on the web, but perhaps none quite taste the same as the one eaten here.

Beach food may be hard to recreate at home because its flavour comes from more than just the masala: the salt, the sticky air, the sound of the waves, sand clinging to your feet, and the easy abandon with which people arrive at the beach simply to have fun.

World.title: PM Modi to address country''s youth on Thursday ahead of National Sports Day
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the youth of the country, including sportspersons, across more than 1500 locations on Thursday (August 27, 2026) to mark the occasion of the National Sports Day which falls on August 29.

Mr. Modi's virtual address will be part of the nationwide programme 'Khelo India Samvaad – Khel Ki Baat, PM Ke Saath', a major initiative of the Sports Ministry to be held two days ahead of the National Sports Day.

Hockey legend Dhyan Chand's birth anniversary, which falls on August 29, is celebrated as the National Sports Day in the country.

"Key excerpts from the Hon’ble Prime Minister’s Independence Day message on Sports and Youth Power will also be showcased. This will be followed by the virtual address of the Hon’ble Prime Minister to the youth across the country," Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya said during a media briefing.

"Through this initiative, youth, athletes and educational institutions are being brought together at 1,500+ locations across the country.

"IITs, IIMs, NITs, AIIMS, premier medical colleges and universities, along with other leading educational institutions, are participating in this nationwide campaign." He said the programme is a major effort to create a direct dialogue between sports-loving youth and India’s policymakers, providing young people with an opportunity to share their ideas, experiences and suggestions.

The programme will begin with a welcome by MY Bharat volunteers, followed by a special video presentation highlighting the transformational changes in India’s sporting ecosystem over the past 12 years.

Following the Prime Minister’s address, physical programmes will commence at 1,500+ locations across the country.

At the national capital, the celebration will be held in four-five locations, including one at the IIT, Delhi, where Mr. Mandaviya will grace the occasion.

"I will be present at the IIT Delhi for the celebrations (on August 27)," the Minister said.

Leading former and current Indian athletes and international medal winners, including Indian Olympic Association president P.T. Usha will also interact with the youth of the country.

Other prominent sportspersons who will interact with the youth include Manika Batra, Deepa Karmakar, Saina Nehwal, Gagan Narang, Sreejesh, Mary Kom, Baichung Bhutia, Pullela Gopichand, Anju Bobby George, Karnam Malleswari, Mirabai Chanu, and some cricketers.

"They (the youth) will share their journeys, challenges, failures, successes and sporting experiences with young participants," Mr. Mandaviya said.

"The objective of the event is to inspire young people with the belief that a champion’s journey does not begin in a grand stadium, but with a small field and a first attempt." Members of Parliament, Members of Legislative Assemblies, Union Ministers, Ministers of State and State Sports Ministers will participate in the programme.

"These elected representatives and dignitaries will engage with youth and seek their ideas and suggestions on the four key themes," he said.

Key objectives of the programme

Mr. Mandaviya said key objectives include the sharing by the youth of their ideas, suggestions and innovative thoughts on four key themes related to sports and youth.

"First, strengthening the sports ecosystem by ensuring better facilities, coaching and opportunities reach the grassroots. Second, nurturing talent for the 2036 Olympics, with a focus on scientific talent identification and athlete development.

"Third, strengthening youth leadership and increasing youth participation in governance. Fourth, Youth Empowerment for Viksit Bharat, including future-ready skills, volunteering and opportunities for nation-building," he said.

The suggestions gathered through the programme will be taken directly to policymakers and the wider sports ecosystem, helping connect ground-level experiences and youth aspirations with policy making.

As part of youth engagement activities, a Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) Quiz will be organised. Youth will also be encouraged to register on the MY Bharat Portal.

The objective is to connect young people beyond a one-day event and make them part of a long-term national youth engagement ecosystem.

World.title: Supreme Court issues notice to Centre, CBI on plea for CBI probe into JPSC exam 'irregularities'
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Monday (August 24, 2026) issued notices to the Centre and the State government on a plea seeking an independent, time-bound probe by the CBI into alleged malpractices in the Jharkhand Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination.

A Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana sought a response from the Union of India, the Jharkhand government, the Jharkhand Public Service Commission, CBI and others.

Senior advocate Manan Kumar Mishra, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that the plea seeks a CBI inquiry or an inquiry by a former judge of this court.

The top court was hearing a petition filed by activist Harisharan Devgan, through advocate Satyam Singh Rajput.

"The present writ petition under Article 32 of the Constitution of India is being preferred in public interest seeking urgent intervention of this court in relation to serious and substantial concerns regarding the integrity, fairness, transparency and credibility of the Jharkhand Combined Civil Services Preliminary Competitive Examination 2025, conducted by respondent no. 2 Jharkhand Public Service Commission pursuant to  No. 01/2026 on April 19, 2026," it said.

The plea has also sought transfer of the investigation from the State CID to the CBI to ensure an impartial probe into public officials and examination agencies.

The petitioner submitted that the controversy cannot appropriately be examined merely as a dispute concerning individual candidates or isolated instances of alleged malpractice.

"The allegations require examination of the entire examination chain, including preparation and printing of question papers, coding, storage, transportation, distribution, conduct of the examination, collection and custody of OMR sheets, scanning, coding and decoding, evaluation, storage and access to electronic examination data, generation of the result and publication thereof," it said.

It has also sought direction to immediately secure all physical and digital evidence, including original and candidate-held OMR carbon copies, CCTV footage, and server audit logs, to prevent tampering.

"The petitioner is conscious that the mere existence of allegations or public protests cannot, by itself, justify cancellation of an examination. The petitioner, therefore, does not seek cancellation merely based on media reports or allegations.

"The principal relief sought is for an independent, impartial, comprehensive and time-bound investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation, so that the nature, extent, mechanism and impact of the alleged irregularities may be objectively determined," it said.

The petition said the consequential question: Whether the preliminary examination can safely be relied upon. must be determined based on objective and scientifically verifiable evidence.

The petitioner said he raises a Constitutional question concerning whether a public recruitment examination conducted by a Constitutional authority has retained the minimum degree of fairness, transparency, reliability and institutional integrity necessary for its result to Constitute the lawful basis for public appointments.

World.title: Dropping Parandur airport project an irreversible setback for Tamil Nadu: M.K. Stalin
World.content:
Former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and DMK president M.K. Stalin on Monday (August 24, 2026) said the State government’s decision to drop the plan to construct an airport at Parandur near Chennai, was not a change but an irreversible setback for Tamil Nadu’s growth.

“It will set the State’s development back by several years. Tamil Nadu’s interests cannot be mortgaged for petty political considerations. An announcement of such far-reaching importance being made under Rule 110, shutting out any opportunity for debate or even for members to voice their views, is deeply troubling,” he said in a post on social media.

Mr. Stalin said Tamil Nadu was a leader in the country across sectors, from electronics exports to automobiles, and that a world-class airport in its capital was not merely desirable but absolutely essential. “Rejecting such a vital project is not change. It is a massive disappointment,” he said.

The former Chief Minister said the site had been carefully selected after evaluating all available alternatives, and the land acquisition process, along with several stages of preparatory work and approvals, had already been completed.

“We had drawn up plans to ensure that construction could begin at a rapid pace once we returned to office. If the new government now starts all over again, identifies another location and goes through the entire process before work can even begin, Tamil Nadu’s growth trajectory itself will drop,” he said.

Mr. Stalin said under the (erstwhile) “Dravidian Model” government, Tamil Nadu had become the first port of call for investors. “This decision threatens to push the State to the bottom of the table. The Chief Minister’s [C. Joseph Vijay] announcement is nothing short of a jackpot for competing States,” he said.

“Without industrial growth, economic targets of one trillion USD or 1.5 trillion USD are simply impossible to achieve. Taken without foresight, planning or consultation, this decision by the TVK government is a devastating blow to the employment dreams of Tamil Nadu’s youth,” he added.

DMK MLAs walk out

Former Finance and Industries Minister Thangam Thennarasu (DMK) said Parandur was the appropriate location for a greenfield airport. He alleged the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam-led government had dropped the project only for political reasons. “If a scheme is dropped for political reasons, it will affect our economy,” he said after DMK members walked out from the House over the Speaker’s refusal to allow them to speak on the issue.

Speaker J.C.D. Prabhakar said no discussion could be permitted after an announcement was made under Rule 110 of the Assembly.

Mr. Thennarasu said the DMK government had proposed to acquire 5,740 acres for the Parandur airport and had already acquired 90% of the land. “The team comprising me, former PWD Minister E.V. Velu, and T.M. Anbarasan, held several rounds of talks with the villagers. All of them, except people of one village, agreed and accepted compensation. As per the land acquisition rules, the land cannot be used for any purpose other than the original project. What will you do with the land?” he asked.

Mr. Thennarasu said only a greenfield airport would help industries and the number of companies manufacturing electronic goods in Sriperumbudur had increased in the expectation that there would be a major airport nearby. “Tamil Nadu tops in the import of electronic goods. The decision will affect industrial investment,” he said.

He also said the Bengaluru airport, which handles 5.5 lakh tonnes of cargo, was able to facilitate trade with European countries and that Chennai also needed a major airport for industrial development. “We have already extended the Metro Rail project up to Sunguvarchathiram because of the decision to build the airport at Parandur. What will happen to it?” he asked.

World.title: Piyush Goyal says India negotiating FTAs with 8 to 9 more blocs, aims to cover 75% of global trade
World.content:
India is in negotiations with at least 8 to 9 more groups of countries and individual nations that together account for another $15 trillion of GDP, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Monday (August 24, 2026).

He added that the country's free trade agreements would eventually cover about 75% of global trade and help position India as a trusted partner in global value chains.

India has a large domestic market and it opens its doors to the world with nine free trade agreements signed in the last four years, he said in Tokyo, while addressing business representatives from India and Japan.

These nine agreements cover economies with a combined GDP of $60 trillion and 38 developed countries.

The earlier trade pacts with countries, including Japan and Korea , and the ASEAN region have opened another $10 trillion of GDP.

"So today India opens up the doors to preferential market access to USD 70 trillion of economy. We are in negotiations with at least 8 or 9 other groups of countries or countries which will add another $15 trillion.

"Basically 75% of global trade will be covered through our free trade agreements, opening India to become a part of the global value chain as a trusted partner," he said.

Mr. Goyal is leading a large business delegation of over 200 representatives here to boost trade and investment ties between the two countries. He said that large opportunities for investments in India are there in areas like data centres, manufacturing and artificial intelligence.

The Minister added that the increasing economic ties should lead towards balanced trade between India and Japan.

World.title: Jadavpur University clash: Inquiry panel chief resigns, varsity to appoint new committee head
World.content:
Professor Subha Shankar Sarkar has resigned as the head of a five-member committee constituted by Jadavpur University to probe into the recent vandalism on its campus allegedly by ABVP workers, citing his inability to conduct the inquiry effectively, a varsity official said Monday (August 24, 2026).

The university will appoint a new committee head to carry out the investigation, he said.

JU acting registrar Selim Box Mandal said, "Sarkar has communicated his inability to head the panel. A new chairperson would be appointed shortly." Mr. Sarkar told Jadavpur University Vice Chancellor Chiranjib Bhattacharjee through an email on Saturday (August 22) that he would not be able to take up the assignment.

"I informed the Jadavpur University vice-chancellor immediately after receiving the communication about my appointment. I am currently in Delhi, and the inquiry would require regular interactions with the people who were present on the campus during the incident," Mr. Sarkar, who is the former Netaji Subhas Open University vice-chancellor, told PTI on Monday (August 24).

Mr. Sarkar said the university authorities had suggested that he could conduct the proceedings online, but he felt that such an inquiry could not be carried out effectively through virtual interactions.

A clash broke out between members of ABVP and Left-leaning student groups at Jadavpur University here early on August 20, with both sides accusing each other of bringing outsiders into the campus.

The two camps had traded allegations over the presence of people from outside the university.

RSS-affiliated Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) alleged that members of the Left student organisations, including the SFI and DSO-DSF, had started confrontations under the cover of a meeting of the Faculty of Engineering and Technology Students' Union (FETSU).

The Left-leaning groups, however, accused the ABVP of bringing outsiders into the campus and indulging in vandalism.

Mr. Sarkar's decision came hours before the teachers’ wing of the RSS, the Akhil Bharatiya Rashtriya Shaikshik Mahasangh, wrote to the JU vice chancellor, opposing his appointment.

The teachers' organisation questioned Mr. Sarkar’s selection to lead the inquiry panel, referring to his removal as the chairman of the West Bengal School Service Commission in January 2022 following proceedings before the Calcutta High Court over alleged irregularities in recruitments.

The university had announced the formation of the committee on August 21, following a demonstration by students, teachers and citizens protesting against the alleged vandalism on the campus.

The RSS-linked teachers’ wing, in its letter to the vice-chancellor, said Mr. Sarkar’s appointment could raise doubts about the “credibility, independence and impartiality” of the proposed inquiry.

It demanded that the panel be headed by a retired judge of the Calcutta High Court or Supreme Court to ensure an independent and transparent investigation.

Bhaskar Sardar, president of the organisation’s JU unit, welcomed Mr. Sarkar’s decision to resign.

Mr. Sarkar was appointed chairman of the school service commission in December 2020 while serving as vice-chancellor of Netaji Subhas Open University, Sardar claimed.

The Calcutta High Court had expressed dissatisfaction over the functioning of the commission and questioned his continuation as its chairman, he said.

"Such a man cannot head an inquiry panel into attacks against us. A conspiracy was hatched against us for the damage of the university plaque," an ABVP spokesperson said.

World.title: CDF Munir, Naqvi in Iran as part of Pakistan's efforts for regional peace
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi reached Tehran on Monday, Iranian media reported after Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) described the visit “as part of Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and stability”.

State media in Pakistan, meanwhile, reported that CDF Munir and Naqvi had held a meeting with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni.

Earlier, ISPR said CDF Munir will “focus on promoting efforts towards peaceful, lasting and comprehensive resolution of the conflict in the Middle East” during the visit.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqai on Sunday said CDF Munir was expected to travel to Tehran to continue efforts to bring peace and security to the region.

He said CDF Munir would lead an official delegation and the “visit aims to strengthen bilateral cooperation between Iran and Pakistan and to continue Pakis­tan’s good offices in support of peace and security in the region”.

During the visit, CDF Munir would meet and hold talks with senior officials Iran, Baqaei added.

The United States and Israel triggered the Middle East war with a massive wave of strikes against Iran on February 28, triggering Iranian retaliation across the region.

An April 8 ceasefire ended nearly 40 days of intense bombardment, but control over the Strait of Hormuz soon emerged as a key flashpoint in the conflict.

Iran has controlled the vital energy conduit since the war began. Reopening the strait, vital for global oil and gas supplies, has become a US priority, but Tehran insists the waterway will remain closed until Washington lifts its naval blockade on Iranian ports, removes oil sanctions and unfreezes Iranian assets abroad.

Pakistan has played a key role in efforts to halt war between Iran and the United States, brokering a memorandum of understanding (MoU) in June, but peace negotiations currently appear stalled.

Last week, US President Donald Trump announced that Washington would ramp up economic pressure on Iran “on an unprecedented scale”.

Washington has urged other governments, including Beijing, to join efforts to further isolate Iran’s economy.

The US is expected to announce details related to the planned sanctions on Mondau, which ​US officials have ​said would be “ the ⁠toughest sanctions in history ” on Iran.

Additional input from AFP

World.title: PML-N secures 5 out of 7 reserved seats up for grabs in AJK Legislative Assembly
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: The PML-N bagged five while the PPP won two of the seven reserved seats that were up for grabs in the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Legislative Assembly on Monday.

Under Article 22(1) of the AJK Constitution, the Legislative Assembly consists of 53 members, including 45 members elected directly through adult franchise and eight members chosen by directly elected representatives.

The reserved seats include five seats for women and one each for Ulema-i-Din or Mashaikh well-versed in the teachings of Islam, Jammu and Kashmir State subjects residing abroad, and technocrats and other professionals.

PML-N’s Chaudhry Abdul Rehman Arain was the only candidate to have submitted his nomination papers for the seat reserved for state subjects residing abroad. He was consequently declared elected unopposed.

After polling for the remaining seats on Monday, PML-N’s Sehrish Qamar, Maryam Idrees and Maryam Zaman, also known as Maryam Kashmiri, secured one seat each reserved for women. Seven votes were polled for each of them, as were for PPP’s Farzana Yaqoob, who claimed the fourth reserved seat for women.

There were just two more contenders — PML-N’s Riffat Abid and PPP’s Zobia Khurshid Raja — vying for the seats for women whose votes were tied at five. Eventually, Raja was declared the winner for the last seat left, with the result being decided by drawing lots.

For the seat reserved for Ulema and Mashaikh, PML-N’s Mohammad Mazhar Saeed won against his sole contender, PPP’s Hafiz Tariq Mahmood, after garnering 26 votes — almost double than Mahmood’s 12.

Similarly, PML-N’s Barrister Syed Iftikhar Gillani also bagged 26 votes to claim the seat reserved for technocrats and professionals, beating PPP’s Sahibzada Zulfiqar Ali by 14 votes.

Shortly after their election, the Election Commission notified the successful candidates.

In days preceding Monday’s polls, elections to seven of the 45 directly elected seats — five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district — could not be held due to the law and order situation in the region. As a result, the 38 members elected so far, representing 84.4 per cent of the directly elected membership, participated in the reserved seat elections.

As the inaugural session of the incoming Legislative Assembly has already been summoned for 2pm on Monday, shortly after the announcement of the results, all newly elected members are expected to take an oath at the hands of outgoing Speaker Chaudhry Latif Akbar, who failed to retain his seat in the elections.

AJK polls

The elections in the region, originally scheduled for July 27, were divided into phases over security concerns amid unrest in the region. The first phase was held on July 27, the second on Aug 2 and the third on Aug 10.

The third phase was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation.

So far, in the direct elections to 38 constituencies, the PML-N has secured 25 seats while the PPP won 12. The lone MLA-elect of the Awami Dast-o-Bazu party has also joined hands with the PML-N.

The PPP has alleged widespread rigging in the polls, with the party also ramping up its criticism of the ruling PML-N in recent days.

Last week, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said that a genuine alliance with the PML-N was not possible until their grievances regarding the AJK polls were addressed as he established formal contact with the PTI and offered to cooperate with the party in Parliament.

Speaking to the media, the PPP chairman alleged that the AJK election process had been made controversial for political interests. He alleged that the federal government’s political and administrative machinery had remained active in AJK throughout the six-phase election process, raising serious questions over its transparency.

The PPP, he said, had raised its objections before the Election Commission, parliament and other constitutional forums, but the PML-N had failed to address its concerns or engage in meaningful dialogue after the polls.

Moreover, he said the commitments and political understandings reached with the PML-N before the prime minister’s election had not been honoured. The PPP had cooperated in the wider national interest, he said, but there could be no genuine alliance with the PML-N unless the party’s concerns over the AJK elections were addressed and political commitments fulfilled.

He pointed out that the government needed PPP’s votes for several important laws, constitutional amendments and difficult bills. He said legislation could not be forced through on the basis of a majority or through coercion.

The discord between the PPP and PML-N was also apparent in the National Assembly on Aug 18, when the former managed to compel the government to virtually suspend the heavy legislative agenda for the day, which included 21 bills.

On Aug 20, when the lower house of Parliament passed two bills pertaining to the military and nuclear command structure, the PPP also objected to the manner in which the legislation was presented. While the party ultimately voted in favour of the bills, Bilawal lashed out at the government for not taking ruling allies on board.

World.title: 'Imran would not have spent 3 years in jail if he wanted to make a deal,' says PTI's Gohar
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Monday brushed aside speculation regarding a deal with the government, saying party founder Imran Khan would not have spent three years in jail if he wanted to make a deal.

He made the remarks while speaking outside the Supreme Court (SC) alongside PTI leader Sardar Latif Khosa after the two met with the court’s registrar.

“Khan sahib does not make deals. He will not stay in the hospital a minute more than is necessary for his tests and treatment. If he had to make a deal, he would not have spent three years in jail,” Gohar said.

“All we have to say is that there should be no politics on his health,” he said.

During the press talk, Gohar said that he and Khosa had arrived at the SC to meet with Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi in connection with the party’s contempt petition against the government’s alleged violation of its Aug 18 order for shifting Imran to Shifa International Hospital.

“I asked to meet the chief justice. He was busy so it could not happen. Myself and Khosa sahib met the SC registrar and requested that a number be allotted to this case and it be fixed for hearing,” he said.

He said that the registrar had assured that a case number would be allotted to the contempt plea. Gohar said that they were also assured of the early fixation of the case before the SC.

“This [Aug 18 order] cannot be ignored. The whole world is looking at the SC and whether it is able to implement its order,” he said.

“We only wanted PTI founder’s medical tests to be conducted at a private hospital, with both his sister Uzma and his personal physician Dr Faisal Sultan included in the medical board examining him,” he said.

Meanwhile, Khosa said that a case number was being allotted to the was in Lahore.

Last week, Imran’s sister Uzma Khan had filed contempt petition before the SC against officials for flouting its Aug 18 order. The petition, filed by Advocate Uzair Karamat Bhandari on behalf of Dr Uzma, also requested the apex court to depute an officer or appoint a local commission to ensure that Imran was immediately shifted to the private hospital in accordance with its earlier directions.

Imran’s hospital transfer saga

Last week, the SC had ordered the government to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board.

A three-member bench headed by Justice Shahid Waheed and comprising Justices Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Ishtiaq Ibr­ahim issued the interim contempt petition, and quoted the registrar as saying that one of the judges directions on petitions seeking Imran’s hospitalisation, access to personal physicians and family members and provision of his medical record to his family.

The court had also ordered that Dr Uzma and Dr Sultan — Imran’s personal physician — be present during the medical check-up by a medical board.

At the same time, Imran’s family members, PTI members and lawyers associated with him were barred from disclosing his health condition or medical reports to the media or public until the next hearing.

The next day, the government had filed a review plea against the court’s order to shift Imran to the private hospital, arguing that the directive was discriminatory and issued in violation of prison rules and principles of natural justice.

However, the SC had returned the plea on Thursday with the objection that the contents of the affidavit and facts, along with the review petition filed under Article 188 of the Constitution, had not been properly drawn up and that one of the paper books was not in order.

The same night, elaborate arrangements were put in place in and around Shifa International Hospital, and all signs pointed to the PTI founder being brought there, in compliance with the SC order.

But, it became clear on Friday morning that Imran had been taken to Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) for a check-up and then subsequently transported back to prison. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar blamed “the security situation created by PTI workers on the way to and outside Al Shifa Hospital” for the diversion.

In a post on X, he said, “In the light of the SC’s order, the prisoner was taken to the hospital under appropriate security arrangements during the night between August 20 and 21.

“A team of qualified doctors, including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist, and a physician, conducted a detailed examination of him and declared him medically fit,” he said.

Later, the Pims administration said that two specialists from Shifa Inter­national Hospital participated in Imran’s eye assessment, while other examinations were carried out by the concerned Pims specialists.

Imran has been taken to Pims multiple times after his eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January.

“The clinical input arising from the ophthalmological assessment was taken into account alongside findings of the investigations conducted at Pims,” the statement said.

Meanwhile, the government on Thursday filed a fresh review petition against the SC’s Aug 18 order. The Islamabad chief commissioner again filed the plea, saying that his office had a direct, substantial and legally protected interest in the matter and that the Aug 18 order adversely affected its constitutional authority.

World.title: PM Shehbaz and Sindh CM 'agree to maintain political tolerance, consultation' amid rift in ruling coalition
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah on Monday, and both agreed to “maintain political tolerance and consultation”, the premier’s party, PML-N, posted on X.

The meeting comes amid an emerging rift between the PML-N and Murad’s PPP, allies in the Centre.

State broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported that the meeting took place in Islamabad while the PML-N said matters of mutual interest and political affairs were also discussed on the occasion.

The talks also covered Sindh-related matters and ongoing development projects, the PML-N’s X post stated.

Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Information Technology Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Khan Cheema and Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik also attended the meeting.

The meeting takes place against the backdrop of the PPP expressing its grievances, particularly those related to recent elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir. The PML-N has come out as the winner in the polls that the PPP alleges were marred by rigging and irregularities.

Last week, the PPP also established formal contact with the opposition, with party Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari saying a genuine alliance with the ruling PML-N was not possible until their grievances regarding the AJK elections were addressed.

While the immediate focus during the meeting was parliamentary cooperation — from restoring the opposition’s participation in committees to pursuing electoral reforms — the meeting also carried a broader political undertone.

The signal from the PPP could have been that, while it remains part of the coalition government, it is willing to engage more assertively with the opposition, particularly as tensions over the AJK election results continue to simmer.

The discord between the PPP and PML-N was also apparent in the National Assembly on Aug 18, when the former managed to compel the government to virtually suspend the heavy legislative agenda for the day, which included 21 bills.

On Aug 20, when the lower house of Parliament passed two bills pertaining to the military and nuclear command structure, the PPP also objected to the manner in which the legislation was presented. While the party ultimately voted in favour of the bills, Bilawal lashed out at the government for not taking ruling allies on board.

On Friday, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz fired a fresh salvo at the PPP, accusing it of corruption and warning political rivals against targeting her government’s performance.

World.title: Info ministry says video of Asif comparing Pakistan's progress with India's is fake
World.content:
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on Monday said that a video of Defence Minister Khawaja Asif comparing Pakistan’s progress with India’s was “fake”, adding that the PML-N leader had not made any such statement.

The ministry shared the purported clip of the minister on its X account. The nearly minute-long video appeared to show a clip from a press conference by the minister on a major news channel.

In the purported video, the minister called on citizens to review the country’s situation. He went on to say that Pakistan and India had gained independence at the same time, yet the difference in progress between the two was evident.

The purported clip showed Asif saying that Balochistan had “slipped from our hands”, the people in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa were facing difficulties and residents of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) had taken to the streets for their rights.

On the other hand, look at India, Asif said in the alleged video, pointing to the country’s progress in technology, infrastructure and the economy.

“We have to ask ourselves whether we are a true democracy. Instead of blaming others, we should question our government and policies,” Asif said in the purported clip.

The clip, which was circulating on social media, was also picked up by Indian media, with News18 publishing an article on the alleged statement by Asif.

Sharing the clip on X, the information ministry said on Monday: “This news is FAKE and the voice in the video is AI-generated.

“Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has not given any such statement. Please verify news from official sources before sharing,” it said.

The same statement was also shared by the information ministry’s fact-checking account on X.

World.title: American varsities urge international students to return to US before new immigration rules come into effect
World.content:
WASHINGTON: Several major US universities have urged international students to return to the United States before September 15, when new federal immigration rules are scheduled to take effect.

Under the new rules, international students can remain in the US as long as they maintain their academic status, with a fixed period of admission for holders of F (academic students), J (exchange visitors) and I (foreign media and journalists) category visas.

Universities, including Harvard, Columbia, Ohio State University, Georgetown, George Washington (GW) and the University of Chicago, warned international students that the changes could affect the terms under which F-1 and J-1 students were admitted and allowed to remain in the country.

Those planning international travel around the September 15 deadline were also advised to reconsider their plans. Universities said returning before that date could help students avoid being admitted under the new fixed-period system.

Harvard’s International Office specifically advised F-1 and J-1 students and scholars to plan their travel so that they were physically present in the US by September 15.

Columbia University set an even earlier target, asking international students to return by September 8 to allow sufficient time for the transition.

Georgetown’s Office of Global Services (OGS) issued targeted warning letters to students, scholars and alumni.

George Washington University’s International Services Office (ISO) advised students to check their records through the university’s portal on or shortly after September 15 to track their new, explicit programme-end dates.

The University of Chicago’s Office of International Affairs held urgent informational webinars to explain the rule’s strict limitations on academic mobility and the shortened 30-day grace period.

The new rule

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) rule, scheduled to take effect on September 15, replaced the long-standing “duration of status,” or D/S system with fixed periods of admission for many international students and exchange visitors.

Under the existing system, eligible F-1 students are generally admitted for the “duration of status,” allowing them to remain in the US while they pursue their approved programme and maintain their immigration status.

Under the new system, students entering or re-entering the US will generally receive an “Admit Until Date” on their Form I-94 — an official entry document issued by the US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) when a foreign national enters the US — and their authorised stay will normally be tied to the length of their programme, subject to a maximum initial admission period of four years.

The change could have significant consequences for students enrolled in programmes that routinely take longer than four years, including some doctoral, medical and other professional programmes. Students who need additional time may have to apply for an extension of stay through US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS).

For students already in the US, the transition rules are less disruptive.

Students who are physically present in the country on September 15 and are maintaining their F-1 or J-1 status will generally be covered by transition provisions and will not immediately have to obtain a new admission period simply because the rule takes effect.

The situation changes, however, for students who leave the US and return after September 15. They could be admitted under the new fixed-date system and receive a specific end date for their authorised stay.

Therefore, universities are urging students to complete international travel before the deadline.

The Ohio State University warned students that the new system could affect the length of their authorised stay and their ability to complete their academic programmes without seeking an extension. It advised students to review their individual circumstances and consult the university’s international office before travelling.

San José State University also highlighted the potential disruption for international students.

Another important change concerns the grace period after completion of an F-1 programme. Under the new rules, students will generally have 30 days, rather than the current 60 days, to remain in the US after completing their programme.

The rules may also affect students who change educational programmes or institutions, transfer schools or require additional time to complete their studies. Students planning to use post-completion Optional Practical Training (OPT) or STEM OPT should therefore pay particular attention to the new requirements and seek advice from their university before making travel or academic decisions.

The new policy has been challenged in the federal court. A coalition of higher-education organisations and labour groups filed a lawsuit seeking to block the rule and asked the court for a preliminary injunction.

But unless a court blocks or delays implementation, universities are advising students to plan on the assumption that the September 15 deadline will remain in force.

If international students are outside the US and intend to return for the fall semester, universities are urging them to return before September 15. They should check their passport, visa, Form I-20 or DS-2019 and I-94 before travelling and contact their university’s international student office if they expect to need additional time to complete their programme.

World.title: Comstech chief remains defiant in face of ‘damning inquiry’
World.content:
• President-ordered probe found OIC official guilty of ‘misconduct, non-compliance’

• Accused official calls inquiry ‘one-sided’, claims Presidency was ‘misused’

ISLAMABAD: An inquiry committee formed on the directives of President Asif Ali Zardari has declared the top official of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation’s (OIC) Standing Committee on Scientific and Technological Cooperation (Comstech) guilty of multiple charges of misconduct.

According to the inquiry report seen by Dawn, Comstech Coordinator General Dr Iqbal Choudhry was accused of financial irregularities, violation of executive orders and non-compliance with court directives.

However, the official in question has questioned the legality of proceedings against him, calling it a “one-sided inquiry”.

According to the inquiry report, Dr Choudhry was initially appointed by then-president Arif Alvi in 2020 during the PTI’s tenure, and was subsequently reappointed by President Zardari for another four-year term in October 2024.

Under Articles 12(2), read with 16(3) of the Comstech statute, the President of Pakistan is the appointing authority for the post of the body’s coordinator general.

Comstech was created in January 1981 at the Third Islamic Summit in Makkah, Saudi Arabia. Headquartered in Islamabad, Pakistan, it aims to promote science, technology and research cooperation among OIC member states.

The inquiry committee was headed by Dr Asim Hussain, the chancellor of Ziauddin University.

Its members included Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (PCSIR) Chairman Dr Syed Hussain Abidi, Ministry of Science and Technology Secretary Shahid Iqbal Baloch and its Chief Finance and Accounts Officer Muhammad Saeedullah Yousafzai.

Inquiry findings

The committee held that Dr Choudhry had failed to implement instructions issued by the president, terming the alleged failure “misconduct”. It also accused him of violating court orders, and failing to reply to complaints.

The inquiry found that meetings of the Comstech Executive Committee had not been convened for the last four years, and that most decisions were taken by Dr Choudhry alone, terming this “maladministration”.

It further maintained that expenditures had been incurred for several years without budgetary approval, which the committee declared “unauthorised and illegal”.

The report recommended strict disciplinary action over the alleged misuse of Comstech funds, including expenditure allegedly made for personal benefit.

The committee alleged that Dr Choudhry undertook more than 70 foreign trips over the last six years without prior approval from the president in his capacity as Comstech chairman. Some of the visits, it said, were to countries not associated with Comstech, while funds were also allegedly used to cover the travel and accommodation expenses of female associates.

The report also pointed out that Dr Choudhry simultaneously held the posts of Comstech coordinator general and director of the International Centre for Chemical and Biological Sciences (ICCBS) from April 8, 2020, to Nov 12, 2024, a period of around four and a half years, despite directives from the ministry to relinquish the additional charge.

The inquiry also cited complaints regarding forced resignations and dismissals of employees, a lack of transparent procedures in disciplinary proceedings, and allegations of nepotism and favouritism in recruitment.

It noted that the World Academy of Sciences, Trieste, Italy, had also issued a reprimand letter to Dr Choudhry.

The inquiry committee has recommended that the matter be referred to anti-corruption institutions for further investigation and appropriate action against Dr Choudhry on multiple counts of alleged misconduct.

The recommendations in the inquiry report have been submitted to the competent authority for further proceedings.

Official’s response

When approached for comment, Dr Choudhry told Dawn he was unaware of any such report, but raised questions over the legality of the inquiry, noting that procedural requirements had not been fulfilled.

He claimed that neither any complaint nor a show cause notice was shared with him, and said that there were “serious procedural flaws in this one-sided inquiry”.

“You cannot do it on the basis of a fake complaint,” he remarked.

He maintained that the president, in his capacity as Comstech chairman, draws his powers from OIC procedures, and could not as as head of the state take a unilateral action against an OIC body which enjoys diplomatic immunity.

Alleging that the Presidency was being misused, he said any inquiry or report prepared without proof or documentation has no legal or ethical standing, and is liable to be challenged in court.

Published in Dawn, August 24th, 2026

World.title: Amnesty International says police in India used excessive force during youth-led protests
World.content:
Indian police used excessive force, including electric shock devices and pellet guns, against youth-led protests that forced the education minister to resign last month, Amnesty International said on Monday.

A report from the rights group clashes with the police account that force was used only after protesters turned violent, and comes after India’s Supreme Court set up a panel on Thursday to investigate violence by both police and demonstrators.

Demonstrations in the capital New Delhi, triggered by the leak of the national medical entrance test, turned violent on July 20 when thousands of protesters attempted to march towards parliament.

Amnesty said witness testimony and visual evidence it had verified confirmed the use of “pellet-firing shotguns, tear gas launchers, grenades, batons and electric shock devices against protesters” in Delhi and the eastern state of Bihar.

Amnesty said it had also verified two instances of a police officer “unlawfully using lethal force against a crowd” in Bihar’s Siwan district. No one was killed.

“The weapons were deployed in a manner that breached international law and standards and domestic policing guidelines,” it added.

Amnesty said that there were “isolated incidents of protesters throwing stones”, but that the “heavy-handed response was state-sanctioned violence masked as crowd control”.

Delhi Police said in a Supreme Court hearing last week they had used force only after protesters “resorted to violence”.

They said anti-social elements “masquerading as aggrieved students” caused “grievous injuries” to security forces.

On Friday, opposition leader Rahul Gandhi staged a sit-in outside a Delhi police station with a 19-year-old protester who said he was injured by pellets during the July 20 demonstration.

Gandhi demanded a police investigation into the shooting, and officers later registered a case over the complaint.

Led by the online Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the protests broadened from anger over exam irregularities into a wider movement over unemployment, opportunities for young people and what critics describe as Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s increasingly authoritarian rule.

The protests proved to be the biggest challenge that Modi has faced after winning a third term in 2024.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts.
